docs.title: UnleashSkill
docs.text:
UnleashSkill is a Unity tool to create game abilities (spells, attacks, passives, summons) without writing code, by assembling nodes in a graph. It targets RPGs, action games and turn-based games.

[Start] ──► [Spell body] ◄── [Movement]          a fireball that moves forward
                 │
                 ▼
            [On hit] ──► [Simple damage]         hits an enemy, deals damage
                     └─► [Apply status]          and burns it for 2 seconds

docs.title: What the tool does for you
docs.text:
• A graph editor: each node is a behavior (projectile, area, damage, status, condition, delay…). A skill reads from left to right.
  • A simulation world: skills move and hit their targets in a fixed-step world, independent of Unity physics and of the frame rate. The same skill gives the same result at 30 or 144 frames per second.
  • Configuration without code: stats, teams, entity types, damage types, statuses, events… are declared in the main menu, then picked from lists.
  • Presentation kept apart from gameplay: effects, sounds, animations and camera shakes are reusable assets. They can be disabled (server, tests) without changing the skill's behavior.
  • A preview in the editor: the skill plays next to the graph, on dummies, without entering Play Mode.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
I want to… Read Install the tool and create my first skill Getting started Understand how a skill runs Concepts Declare my stats, teams, statuses Configuration Set the cooldown, the cost, the slots Skills Know what a node and its fields do Node reference Get inspired by a complete skill Recipes Develop the tool itself (engine, nodes, tests) Technical

Language

The editor is in English by default. French is available in Edit → Preferences → UnleashSkill → Language; this documentation is also available in French (language selector at the top of the page).

Online and offline

This documentation describes UnleashSkill 1.x. Its latest version is online at pim103.github.io/UnleashSkill-docs; the package contains an offline copy (PDF, in English and in French) in Assets/UnleashSkill/Documentation/, with the changelog.

docs.title: The nodes' dropdowns are empty
docs.text: No configuration is loaded. Main Menu → Load configuration.

docs.title: At runtime, nodes do not find the stats (“No active configuration”, “Target stat not found”)
docs.text: The scene's UnleashSkillManager has no Default Configuration. Assign it in its inspector.

docs.title: The skill does not fire
docs.text: Read the result of Cast / CastSlot (SkillCastResult): on cooldown, insufficient cost, locked actions (stunned), empty slot, passive slot, slot locked by a replacement.

docs.title: The skill fires but hits nothing
docs.text:
• Is the target of another team (Enemy filter)? Two entities without a team are allies.
  • Is the target targetable (Is Targetable) and not Untargetable or Intangible (status)?
  • Does the Entity type filter keep this type (type hierarchy)?
  • Do the Scenery layers (Simulation) contain the layer of the entities' colliders? The skill then stops on their collider as on a wall.
  • Does the layer matrix allow the contact?

Enable simulation debugging (gizmos) to see the bodies and hurtboxes in the Scene view.

docs.title: The projectile is invisible
docs.text: The module has no Visual, or the presentation is disabled. The skill works anyway.

docs.title: No effect or sound in the build
docs.text: Fill in the Presentation Library of the UnleashSkillManager: without it, only the editor's default library is found.

docs.title: Error on every playback of an animation
docs.text: The clip carries UnleashPhase events but the character has no AnimationPhaseEventReceiver component. Add it.

docs.title: My character's root motion is added to an attack's movement
docs.text: An OnAnimatorMove of your game on an entity's Animator is not cut by the tool during an attack that moves the character. Test IsRootMotionCut(animator) of the PlayablesEntityAnimator in your script and ignore the root motion when it is true.

docs.title: The game slows down when there are many skills
docs.text: Beyond Max ticks per frame, the extra ticks are dropped and the game visibly slows down. Enable Burst (Simulation), increase the Cell size if the targets are large, or lower the Ticks per second.

docs.title: The editor is in French (or in English)
docs.text: The language is set per user in Edit → Preferences → UnleashSkill → Language. Unity menus stay in English.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
These pages explain how the tool thinks about a skill. They avoid surprises: why a node only hits the target of its branch, why a projectile does not read Unity physics, why a visual effect can be disabled without changing the fight.

Page Question Graph, nodes and ports How does a graph read, which nodes connect where? Running a skill What happens between the cast and the end of a skill? Targets and branches Whom does a node affect? Aim, anchors and directions Where does the skill aim, where does it start, toward where, and how does it choose its targets? Simulation world How do skills move, hit and count time? Dynamic values How can an amount depend on a stat, a distance, a charge? Presentation Where do effects, sounds and animations live?

docs.title: Targets and branches
docs.text: When a node fires its outputs, each following node receives a branch: a copy of its parent's targets, aim point and direction. This is the rule that decides whom an action affects.

docs.title: An action affects the targets of its branch
docs.text:
[Spell body] ─► [On hit] ─► [Damage]

On each contact, On hit creates a dedicated branch that contains the target hit. The Damage applies to it, and to it only. If the projectile goes through three enemies, there are three branches and three damage applications.

docs.title: Sibling branches: each its own
docs.text:
[Start] ─► [Fork ×3] ─► [Spell body] ─► [On hit] ─► [Damage]

Fork creates three branches, one per projectile, each with its direction. The second projectile does not see the first one's targets. A child branch inherits its parent's data; a sibling branch never sees the other's data.

docs.title: Choose new targets
docs.text:
To affect something other than the current target, add a Target selection: it looks for entities (in a shape around the caster, the aim point or the target; the caster's summons; spells) and filters them (team, type, status, stat, position), then sorts them and keeps a number of them. Its Targets output carries the entities found, its No target output fires when nothing is found.

Examples:

  • “heal the most wounded ally”: Selection (allies around the caster, sort by lowest HP, 1 target) → Heal;
  • “lightning bounces on 3 enemies”: Chain, which chooses the next target on each bounce.

A Selection can also be connected as a setting of another node (Area, Chain, Fork, Summon) through its Selection output: it is then not executed, it tells that node how to choose its targets. See Aim, anchors and directions.

docs.title: See what a node receives
docs.text:
The editor deduces from the graph what each connection carries and shows it with the same vocabulary:

Term What it is Received targets the targets of the node's branch: those an action acts on Event target the single target of a branch fired by a listener or a trigger (the entity hit, the event's subject) Aim point frozen at cast time, replaced by an Aim node Branch direction written by Fork (fan, circle), followed by modules and movement Module body the module upstream (projectile, area…): what On hit, On tick, On expire listen to
  • Connection label: on link hover, a short text in the middle (“targets hit by “Projectile””, “no target (caster only)”, “one target per branch (“Fork”) · branch direction”); the Labels button of the toolbar always shows them.
  • Port tooltip: on port hover, everything it receives or emits (received targets, aim point, branch direction, module body), and what the node reads.
  • “!” badge on the title of a node that reads what it will never receive: Damage connected directly to the Start (no received target: an On hit, an area or a Target selection is needed), an On hit without a module upstream, a Selection connected both as a setting and in the flow. A skill cast by Cast skill receives the targets of the one that casts it: the warning of Damage on the Start can then be ignored.

docs.title: Branch data
docs.text:
A branch also carries:

  • a direction (written by Fork as a fan or a circle, read by modules and the Movement);
  • a damage multiplier (multiplied by Fork, Chain or Multiply damage, applied by the damage nodes);
  • marks (for example Critical, applied by Mark branch), read by damage and listeners;
  • the aim (aim point, direction, pointed entity; see Aim, anchors and directions), and the value of the event that created the branch.

docs.title: The caster
docs.text: Some nodes target the caster rather than the received targets: their holder or target field offers Caster (Apply status on self, Dash, Heal self). The caster is shared by the whole execution.

docs.title: Dynamic values
docs.text: Many numeric fields (damage, heal, chance, durations, stacks, reaction strengths…) are not plain numbers: they are dynamic values (ValueSource). By default they look like an ordinary field; a menu changes their mode.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
Mode The value comes from… Example Fixed a number 20 damage Stat a stat of the caster or of the target: current value, maximum or % of the maximum 50% of the caster's Attack Status stacks the number of stacks of a status on the target or the caster 10 damage per Bleed stack Execution value a value of the cast: elapsed cast time, charge ratio, last damage dealt, number of received targets, blocks of the module body (bounces), or a skill variable damage × charge ratio Event value the value carried by the event that fired the branch heal 30% of the damage taken Distance a distance in the simulation plane: caster → target, caster → impact point, or center of the area (impact point) → target (see Distances) more damage up close, explosion that falls off Formula an expression that combines the sources above 0.5 * LastDamage + Stat(Strength)

Each mode accepts a multiplier, an addition and optional bounds: value × multiplier + addition, clamped between the minimum and the maximum.

docs.title: Formulas
docs.text:
Element Syntax Operators numbers (decimal point), + - * / % ^, parentheses Functions min(a, b, …), max(a, b, …), clamp(x, min, max) Stat Stat(name[, Caster\|Target][, Current\|Max\|Percent]) — caster and current value by default Stacks Stacks(status[, Target\|Caster]) — target by default Skill variable Var(name), or just the name Execution values Targets, LastDamage, StacksRemoved, RemainingDamage, CastTime, Charge, Kills, Blocks, EventValue, Distance, ImpactDistance, CenterDistance (see Distances) Random Random() — roll from 0 to 100 (excluded), with the execution's random generator (reproducible) Comparators < > <= >= = != (== accepted) — 1 if true, 0 otherwise; = tolerates a gap of 0.0001 Logic not, and, or — a non-zero value is true

The formula is checked in the editor: an unknown stat, status or variable name is reported, as is a syntax error (with its position).

Precedence, from strongest to weakest: ^, sign -, * / %, + -, comparators, not, and, or. So Stat(HP, Target, Percent) < 30 and Distance <= 5 reads without parentheses, and 2 + 3 > 4 is 1. Two comparisons do not chain: 1 < x < 3 is an error, write 1 < x and x < 3. and, or and not are reserved: a variable with one of these names is read with Var(…).

A comparison returns 1 or 0: it serves as a condition (Formula mode of Check condition) or as a factor in a calculation, e.g. 20 + 10 * (Targets >= 3).

Formulas written before 1.0

The French vocabulary of earlier versions is still read: et, ou, non, Lanceur, Cible, Courante, Pourcent, Hasard(), Cibles, DerniersDegats, StacksRetires, DegatsRestants, TempsIncantation, Tues, ValeurEvenement, DistanceImpact. Existing skills keep working without changes.

docs.title: Distances
docs.text:
A distance is measured in the simulation plane (the height difference does not count), between two points:

Distance (field) Formula From… To… Without that point Caster To Target Distance the caster the target 0 without a target Caster To Impact Point ImpactDistance the caster the branch's impact point (where a module body hit, from On hit) to the target Impact Point To Target CenterDistance the center of the branch's Area, at its latest detection; outside an area, the branch's impact point the target from the caster

ImpactDistance grows with the distance the projectile traveled: it does not say where the target stands in the explosion. For damage that falls off from the center of an area, use CenterDistance. In the branches of an area (its Targets in the area output and its listeners, On hit), the distance starts from the center of the area, even when the impact point of a detection is on the target.

Example — explosion that falls off: Spell body → On hit → Area (Anchor: Impact point, Radius 3, Duration 0) → Simple damage, damage in Formula mode: max(20 - CenterDistance * 5, 0). An enemy 0.5 m from the center takes 17.5 damage, an enemy 2.5 m away takes 7.5, wherever the caster stands.

docs.title: Evaluated for each target
docs.text: When the source depends on the target (a target stat, its stacks, its distance), the value is computed target by target: the same area deals different damage to each one.

docs.title: Skill variables
docs.text:
Variables are declared in the skill settings: a name and an initial value, reset on each cast. The Store value node writes them from any source; the Execution value mode reads them back. They are shared by the whole execution.

Example — “each enemy hit increases the damage of the final explosion”: On hit → Store value (Counter + 1); then On expire → Damage (Execution value: Counter × 15).

docs.title: Running a skill
docs.text: Each cast creates an execution (SkillExecution): an isolated instance of the skill. Two casts of the same fireball are two independent executions, with their own targets and their own data.

docs.title: From cast to end
docs.text:
1. Check: the caster's actions are not locked, the cooldown has elapsed, the cost is available. Otherwise, the cast is refused and nothing starts.
  2. Cast: the cost is taken, the cooldown starts.
  3. Cast time (if the skill has one): the Start's During cast branch starts. A hit taken or a stun can interrupt it depending on the skill's setting; the cost is then refunded and the cooldown reset.
  4. Release: the Start's main output fires.
  5. Flow: each node does its job, then fires the nodes that follow it.
  6. End: the execution ends when no node is active anymore. Listeners (On event, On tick) and flying modules keep it alive.

docs.title: Instant and persistent nodes
docs.text:
• An instant node (Damage, Apply status, Play sound…) acts and hands over to its outputs right away.
  • A persistent node lasts: a projectile flies, a Delay waits, a Repeat starts again, a listener waits for its event. It fires its outputs when the time comes (on impact, at the end of the delay, on each event).
  • A node that fails (false condition, missed chance, no target) ends without firing its outputs: the rest of this branch does not happen.

docs.title: Shared data
docs.text:
• The skill variables (declared in the settings) are shared by the whole execution. Store value writes them, dynamic values read them.
  • The targets, the aim point and the direction belong to each branch (see Targets and branches).

docs.title: Cancellation
docs.text:
An execution stops before its end when:

  • the caster dies or is disabled (unless the skill is set to outlive it: a projectile already fired, a burn already applied);
  • the game interrupts it (CancelSkill, CancelSlot);
  • a held skill is released, or an aim is canceled.

The effects already applied remain (damage, applied statuses); flying modules and listeners disappear.

docs.title: Graph, nodes and ports
docs.text: A skill is a SkillGraphModel asset: a list of nodes and connections, plus the skill settings (cooldown, cost, cast time…).

docs.title: The Start node
docs.text:
Every skill has a Start node, called when it is cast. Its outputs:

  • Module: toward the first module (projectile, area, attack…);
  • Trigger: toward immediate actions (heal the caster, status on self…);
  • During cast (skill with a cast time): a branch that starts at the beginning of the cast and stops at its end (charge visual, caster slowdown).

docs.title: Node families
docs.text:
Family Role Examples Module An object of the skill that exists in the world, with a body that moves and hits Spell body (projectile), Area, Beam, Attack (melee), Summon Behavior Modifies a module: how it moves, how it grows Movement, Scale over time Condition Listens to a module or filters the targets On hit, On expire, On tick, Entity type, Chance, Stat condition Support Shapes the flow: wait, repeat, split, choose targets Delay, Repeat, Fork, Chain, Target selection, Aim, Check condition, Random choice Action Does something to the targets or to the game Damage, Heal, Apply status, Reactions, Dash, Kill, Cast skill, Replace slot Trigger Listens to the game while the skill lasts On event, Timer, Stat listener Presentation Effects, sounds, animations, shakes — no effect on the fight Play effect, Play sound, Play animation, Camera shake

The complete list, with each node's fields, is in the node reference.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
Each connection links an output to an input of the same type. The port color tells its type:

Type Color What goes through Example Module Blue The main flow between modules Start → Spell body Trigger Green The firing of an action, with its targets On hit → Damage Condition Orange Listening to a module, or a filter Spell body → On hit Support Purple A behavior modifier Movement → Spell body Selection Cyan A setting, not flow: how a node chooses its targets Target selection → Area (see Aim, anchors and directions)

A few nodes have several outputs of the same type, named:

  • Check condition: True / False;
  • Target selection: Targets / No target, and Selection (setting of another node);
  • Random choice: Output 1, Output 2…;
  • Area, Attack, Beam: Targets in the area or Hit targets (actions on the targets) / Listeners (nodes that listen to the module, such as On tick);
  • Summon: Summon / Listeners;
  • Start: cast / During cast.

docs.title: Reading a graph
docs.text:
A graph reads from the Start, following the arrows. An output can go to several nodes: they all run, each one with its own copy of the targets (see Targets and branches).

[Start] ─► [Spell body] ─► [On hit] ─┬─► [Damage]
                ▲                    └─► [Apply status]
            [Movement]

docs.title: In the editor
docs.text:
• Space or right-click → Create Node: add a node (search by name).
  • Drag from one port to another: connect; only compatible ports snap together.
  • The main fields are shown on the node; the secondary settings are folded in Options. Some fields only appear when another one makes them useful (the maximum range only appears in the Movement's “range” mode).
  • Hovering a link or a port shows what flows through it; Labels shows it on every link, and a “!” badge flags a node that reads what it will never receive (see Targets and branches).
  • Save saves the asset. Skill settings shows the skill's settings in the inspector. Preview opens the skill playback.

docs.title: Presentation
docs.text:
The presentation is what you see and hear: particle effects, sounds, character animations, camera shakes, projectile visuals. In UnleashSkill, it is kept apart from gameplay:

  • nodes emit intentions (“play this effect here”);
  • reusable assets describe the content (which prefab, which sound, which volume);
  • a presentation system spawns them, pools them and stops them.

Consequences: the same impact effect serves a hundred skills; tuning a sound touches no skill; the presentation can be disabled (server, tests) without changing the fight.

docs.title: The library
docs.text:
All definitions are stored in a global presentation library (PresentationLibrary), edited in Main Menu → Presentation. Each definition has a stable identifier; nodes pick it from a list.

Definition Contents Effect Particle prefab, mode (one-shot, persistent, attached), duration, scale, pool size Sound One or more clips (picked at random), volume, pitch variation, spatialization, mixer group Camera Shake Amplitude, frequency, duration, range Animation Clip played on the character, with its phases (startup, active hit, recovery) extracted from the clip Module Visual Visual of a module: body prefab, launch, loop, impact and expiration effects and sounds

They can also be created with Create → UnleashSkill → Presentation. The Presentation menu has a Preview column that plays the selected definition.

docs.title: Presentation nodes
docs.text:
• Play effect: a definition and an anchor (impact point, target, caster, module body), attached or not, bone, scale. A persistent effect can receive a key to be stopped later.
  • Stop effect: stops the effects played with a key in the same execution.
  • Play sound, Camera shake, Play animation.

They are instant and have no effect on the fight. The secondary settings (anchor, bone, scale) are folded: by default, choosing the definition is enough.

docs.title: Module visuals
docs.text:
A module (projectile, area…) chooses a Visual (Module Visual). The visual's prefab follows the simulated body, interpolated between two ticks; the launch, loop, impact and expiration effects play by themselves. A module without a visual stays valid: its body is invisible. In turn-based mode, an area or a beam stays visible for the visual's Turn Display Duration after its last activation.

Module visuals are pooled per prefab. In real-time mode, the SkillPooler takes the body prefab's instance from its prefab's pool: at the end of the module, the visual is disabled and returned there, then reused by the next module with the same prefab, reset (position, rotation and scale under the module body, trails cleared, particles restarted, colliders disabled). The pool only grows: it holds as many instances as the peak of simultaneous modules. A script placed on the visual that keeps state resets it in OnEnable. Two exceptions:

  • the entity of a Summon is not pooled: it keeps its colliders and its state, so it is created for each summon and destroyed at its end;
  • in turn-based mode, a visual replayed by the presentation (projectile resolved on the selection, area or beam in turns) comes from the presentation system's own pool, per prefab too.

So the visual of a module is carried by the SkillPooler in real-time mode, and by the presentation system only for these replays in turn-based mode: to count the visuals displayed, read the pooler's counters, or the presentation's in turns (see Diagnose and measure).

With the presentation disabled, no module visual is created (see below).

docs.title: Animations
docs.text:
The tool plays the clips itself on the character's Animator (Playables): no state to create in the Animator Controller. The phases of an attack (start of the hit, end of the hit) and the weapon's trajectory are extracted from the clip in the editor: gameplay reads this data, it never depends on the animation at runtime.

Animation events

A clip that carries UnleashPhase events must be played on a character that has an AnimationPhaseEventReceiver component, otherwise Unity shows an error on every playback. The phase curve does not need it.

docs.title: Disable the presentation
docs.text: Disabled, the presentation ignores every command: no effect, no sound, no module visual. The fight is identical. It is the setting of a server or of automated tests. See Simulation and general settings.

docs.title: Simulation world
docs.text: Skills do not move with Unity physics. They live in a simulation world (SkillWorld) that advances in fixed steps (ticks, 60 per second by default). Result: a skill behaves the same whatever the frame rate, and can run without display (tests, server).

docs.title: What is in the world
docs.text: Element What it is Entities Casters and targets (SkillCaster), through their hurtboxes. Their position is read at the start of each tick. Module bodies The body of a module: sphere, capsule or box. A projectile sweeps its path from one tick to the next: it does not go through a thin target, even a very fast one. Scenery Walls and ground: the colliders of the Unity layers chosen in Simulation (Scenery layers, none by default). Dynamic obstacles Walls that move or appear (a wall skill, a summoned rock).

docs.title: Hitting
docs.text:
A module hits according to its hit rules (Hit Policy):

  • number of targets before stopping (1 for a classic projectile, 0 to go through everything);
  • re-hit of the same target (never, or after a delay: an area that strikes every second);
  • stop on obstacles, line of sight.

The layers (entities, skills, obstacles…) and their collision matrix are set in Simulation.

docs.title: Time
docs.text:
• Skill durations (delays, statuses, lifetimes) are counted in simulation time, not in real time.
  • Time can be slowed down or frozen globally or per entity: hitstop (brief freeze on impact), slowing a target, time zones. A burn follows its target's time; a delay follows the caster's.
  • The visual is interpolated between two ticks: it stays smooth at any frame rate.

docs.title: Visual and logic are separate
docs.text: The prefab you see (a module's visual) follows the simulated body; it never drives it. Moving the visual by hand does not move the skill, and disabling the presentation does not change the fight.

docs.title: 2D and 3D
docs.text: The world works in a configurable plane: XZ for 3D (top-down or general view), XY for 2D (Unity's 2D convention). The static scenery is read by 3D physics, 2D physics, or not at all. The nodes' shapes stay the same; the plane determines the possible directions.

docs.title: Aim, anchors and directions
docs.text:
All the targeting of a skill answers four questions. Each one has a single tool, the same on every node: when a node asks for a position, a direction or targets, it is always one of these four answers.

Question Tool Decided Where is the player aiming? The Aim: a point, a direction, the pointed entity once, at cast time Where does this node start, and toward where? An Anchor and a Direction node setting Who is affected? The received targets, or a connected Target selection during the skill How does the body move? The Movement, or a Trajectory from the library module setting

docs.title: The Aim
docs.text:
When the player casts the skill, the tool records where they aim: the aim point (in the play plane), the direction from the caster toward this point, and the pointed entity if there is one. This aim is frozen: if the player moves the mouse while the fireball flies, the fireball does not change its mind.

Caster Aim point frozen Branch A: same aim Branch B: same aim After “Aim”: new point The aim is copied into each branch. Only the Aim node replaces it, for the nodes that follow it.
  • The Aim node shows an indicator, waits for the player to confirm, brings the point back within the skill's range, then replaces the aim of its branch. This is how you make a “click to place an area” skill.
  • Why freeze it? For the same aim, the skill always behaves the same way: the editor preview, turn-based mode and a server replay exactly the same cast. An AI or your code can give the aim themselves (see Cast a skill from code).

Exception

A channeled beam that follows the mouse reads the aim continuously. The node says so in its documentation; no other node does it.

docs.title: Anchor and Direction
docs.text:
Each node that places something (a projectile, an area, an effect, the center of a fan) has an Anchor field. Each node that orients something has a Direction field. They are the same lists everywhere; a node only offers the values that make sense for it.

Caster Module body Impact point Received target Aim point Top view. An anchor also accepts an offset (forward, side, height, in the aim frame) and a maximum range. Anchor The position of… Caster the one who casts the skill Aim point the aim Received target the first target received by the node Each received target once per target (effects, fan “on the targets”) Module body the projectile or the area that carries this node Impact point the exact place of the contact Named object a named object of the caster Direction Goes… Toward the aim point from the anchor toward the aim (default of new nodes) Caster forward where the caster is looking Toward the received target from the anchor toward the first target Away from the caster moving away from them (explosion, repulsion) Random at random, reproducible

Follow the branch direction (checked by default): behind a Fork in a fan, each branch receives its own direction, which takes precedence over the field's. This is what sends three projectiles in a fan with a single Spell body.

docs.title: Who is affected
docs.text:
A skill reads as a tree of branches. Each connection passes a list of received targets to the next node, and a node only works on the targets of its branch (details in Targets and branches).

[Start] ─► [Spell body + Movement] ─► [On hit] ──(the target hit)──► [Simple damage]

The projectile targets nobody: it moves forward. On hit activates on each entity met and opens a branch that only contains this entity. The Damage therefore strikes the target hit, once per contact.

To choose other targets, use Target selection: a source (around the caster, around the aim point, my summons…) and criteria (team relation, entity type, status, stat, position, sort, count). The node is used in two ways.

In the flowAs a setting of another node 
[Target selection] ──Targets──► [Heal]
 3 most wounded allies

The node runs, searches, and passes the targets found through its Targets output (or No target if nothing is found).

[Target selection] ┄┄Selection┄┄► [Area]
 enemies, lowest HP, 3

Its Selection output (cyan port) connects to another node's Selection input. The node is not executed: it tells the other node how to choose. The same Selection can set several nodes. Choose the Provided by the consumer source so that it works on the candidates of the node it sets.

Node set What the Selection changes Area among the entities in the area, keeps those that pass the criteria, sorted from the center (“the 3 most wounded in the area”) Chain on each bounce, chooses the next target around the previous one with these criteria and this sort Fork the chosen targets replace the received targets, for every pattern Summon the summon's target, once its attack behavior exists

Without a connected Selection, each node keeps its usual behavior.

Warning

A Selection connected as a setting ignores its own flow inputs. Do not connect it in the flow as well.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Fireball: the Spell body appears on the Caster (anchor); its Movement pushes it Toward the aim point (direction); On hit passes the target hit to the Damage.

[Start] ─► [Spell body] ─► [On hit] ─► [Simple damage]
               ▲ Movement: Toward the aim point

Fan of three arrows: Fork (fan, 3, 30°) creates three branches, each with its direction; the same Spell body, whose Movement follows the branch direction, flies in all three.

[Start] ─► [Fork ×3] ─► [Spell body] ─► [On hit] ─► [Simple damage]

Meteor shower placed on click: Aim waits for confirmation, brings the point back within range and replaces the aim; the Area appears on the Aim point and the Damage hits the entities inside.

[Start] ─► [Aim] ─► [Area] ──(entities in the area)──► [Simple damage]
                     anchor: Aim point

Chain lightning that targets the weakest: without a Selection, Chain bounces on the closest; with a Selection as a setting (enemies, lowest HP), each bounce chooses the most wounded enemy in range.

[Spell body] ─► [On hit] ─► [Chain] ─► [Simple damage]
                                ▲
      [Target selection] ┄┄┄┄┄┄┘ (Selection)

docs.title: Trajectories
docs.text: The Movement node moves a module forward (line, boomerang, wander, pursuit). To go further, the Trajectory node reads a definition from the library (main menu → Trajectories): a sequence of segments (line, curve toward a point, orbit, pursuit, return), computed in the aim frame (forward = movement direction, side = right). Each segment chooses what happens against a wall (stop, slide, bounce, next segment), up to a maximum number of blocks, whether it hits what it meets in flight or ignores obstacles, and can oscillate (sine wave on the side or in height). A curve can rise to an apex: in 3D, the height is simulated (a lobbed shot passes over an entity and hits an obstacle in the air); in 2D, only the visual rises. The Trajectories tab shows the path, with a time slider and adjustable direction and aim point. The Convert to definition button of a Movement creates the equivalent definition and replaces the node.

docs.title: Skills created before these settings
docs.text:
The old fields (spawn point, Fork anchor, Movement direction, Chain filters) are converted on opening, without changing the skill's behavior. They stay hidden in the node's options.

Before Now Main target, Branch target Anchor: Received target Aim point, Target point Anchor: Aim point Skill prefab parent, Parent module Anchor: Module body Forward caster Direction: Caster forward Chain filters and sort Target selection connected to Chain

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The configuration (UnleashSkillConfiguration, an asset) describes the rules of your game: which stats exist, which teams, which statuses, which events. Skills only contain references to this data (identifiers), picked from lists.

Nothing is hard-coded in the tool: no “Fire / Ice” enum, no “On critical hit” node. You declare your damage types, statuses and marks, and the generic nodes use them.

docs.title: Active configuration
docs.text:
• Main Menu → Load configuration / Create configuration. The loaded configuration feeds every dropdown of the editor.
  • At runtime, the Default Configuration of the UnleashSkillManager is loaded at startup.
  • You can have several configurations (production, tests, PvP mode) and switch from one to the other.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
Menu section Page Stats, Entity Types, Teams, Stat Templates, Tags Entities Damage Types, Reactions Damage and reactions Statuses (and control categories) Statuses Events, Marks, Skill tags Events, marks and skill tags General Settings, Simulation Simulation and general settings Skills List of the configuration's skills (add, edit, remove)

Compare by identifier

Each piece of data has a stable identifier (UUID). Renaming a stat or a status breaks no skill: skills keep the identifier.

docs.title: Damage types
docs.text:
A damage type (Physical, Magical, Fire…) is chosen by each damage node and each periodic status. It carries modifiers that adjust the damage based on stats: for example, the target's armor reduces physical damage.

Modifier setting Role Stat Stat read (of the attacker, or of the target with Use the target's stat). Modification type How it applies to the damage. Value source Fixed value, or stat multiplier.

Status immunities can target damage types.

docs.title: The damage pipeline
docs.text:
All damage (Simple damage, Advanced damage, periodic statuses) goes through the same path, in this order:

  1. the subject's immunities;
  2. damage taken multiplier (status);
  3. absorption (shield that absorbs N hits);
  4. redirection of a share of the damage to another entity;
  5. reflection of a share to the attacker;
  6. application, with an optional minimum HP (“bleeding cannot kill”);
  7. events (Hit, Kill, Death).

Steps 1 to 6 are status behaviors.

docs.title: Reactions
docs.text:
A reaction is what a hit does to the target's body: knockback, stun, freeze. They are applied by the Reactions node.

Behavior Effect Displacement Knockback, pull; outward, lateral, vertical directions, or along the attacker's aim. Freeze Target hitstop: its time freezes for a moment. Applies a status For example Stun applies the Stunned status. No native effect The game or a listener decides.

A new configuration contains Knockback and Stun.

docs.title: Profiles per entity type
docs.text: A profile adapts the reactions to an entity type: a boss is knocked back less (Multiplier), only beyond a Threshold, or never (Immunity). Per status category, it also sets a duration multiplier (Duration ×), an immunity, and the No diminishing returns option.

docs.title: Stats
docs.text:
A stat is a numeric value of an entity: HP, mana, attack, armor, rage…

Setting Role Stat name Name displayed and used in formulas (Stat(Strength)). Stat type Number or percentage. Has a maximum value The stat has a maximum (HP), read by “% of the maximum”. Triggers death at zero The entity dies when the stat drops to 0 (HP). Regeneration Native regeneration: amount or percentage of the maximum, at an interval (seconds). It advances with the entity's simulation time. Amount and interval are dynamic values (▾ button) evaluated for the entity that carries the stat and read again on each gain: an “HPRegen” stat drives HP regeneration with the Stat source, or a formula Stat(HPRegen) * 2. Execution values, event values and distance are 0 there. Show a slider The stat can be linked to an interface bar (UI sliders setting of the SkillCaster).

docs.title: Stat Templates
docs.text: A template gives the starting values (default and maximum) of each stat for a kind of entity: Warrior, Mage, Goblin… The SkillCaster chooses its template in its inspector; a summon can receive its own.

docs.title: Teams
docs.text: A team decides who is an ally and who is an enemy. Two entities of the same team are allies; two entities without a team as well. A skill (and each of its projectiles) has its caster's team. The nodes' “enemies” and “allies” filters rely on it.

docs.title: Entity Types
docs.text:
An entity type classifies entities: Player, Monster, Boss, Summon… A type can have a parent type: a “Monster” filter also keeps Boss entities if Boss inherits from Monster.

Use by default for skills: the type given to the skill bodies themselves (for skills that target other skills).

Types are used by filters (Entity type, Target selection), reaction profiles (a boss is not knocked back) and statuses.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text: Entity labels applied by the old Apply Tag node. For a timed effect on an entity, prefer a status: it can be cleansed, is subject to immunities and visible through “Has the status”. The labels of skills are the skill tags.

docs.title: Events, marks and skill tags
docs.text: These three sections let you write reactive skills (“when I kill an enemy…”, “when an ally is frozen…”) without a specialized node.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: An event is a combat fact broadcast to every listener. It carries a source (who caused it), a subject (who undergoes it), a value, the source skill's tags and the branch's marks.

docs.title: Native events
docs.text:
Emitted by the engine, they cannot be deleted:

Event When Hit Damage or a reaction is applied (seen as “dealt” by the source, “taken” by the subject). Kill / Death An entity dies (Kill: from the killer's point of view). Status applied / Status removed With the reason for the removal: expired, cleansed, consumed. Skill cast A skill starts. Cast interrupted A cast is cut. Summon created A Summon module spawns an entity. Obstacle contact A pushed body hits an obstacle (pinning a target against a wall).

docs.title: Custom events
docs.text: You declare your own events (Parry, Successful dodge…) with a name and a description of what they carry. They are emitted by the Emit event node or by the game's code.

docs.title: Listening
docs.text:
The On event node listens to an event while the skill lasts, with filters: role of the source and of the subject (me, my allies, my enemies, my summons, anyone), tags of the source skill, marks, event-specific filter (this status, this damage type). Each event received creates a branch whose target is the subject (or the source) and which carries the event's value.

[Start] (passive slot)
   └─► [On event]  Status applied · status = Frozen · subject = my enemies
          └─► [Apply status]  “Glacial rage” on the caster

A branch born from a listener does not fire it again: no infinite loop.

docs.title: Marks
docs.text: A mark is applied to a branch, for example Critical by a successful Chance. Damage nodes and listeners read it (“when I land a critical hit…”). A new configuration contains the Critical mark.

docs.title: Skill tags
docs.text:
A skill tag (BasicAttack, Melee, Projectile, Fire…) is set in the skill settings. It is passed in the skill's events and hits, and serves as a filter:

  • for listeners (“when a basic attack hits”);
  • for status immunities and locks (silence locks Magic skills);
  • for Replace slot and Modify cooldown (“Fire skills recharge 2 s faster”).

docs.title: General settings
docs.text:
Setting Role Configuration name, Description Identification. Game mode Real time (action, MOBA) or Turn-based (tactical RPG). In turn-based mode, durations (cooldowns, cast time, statuses, areas, channeled beams, summons, Delay, Repeat, Timer) are counted in turns (AdvanceTurn) and a skill resolves instantly on the selected targets (see Cast from code). A mode change updates the units shown in an open graph (s or turns). Presentation Skill effects, sounds and shakes, enabled by default. Unchecked (server, tests, tools): presentation commands are ignored and return PresentationHandle.None, gameplay is unchanged. Turn wait Turn-based: what the next turn waits for after a skill (SkillExecution.IsTurnReady, TurnReady event). Presentation (default): the end of its logic and of its effects; Execution: the end of its logic; None: nothing. A skill can override it (Skill settings). See Cast from code.

Presentation from code

UnleashSkillManager.PresentationEnabled reads the setting of the active configuration and follows its changes. Set from code, it holds until that setting changes (a game mode change leaves it as is). UnleashSkillConfiguration.GeneralSettingsChanged is raised when the game mode or the presentation setting of a configuration changes.

docs.title: Simulation
docs.text: Settings of the simulation world.

docs.title: World
docs.text: Setting Default Role Plane XZ XZ: 3D. XY: 2D. Static scenery Physics3D Reading of the static scenery: 3D physics, 2D physics, or none. Scenery layers none Unity layers of the scenery (walls, obstacles, ground). Do not put entity colliders there: they would stop skills like a wall. In 3D, a module body moves along the plane: the scenery stops it only where it crosses the body's height. The ground, in one collider or in tiles, and a ceiling do not stop it; a slope stops it where it reaches its height. Keep the center of the body above the ground surface. Walls layer (entities) 2 Layer of the colliders placed by a Blocker support to stop entities. Keep it out of the scenery layers.

docs.title: Fixed step
docs.text: Setting Default Role Ticks per second 60 Simulation ticks per second. Max ticks per frame 5 Beyond that, the extra ticks are dropped and the game slows down (no speed-up to catch up).

docs.title: Grid and queries
docs.text: Setting Default Role Cell size (m) 2 m Size of a cell of the spatial grid, about the size of a target. History depth (ticks) 32 Ticks of positions kept in memory (debugging, and later lag compensation). Candidate cap 64 Cap on the results of a search (0 = unlimited). Burst yes Collisions compiled by Burst; disabled, the same code in managed C#.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text: The layer matrix tells which layers touch: entities, skills, obstacles… A skill that must hit other skills (a wall that sets projectiles on fire) goes through this matrix.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
Simulation trace and warnings (dropped ticks, truncated results), gizmos in the Scene view (bodies, hurtboxes, queries), trace size.

The game's world works on a copy of these settings: a change made here in Play Mode applies to the next world (UnleashSkillManager.ResetWorld()). To turn debugging on for the current game only, from code: UnleashSkillManager.World.Settings.Debug = true (Diagnose and measure).

docs.title: Statuses
docs.text:
A status is a timed effect applied to an entity (or to a skill): Stunned, Bleeding, Shield, Rage, Invisible… It is declared once in the configuration, then skills apply it with Apply status, remove it with Remove status and adjust it with Modify status.

Every timed effect on an entity should be a status: it can then be cleansed, is subject to immunities and diminishing returns, and is visible through the “Has the status” condition and the game's interface.

docs.title: Status settings
docs.text: Setting Role Name, Icon Display (game's status bar). Positive / negative Negative: removed by a cleanse; positive: by a dispel. Category Control category (optional): diminishing returns, reaction profiles. Max stacks Maximum number of stacks. Duration Default duration when the node does not give one (0 = permanent, until removed). Stacking New application of a status already present: adds a stack and refreshes, independent durations per stack, replaces, or ignores. Presentation Effect and sound on application; attached effect and looping sound while the status is active. Behaviors What the status does (several possible).

docs.title: Behaviors
docs.text:
Behavior Effect Periodic Damage or heal per stack at an interval (damage type, dynamic value). Stat modifier Adds to a stat (fixed or in %, per stack), or replaces it while the status is applied. Lock Locks movement, actions, or skills that have certain tags (silence, disarm). Untargetable Excluded from enemy selections. Intangible Its hurtboxes are disabled: nothing hits it. Immunity To statuses (per status or category), to damage types, to skills that have certain tags. Removal on event Removed when the entity is hit (sleep), casts a skill (invisibility)… with exceptions per tag. Event only No native effect: the game or a listener decides (fear, blindness). Absorbs hits Absorbs N hits, then removes itself (reason “consumed”). Redirection Redirects X% of the damage to another entity (the closest summon…). Minimum HP HP does not go below N, optionally for a damage type, only once (resurrection). Reflection Reflects X% of the damage to the attacker. Damage taken multiplier Increases or reduces the damage taken.

Durations advance with the holder's simulation time: a status on a slowed entity lasts longer in real time.

docs.title: Control categories
docs.text:
A category (Hard control, Soft control…) groups statuses for diminishing returns: within a time window, each new application lasts less (for example 100%, 50%, 25%, then immunity for a duration). Reaction profiles can, per category, multiply the durations or disable diminishing returns (boss).

A new configuration contains the Hard control and Soft control categories, and the Stunned, Rooted and Silence statuses.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
This path goes from installation to a first skill that works in Play Mode, in four steps:

  1. Installation — requirements and opening the main menu.
  2. Set up a scene — configuration, manager, caster and targets.
  3. First skill — a fireball built node by node, tested in the preview.
  4. Cast a skill from code — connect the tool to your game's controls.

Allow half an hour for the whole path.

docs.title: Cast a skill from code
docs.text: The SkillTester is for trying things out. In a real game, your controls (player) or your AI (monsters) cast the skills, through the SkillCaster API.

docs.title: Cast a skill
docs.text:
using UnityEngine;
using UnleashSkill;
using UnleashSkill.Execution;

public class PlayerSkills : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private SkillCaster caster;
    [SerializeField] private SkillGraphModel fireball;

    void Update()
    {
        if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.Q))
        {
            SkillCastResult result = caster.Cast(fireball, out SkillExecution execution);
            if (result != SkillCastResult.Success)
                Debug.Log($"Cast refused: {result}");   // on cooldown, not enough mana, stunned…
        }
    }
}

Input System

Input.GetKeyDown belongs to the old Input Manager: with only the Input System package active (Project Settings → Player → Active Input Handling: Input System Package (New)), it throws an exception. Read the key through the Input System instead:

using UnityEngine.InputSystem;

if (Keyboard.current != null && Keyboard.current.qKey.wasPressedThisFrame)
    caster.Cast(fireball, out SkillExecution execution);

The examples of this page use Input; the same replacement applies to them (wasReleasedThisFrame for GetKeyUp).

Cast checks everything before casting: locked actions (stun), cooldown, cost. The result gives the reason for a refusal. To gray out a button without casting anything, use CanCast(graph).

docs.title: By slots
docs.text:
With a SkillSlots component on the caster, you cast by slot number. It is the recommended way: it handles combos, passives and replaced slots.

Method Use CastSlot(slot) Casts the slot's skill. PressSlot(slot) / ReleaseSlot(slot) Press and release of a key: required for charged skills (the skill fires on release) and held skills (channeling). CanCastSlot(slot) Checks without casting. CancelSlot(slot) Cancels the execution started by the last press. GetCooldownRemaining(graph) Time left before it can be cast again (seconds, or turns in turn-based mode). 
for (int slot = 0; slot < 4; slot++)
{
    if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.Alpha1 + slot)) caster.PressSlot(slot);
    if (Input.GetKeyUp(KeyCode.Alpha1 + slot))   caster.ReleaseSlot(slot);
}

docs.title: Aim
docs.text:
Skills that travel toward a point or a target read the caster's aim, which your controller fills every frame:

PointedTarget aim = caster.PointedTarget;
aim.Position = hit.point;                       // aim point (Vector3.positiveInfinity: nothing)
aim.Enemy = hit.collider.GetComponent<SkillTarget>();

PointedTarget also has Ally (pointed ally), Spell (pointed module body of another skill) and Selection (turn-based mode, below).

The aim is frozen at cast time (at the end of the cast time for a skill that has one): a projectile that left toward the aim point is no longer influenced by the mouse. An AI or a server can give the aim without going through PointedTarget:

var options = new SkillCastOptions
{
    Aim = SkillAim.Toward(point, caster.transform.position, CollisionPlane.XZ, caster.transform.forward, target)
};
graph.TryCompute(caster, out SkillExecution execution, options);

A skill that contains an Aim node (formerly Targeting) follows the mouse until confirmation, then freezes this point for the rest of the skill; it waits for a confirmation: call caster.ConfirmTargeting() on click, caster.CancelTargeting() on right-click (the cost is refunded). caster.IsAiming tells that an aim is in progress.

docs.title: Lock your controller
docs.text:
The tool moves an entity during a knockback, a rush or an attack's lunge, and locks its movement during a stun, but it does not drive your controller. Your controller reads the entity's locks and skips its own movement while it is locked:

using UnityEngine;
using UnleashSkill;

[RequireComponent(typeof(CharacterController))]
public class PlayerMovement : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private SkillCaster caster;
    [SerializeField] private float speed = 6f;
    private CharacterController controller;

    void Awake() => controller = GetComponent<CharacterController>();

    void Update()
    {
        Move(new Vector3(Input.GetAxisRaw("Horizontal"), 0f, Input.GetAxisRaw("Vertical")), Time.deltaTime);
    }

    public void Move(Vector3 input, float deltaTime)
    {
        // Knockback, rush, stun, root, attack lunge: the skill moves the entity (or nothing does), not the input
        if (caster.IsMovementLocked)
            return;

        controller.Move(Vector3.ClampMagnitude(input, 1f) * speed * deltaTime);
    }
}
Property True while IsMovementLocked a skill moves the entity (Lock Controller During Forced Movement option, until the tick after the last movement), a status locks it (Stunned, Rooted of a new configuration), a dodge or an attack phase that locks movement is running. IsActionLocked the entity can no longer cast (Stunned, an attack phase that locks actions): Cast and CanCast already refuse (ActionLocked). Read it to gray out the skill bar.

The OnLockChanged event is raised when a lock starts or ends (an animation of the stunned character, for instance). Your code can lock the entity itself: caster.Lock(source, EntityLockFlags.Movement), then caster.Unlock(source).

docs.title: Interrupt
docs.text:
• caster.CancelSkill() interrupts all the caster's running skills, caster.CancelSkill(graph) those of one skill.
  • When the caster dies or is disabled, its running skills are canceled, except those set to outlive it (see Skill settings).

docs.title: Turn-based
docs.text:
In turn-based mode (configuration, General settings), durations are counted in turns: call AdvanceTurn() once per turn of each entity, for example at the end of its turn. It is the only moment its timed effects advance:

  • Caster (caster.AdvanceTurn()): its running skills (cast, area, channeled beam, Delay, Repeat, Timer), its statuses, then its cooldowns.
  • Other entity (target.AdvanceTurn(), a SkillTarget): its statuses. The burn applied by a Fireball advances on the turn of the target that burns, not on the caster's.

A duration field keeps a single value: the same one is read in seconds in real time and in turns in turn-based mode, without conversion when the mode changes. The editor shows the unit according to the mode (“Duration (turns)”). A duration is rounded up to the next turn (0.5 → 1 turn), a rate is a whole number of turns (1 = every turn). Continuous fields (growth of an area, speed and range of the Movement) are marked visual only: they have no effect on the game.

A skill resolves instantly, in the call that casts it: no projectile flight or detection in space. Its targets are those the player selected before casting:

caster.PointedTarget.Selection.Clear();
caster.PointedTarget.Selection.Add(target);  // one or more entities
caster.CastSlot(0);                          // damage, statuses… applied before returning

Without a list, the aimed enemy (PointedTarget.Enemy), then the aimed ally (PointedTarget.Ally), act as the selection.

Module In turn-based mode Projectile, Spell body Hits the selected entities directly. Its On hit keeps its filter (enemy, ally) and its number of targets: a Fireball with 1 target hits the first selected one. Area One activation at cast on the selected entities (wherever they are). With a duration, one activation on each turn of its rate, on the same entities (those of the cast), then the area ends at the end of its duration in turns. Beam Instant: one shot. Delayed: one shot after its delay in turns. Channeled: one shot at cast then one on each turn of its rate during its duration in turns. Always on the entities selected at cast. Attack Resolves in the turn it is cast: its phases follow one another at once (Attack phase hears each of them), the impact hits each selected entity once, wherever it is, then the attack ends. Its phase durations only time the replay; the caster does not move. Summon Its lifetime is counted in the caster's turns: a 3-turn summon disappears during the caster's third AdvanceTurn(). Its movement and its contact (On hit) stay on the world tick. Chain Bounces only between selected entities, within bounce range. Aim Does not aim: it freezes the current selection for the following modules. Delay, Repeat, Timer Their delay, interval and duration are counted in the caster's turns. Cast time Counted in the caster's turns (Skill settings, “Cast time (turns)”): a 2-turn cast fires the skill during the caster's second AdvanceTurn(), on the selection of that moment; 0: the skill resolves in the call. The During cast output runs in the meantime (its Delays advance on the same turns), an interruption cancels the skill and refunds its cost. A charged cast without a key fires at its minimum in turns. CastInTurns is true and CastRemaining is in turns, for a cast bar. Statuses Duration and period (Periodic behavior) in the holder's turns: a 2-turn burn with period 1 ticks on each of the target's two turns, then expires.

The skill stays active as long as an area, a channeled beam or a delay is not over: it ends during the AdvanceTurn() that reaches the end of its duration. The world does not need to run between two turns; if it runs (for the visuals), it does not advance these durations.

A wall (Blocker) stays still in turn-based mode; its lifetime is counted in turns.

Visual replay. The fight is resolved in the call, but its presentation is replayed over time: a projectile's visual flies from its spawn point to its target at the speed of its Movement, and the impact (effect, sound, and everything its On hit nodes fire: displayed damage, statuses) is presented on arrival. With several targets (piercing), each one is presented at its arrival time and the visual flies to the farthest. A projectile without movement presents everything at cast. An impact set to play on stop is played on the contact that ends the projectile (its On hit reaches its number of targets), otherwise on the farthest target. The total duration is known as soon as the cast returns: the last replayed impact, plus the own duration of the effects it starts (one-shot effect, sound, shake, animation, read from the presentation library):

SkillExecution execution = …;                  // execution cast (already finished on the game side)
float wait = execution.PresentationDuration;   // seconds until the last effect has played

Without presentation (Presentation Enabled unchecked, see Simulation), no module visual is created and the duration is 0.

Areas and beams. Their visual is shown at cast and stays in place while they last (an area that follows its caster or its target moves with it on each turn). After its last activation, it stays visible for the Turn Display Duration of its Module Visual (1 second by default), then its end is presented (expiration effect and sound, visual removed). An instant area or beam, resolved in the cast call, is thus visible for that duration, which counts in PresentationDuration.

Waiting before the next turn. Your turn manager does not need to compute this wait: the execution tells when the next turn can start, according to the Turn wait setting (configuration, General settings; a skill can override it in its Skill settings):

Turn wait IsTurnReady becomes true Presentation (default) Once the logic of the cast is resolved, and its presentation has played (PresentationRemaining at 0). Execution Once the logic of the cast is resolved, without waiting for the effects. None Right away.

The logic is resolved (IsTurnLogicResolved) when the execution is finished, or when it only waits for turns: a cast, an area, a channeled beam, a Delay counted in turns does not hold the turn, while an aim, a dash or a module still counted in seconds (Attack) does.

caster.CastSlot(0);
SkillExecution execution = …;
execution.TurnReady += e => turnManager.NextTurn();   // raised once, after the frame that makes the turn ready

TurnReady is raised by the manager's presentation frame (also when the presentation is disabled), the first frame after the cast for a skill that is ready at once. After AdvanceTurn(), what the turn starts (outputs of an expired Delay) is waited for in the same way and TurnReady is raised again. You can also poll IsTurnReady.

docs.title: Make an entity die
docs.text: A stat set to “trigger death at zero” (HP) makes the entity die. The game can also kill it itself with TriggerEntityDeath(). By default, a dead SkillCaster cancels its skills and disables itself; override OnEntityDeath() to change this behavior (death animation, ragdoll…).

docs.title: First skill: a fireball
docs.text:
Goal: a projectile fired in front of the caster, hits the first enemy, deals 20 damage and burns it for 2 seconds.

This guide starts from the scene of Set up a scene and the default configuration (stat HP, teams Player and Enemy). It creates on the way what the default configuration does not have: a burn status and a visual for the projectile.

docs.title: A burn status
docs.text:
1. UnleashSkill → Main Menu → Statuses, then Add a status.
  2. Name it Burn, open its Settings: Default Duration 2 (seconds).
  3. Add a behavior ▾ → Periodic: Effect Damage, Stat HP, Interval 0.5, Amount Per Stack 3. The target loses 3 HP every half second while it burns.
  4. Click Save.

docs.title: A visual for the projectile
docs.text:
A projectile works without a visual, but stays invisible. Any prefab can serve as its visual:

  1. GameObject → 3D Object → Sphere, then drag it from the Hierarchy into the Project window (for example into Assets/): it becomes the prefab Sphere. Delete the sphere from the scene. Its collider is ignored: a visual has no role in the logic.
  2. UnleashSkill → Main Menu → Presentation, tab Module visuals: type Fireball in the name field and click Create.
  3. In the new definition, drag the Sphere prefab into Body Prefab. Click Save.

See Presentation for the launch, loop and impact effects a visual can also play.

docs.title: 2. Create the skill
docs.text:
• UnleashSkill → NodeEditor, then Create a new skill graph. Choose a name and a folder (for example Assets/Skills/MyFireball.asset).
  • The graph opens with a Start node: it is the entry point of the skill, called when it is cast.
  • Also possible: right-click in the Project window → Create → UnleashSkill → Skill Graph, then double-click the asset.

To add a node: Space in the graph, or right-click → Create Node. A search window lists the nodes by category (Action, Behavior, Condition, Module, Presentation, Support, Trigger).

docs.title: 3. The projectile
docs.text:
1. Add a Module → Spell body. It is a module: an object of the skill that exists in the world (projectile, area, beam…).
  2. Connect the Module output (blue) of the Start to the Module input of the Spell body.
  3. In the Spell body, choose the visual Fireball in Visual.
  4. Add a Behavior → Movement and connect its Support output (purple) to the Support input of the Spell body. Set:
    • Speed: 10 (meters per second);
    • Direction: Caster forward;
    • End Mode: Lifetime, Duration: 5 (the projectile disappears after 5 s if it hit nothing).

The size of the projectile is the Scale field of the Spell body: (1, 1, 1) gives a sphere of 0.5 m radius.

docs.title: 4. Hit an enemy
docs.text:
1. Add a Condition → On hit and connect the Condition output (orange) of the Spell body to its Condition input. This node listens to the projectile's contacts.
  2. Keep Target Filter on Enemy: only entities of another team fire what follows. The caster is never hit by its own projectile.
  3. Hit Policy: keep one target before stopping. The projectile stops at the first enemy hit (0 = it goes through everything).

docs.title: 5. The effects
docs.text:
1. Add an Action → Simple damage and connect the Trigger output (green) of On hit to its Trigger input.
    • Damage: 20;
    • Target Stat: HP;
    • Damage Type: leave empty (the default configuration has none; see Damage and reactions).
  2. Add an Action → Apply status, also connected to the Trigger output of On hit.
    • Status: Burn;
    • keep Override Duration unchecked: the status lasts the duration of its definition (2 s).

Both nodes receive the target hit: they apply to it only.

[Start] ──Module──► [Spell body] ◄──Support── [Movement]
                         │ Condition
                         ▼
                     [On hit]  (Enemy)
                         │ Trigger
                ┌────────┴────────┐
                ▼                 ▼
         [Simple damage]    [Apply status]
              20 HP              Burn

Click Save in the toolbar.

docs.title: 6. See the skill in the preview
docs.text:
Click Preview in the toolbar: a panel opens next to the graph, with a caster and dummies. The skill replays in a loop and restarts on every change to the graph.

  • ⏮ restarts, ▶ pauses, ⏭ advances one tick, the speed menu slows the playback down;
  • Frame recenters the camera;
  • Staging sets the number, layout and team of the dummies.

docs.title: 7. Cast it in Play Mode
docs.text:
1. Open the scene of Set up a scene: Player has a SkillTester.
  2. In the graph editor, click Link to scene: the skill is put in slot 0 of the SkillTester.
  3. Enter Play Mode and press Space: the sphere flies toward Enemy and hits it. Select Enemy to follow its HP in the inspector.

Each fireball takes 20 HP, plus 12 HP of burn (4 ticks of 3). After the fourth, Enemy reaches zero HP and disappears.

Nothing happens?

Check that Enemy is in front of Player (blue axis), in the team Enemy, and that the UnleashSkillManager has its configuration. Troubleshooting lists the usual causes.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Three projectiles in a fan: a Support → Fork between the Start and the Spell body.
  • An explosion on impact: replace the damage with a Module → Area fired on hit.
  • A cooldown and a mana cost: Skill settings in the toolbar (see Skill settings).

The full breakdown, with these variants, is in the Fireball recipe.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Unity 6.0 LTS (6000.0) or newer.
  • Unity packages required by the tool: Burst and Mathematics (collision core) and uGUI (entity stat bars). They are declared as dependencies of the package: if the import does not add them, install them from Window → Package Manager → Unity Registry. The editor uses UI Toolkit, a built-in module.
  • Built-in modules used by the tool, enabled in a new project: Physics, Physics 2D, Animation, Audio, Particle System, Director, UI and UI Elements. Keep them enabled in Window → Package Manager → Built-in.
  • Optional: Cinemachine 3 (camera shakes), Addressables (graph loading by name with SkillGraphLoader: the SkillGraph label instead of the Resources folders, see Skill graphs in a build), Input System (SkillTester keys, otherwise the old Input Manager). The tool detects them and works without them.
  • No render pipeline required: Built-in, URP and HDRP all work.

docs.title: Import the package
docs.text:
1. Open your project (a new 3D project is fine for this guide).
  2. Window → Package Manager, then My Assets: select UnleashSkill, click Download, then Import.
  3. Keep every file checked and click Import.

The package adds a single folder:

Folder Contents Assets/UnleashSkill/Runtime/ The framework (assembly UnleashSkill): manager, casters, nodes, simulation world, presentation Assets/UnleashSkill/Editor/ The editor (assembly UnleashSkill.Editor): main menu, graph editor, preview, translations Assets/UnleashSkill/Documentation/ This documentation for offline use (PDF), the changelog Assets/UnleashSkill/LICENSE.md, Third-Party Notices.txt License and third-party notices

Your own data never goes in this folder, so an update of the package does not touch it.

docs.title: First opening
docs.text:
When the editor compiles the package for the first time in a project without configuration, it creates the data folder Assets/UnleashSkillData/ with:

  • UnleashSkillConfiguration.asset, a default configuration: teams Player and Enemy, entity types Character and Spell (the type of the module bodies), stats HP (100, death at zero), Mana (100) and Attack (10), stat template Default;
  • Presentation/PresentationLibrary.asset and TrajectoryLibrary.asset, empty libraries for effects, sounds, visuals and trajectories.

The data folder can be moved: Edit → Project Settings → UnleashSkill.

docs.title: Editor language
docs.text: The editor is in English by default. To switch it to French: Edit → Preferences → UnleashSkill → Language. Open windows are rebuilt right away, without recompiling; Unity menus (UnleashSkill → …) stay in English. This documentation exists in both languages (language selector at the top of the page).

docs.title: The main menu
docs.text:
Open UnleashSkill → Main Menu. It is the entry point of the whole tool:

  • at the top, Load configuration / Create configuration: the active configuration (see Configuration);
  • Skill Editor: opens the graph editor;
  • Skills: the list of the configuration's skills;
  • Presentation: effects, sounds, shakes, animations and module visuals;
  • Configuration section: General settings, Simulation, Stats, Entity Types, Teams, Damage Types, Tags, Stat Templates, Reactions, Statuses, Marks, Events, Skill tags.

The graph editor also opens with UnleashSkill → NodeEditor, or by double-clicking a skill in the Project window.

Check the installation

The console shows no error, the main menu opens and shows Default Configuration at the top. If not, see Troubleshooting.

Next step: set up a scene.

docs.title: Set up a scene
docs.text: A scene that casts skills needs three things: a configuration, a manager and entities (casters and targets). This page builds a test scene step by step: a player and an enemy face to face.

docs.title: 1. Check the configuration
docs.text:
The configuration (UnleashSkillConfiguration) holds all the game data: stats, teams, entity types, statuses… Nodes pick their values from lists read from it.

  • On the first opening, the editor created a default configuration in Assets/UnleashSkillData/UnleashSkillConfiguration.asset (see Installation): UnleashSkill → Main Menu loads it automatically.
  • Load configuration chooses another one, Create configuration starts from an empty configuration. Or: right-click in the Project window → Create → UnleashSkill → Configuration.

The loaded configuration is the active configuration of the editor: every dropdown of the nodes and inspectors reads it. It is kept after a recompilation or a restart of Unity (the last one loaded, otherwise the project's). Each section is detailed in Configuration.

docs.title: 2. Add the manager
docs.text:
1. Create a new scene (File → New Scene, Basic template), and save it.
  2. Create an empty GameObject (GameObject → Create Empty), name it UnleashSkill.
  3. Add the UnleashSkillManager component to it.

It is the central point of the tool at runtime: it owns the simulation world, the running skill executions, the visual pool and the presentation system. When the component is added, its fields are filled with the project's data:

Field Role Default Configuration Configuration loaded when the game starts. Required: without it, nodes that read a stat or a type find nothing. A test or a tool of the game checks it from code with UnleashSkillManager.DefaultConfiguration. Presentation Library Library of effects, sounds, shakes, module visuals and animations. Empty: the one of the data folder (Presentation/PresentationLibrary.asset), read by the editor and given to the manager by the build. Trajectory Library Library of the trajectories read by the Trajectory node. Same rule: empty, the one of the data folder (TrajectoryLibrary.asset). Original Prefab Optional. Base object of the skill visuals, copied for each module body. Empty: a built-in empty object.

One manager per scene.

Nothing has to be filled by hand for a build: each built scene gives its manager the project libraries it lacks (the project's scene is not modified). If the project has none of them, the build writes it in the console, and the manager says it again when the game starts. A manager created from code at runtime is not completed: place it in the scene, or set PresentationLibrary.Active and TrajectoryLibrary.Active after creating it.

docs.title: 3. Create the entities
docs.text:
Every entity that casts skills or receives them (player, monster, dummy, summon) has the SkillCaster component.

  1. The player: GameObject → 3D Object → Capsule, named Player, at position (0, 1, 0). Add the SkillCaster component. When it is added, it receives the first team, the first entity type and the first stat template of the active configuration; with the default configuration:
    • Entity Type: Character;
    • Team: Player;
    • Stat Template: Default.
  2. The enemy: another capsule named Enemy, at position (0, 1, 8), that is 8 meters in front of the player (its blue axis, forward). Add a SkillCaster and change its team to Enemy (type Character, template Default).

An empty field

The inspector warns about an empty Team, Entity Type or Stat Template. Two entities without a team are allies: a skill filtered on enemies (On hit on Enemy) never touches them. A SkillCaster added from code receives nothing: set its fields yourself.

The inspector of a SkillCaster offers:

Setting Role Entity Type Type of the entity (Player, Monster…), read by the “Entity type” filters. Team Team. Two entities of the same team are allies; a skill has its caster's team. Stat Template Starting stat template (HP, mana…). Is Targetable Unchecked: the entity is never chosen as a target. Lock Controller During Forced Movement Locks the entity's movement during a movement imposed by a skill, for your character controller to read (see below). UI sliders Interface bars to update for the stats that have one.

When its health (HP) reaches zero, a SkillCaster dies: it cancels its skills and its GameObject is disabled.

docs.title: Hit shapes (hurtbox)
docs.text:
Skills hit entities through their hurtboxes, simple shapes (sphere, capsule, box) registered in the simulation world. Without settings, an entity gets a capsule derived from its collider or renderer: the capsules of this scene need nothing more. To set it, add the Hurtbox component (menu UnleashSkill/Hurtbox): one or more shapes, and an optional tag (head, weak point) passed along with the impacts.

Unity colliders are not used by skills

Skills read neither Physics nor the entities' colliders: everything goes through the simulation world. A collider stays useful to your character controller and to the static scenery.

docs.title: Movements imposed by a skill
docs.text:
A knockback, a rush or a pull moves the entity through the component it has: CharacterController first, otherwise Rigidbody, otherwise the transform directly. During an imposed movement, the entity's movement is locked (Lock Controller During Forced Movement option of the SkillCaster, checked by default): IsMovementLocked is true until the tick after its last movement.

The tool does not drive your controller: your controller reads the lock and skips its own movement while IsMovementLocked is true, otherwise the player's input is added to the knockback. The same lock comes from the statuses (Stunned, Rooted of a new configuration), a dodge and the phases of an attack that lock movement. IsActionLocked tells that the entity can no longer cast (Cast already refuses it). See the controller example in Cast a skill from code.

docs.title: Skill slots
docs.text: To cast skills by keys (slot 1, 2, 3…), the caster has a SkillSlots component that holds its skills. See Slots, passives and combos.

docs.title: 4. Test without code
docs.text:
Add the SkillTester component on Player (it adds SkillSlots with it). In Play Mode, it casts slot 0 with Space and slots 0 to 8 with keys 1 to 9: enough to try your skills before connecting them to your own controls (Cast a skill from code). The Link to scene button of the graph editor puts the open skill in slot 0 of the scene's SkillTester. Without a SkillTester in the scene, it offers to create one: a Skill Tester object at the origin, with a SkillCaster (team, type and template of the active configuration) and the SkillTester, plus a Skill Controller object with the UnleashSkillManager if the scene has none. Place it and check its team before playing.

Next step: create a first skill.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
Complete skills, broken down node by node, to rebuild in the graph editor. They do not use the example data of a project: what a recipe needs (stat, status, visual) is listed at its start.

Recipe What it shows Fireball Projectile, contact, damage, status; fan and explosion variants

More recipes will follow: areas, melee, summons, reactive passives.

docs.title: Fireball
docs.text:
Needs: the scene of Set up a scene with the default configuration (stat HP, teams Player and Enemy), a periodic status Burn and the Fireball visual (both created in First skill).

The caster throws a fireball in a straight line. It moves until it hits an enemy, deals impact damage, then burns it for 2 seconds.

docs.title: Graph
docs.text:
[Start]
   │ Module
   ▼
[Spell body] ◄─Support─ [Movement]   straight line, speed 10, 5 s
   │ Condition
   ▼
[On hit]   enemies, 1 target
   │ Trigger
   ├───────────────────┐
   ▼                   ▼
[Simple damage]   [Apply status]
  20 on HP           Burn

docs.title: Nodes
docs.text: Node Role Settings Start Entry point — Spell body The projectile: a simulated body (0.5 m sphere) and its visual Visual: fireball; Scale (1, 1, 1) Movement Moves the projectile forward Speed 10; Direction Caster forward; End Mode Lifetime, Duration 5 s On hit Listens to the projectile's contacts Target Filter Enemy; Hit Policy: 1 target, a single hit per target Simple damage Impact damage 20, stat HP; Damage Type empty (the default configuration has none) Apply status The burn Status Burn: 2 s, 3 damage every 0.5 s (Periodic behavior), definition's duration

docs.title: Why a status for the burn?
docs.text:
A burn could have been a repeated damage node. As a status, it becomes:

  • cleansable (Remove status, all negative ones);
  • subject to immunities (“immune to fire”);
  • visible to other skills (“+50% damage on a burning target”, Has the status condition);
  • displayable by the game (icon in the status bar).

docs.title: Only monsters
docs.text: Add a Condition → Entity type between On hit and the effects: only targets of the chosen type (subtypes included) are hit. Create the type first (Main Menu → Entity Types, for example Monster) and give it to the enemies.

docs.title: A damage type
docs.text: Create a damage type (Main Menu → Damage Types, for example Magic) and choose it in the Damage Type of the damage: resistances and reactions of the targets then apply to it (Damage and reactions).

docs.title: Three projectiles in a fan
docs.text: Add a Fork (Support) between the Start and the Spell body: 3 branches in a fan, each with its direction. Each projectile hits its own targets. The branch damage multiplier can reduce the damage of each projectile.

docs.title: Explosion on impact
docs.text:
Replace the effect nodes with an Area fired on hit: its Targets in the area output receives every enemy around the impact point.

[On hit] ─► [Area] radius 3 ─► [Simple damage]

docs.title: Critical hit
docs.text: Add a Chance (25%) before the damage, then a Multiply damage (×2) and a Mark branch (Critical) on its True output. An On event listener (Hit, Critical mark) can then react to critical hits.

docs.title: Charge
