docs.text: Switch the skill to a charged cast (skill settings) and give the damage a Charge dynamic value: the longer you hold, the more the fireball hurts.

docs.title: Node reference
docs.text:
One page per node: ports, fields exposed in the editor, default value and description. The node families and port types are explained in Graph, nodes and ports.

Serialized names and numeric values (port types, choices) are those of a skill's asset file: Hand-written assets explains how to write a graph by hand.

docs.title: Apply status
docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Apply status Class ApplyStatusModel Serialized type {class: ApplyStatusModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Status statusUuid Status (configuration) — Status of the configuration Holder holder Choice: ReceivedTargets (0), Caster (1), BranchSpells (2) ReceivedTargets Holder: each received target, the caster, or each received skill instance (Target selection, “spells” sources) Stacks stacks Dynamic value 1 Stacks applied (rounded, up to the status's maximum) Override Duration overrideDuration Boolean no Duration specific to the node; unchecked: the duration of the status definition Duration duration Dynamic value 5 Duration in seconds (if checked). 0 or less: nothing is applied. Turn-based: in turns, rounded up to the next turn. Link link Choice: None (0), CastPhase (1), Execution (2) None Bound to: nothing (the status follows its duration); the cast (“During cast” branch: removed at release or on interruption); the execution (passive: removed when it is disabled or on death; the execution lives until it is canceled)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to put a configured status (burn, poison, stun, shield, buff…) on an entity. What the status does (periodic damage, stat modifier, lock, immunity…) is set once in Main Menu → Statuses; the node only chooses who gets it, how many Stacks, and for how long.

  • Holder: each received target (after On hit: the entity hit), the caster (self-buff), or each received spell instance.
  • Duration: unchecked Override Duration, the status lasts the duration of its definition; checked, the node's own duration (a dynamic value: it can grow with a stat or the charge).
  • Link: Cast, in the “During cast” branch of the Start, the status is removed when the cast ends (charging aura); Execution, in a passive, it lasts as long as the passive (aura removed when the passive is disabled or on death).

The node is instant: the status lives on its holder, independently of the skill, and its outputs run if the status was applied to at least one holder.

When not to use: a single instant hit is a Simple damage; a permanent change of a stat outside any status is a Stat modifier. Prefer a status to repeated damage nodes: it can be cleansed, blocked by an immunity, and read by other skills (Has the status).

Example:

[On hit] ─┬─► [Simple damage]  20 HP
          └─► [Apply status]   Burn (definition's duration)

docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Anchor anchor Choice: ModuleBody (0), Caster (1) ModuleBody Followed anchor: the module body (projectile, attack…) or the caster Offset offset Vector3 (0, 0, 0) Offset in the anchor's frame: x to the right, y the plane normal (up in 3D), z forward Keep Relative Position keepRelativePosition Boolean no Keep the target's position relative to the anchor at the moment of the grab (plus the offset); otherwise the target is brought onto the anchor + offset Duration duration Dynamic value 0 Grab duration in seconds, at the target's pace. 0 = until the end of the anchor Movement Priority movementPriority Integer 50 Priority of the (forced) movement requests; higher than a knockback (10) by default Attached Status attachedStatusUuid Status (configuration) — Status applied to the target during the grab, removed when it ends (None = no status) Release Event releaseEventUuid Event (configuration) — Event that releases a target when it is its subject (None = no end on event)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to grab an entity and carry it: a harpoon that drags its victim, an impaling spear, a grab that holds an enemy in front of the caster. Each received target follows the Anchor (the module body, or the caster) at the Offset, pushed every tick by a forced movement request: walls still stop it. Keep Relative Position keeps the gap at the moment of the grab instead of snapping the target onto the anchor.

The grab ends, per target, when the Duration elapses (0 = as long as the anchor exists), when the anchor disappears (projectile stopped, attack finished), on the Release Event, or with a Detach node. An Attached Status (stun, “Impaled”) lasts exactly as long as the grab. The outputs run once every grab is over: chain the throw, the final hit or the knockback there.

When not to use: to push an entity once (knockback, launch), use Reactions; to move the caster, Dash.

Example:

[Start] ─► [Spell body] ─► [On hit] (Enemy, 1 target) ─► [Attach] (Module body, 2 s) ─► [Simple damage]
                ▲
           [Movement]

docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Cast skill Class CastSkillModel Serialized type {class: CastSkillModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Skill skill SkillGraphModel — Skill cast Link link Choice: Linked (0), Independent (1) Independent Bound: waits for the end of the cast skill, canceled with this skill. Independent: outputs right away Pay Cost payCost Boolean no Takes the cast skill's cost (refused if the caster cannot pay) Use Cooldown useCooldown Boolean no Respects the cast skill's cooldown (refused if it is running) and starts it

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to cast another skill from this one, so that a shared piece is built once: the same explosion cast by several skills, a follow-up skill cast at the impact point, a passive that casts a skill when it triggers. The cast skill receives the branch: its received targets (its Start passes them on), aim point, impact point and branch direction.

  • Link: Independent, the outputs run right away and the cast skill lives on its own; Linked, the outputs wait for the end of the cast skill, which is canceled with this one.
  • Pay Cost and Use Cooldown: by default the cast skill is free and ignores its cooldown (this skill was already allowed). Checked, the cast is refused if the caster cannot pay or the cooldown is running, and the node ends without outputs.

When not to use: to repeat part of the same graph, use Repeat or a Timer; to give the player another skill in a slot, Replace slot.

Example:

[Start] ─► [Spell body] ─► [On hit] ─► [Cast skill] (Explosion, Independent)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
The amount follows the configuration's damage formula (Damage formula menu): the node's base, then each step of the formula in order. By default: damage type, multipliers (branch: Fork, Chain), then the “Critical” Roll step — (base + type) × multipliers × critical. The type's modifiers (the caster's Phys att for Physical…) are therefore multiplied by the branch and by the critical hit.

The critical hit has nothing special: it is a Roll step (chance, multiplier, mark applied to the hit) that you tune, rename, delete, or complete with other rolls in the configuration. Damage Step Overrides gives this node its own chance and value for a step (e.g. a skill that crits 50% of the time).

docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Subject subject Choice: Caster (0), ReceivedTargets (1) Caster Moved entity: the caster, or each received target (summons) Direction direction Choice: Forward (0), Backward (1), TowardTarget (2), TowardTargetPoint (3), BehindTarget (4) Forward Forward / backward: branch direction (Fork), otherwise the caster's aim. Toward the target: the branch's closest one, followed. Aim point: the aim's point. Behind the target: opposite to its aim. Distance distance Number 5 Forward / backward: distance traveled, in meters. Toward a target or a point: maximum distance (0 = no limit) Duration duration Number 0.2 Duration of the movement in seconds, at the moved entity's pace (0 = instant: teleport) Stop Range stopRange Number 1 Toward the target: the dash stops at this distance from its center Behind Distance behindDistance Number 1.5 Behind the target: distance behind its center Pass Through Walls passThroughWalls Boolean yes Instant: teleport through walls; otherwise a one-tick movement, stopped by walls Movement Priority movementPriority Integer 5 Priority of the movement requests (the highest of the tick wins: a knockback of 10 interrupts the dash) Facing facing Choice: Keep (0), MovementDirection (1), Target (2) Keep Orientation of the entity: kept, turned toward the dash direction, or toward the closest target (followed; a “behind the target” ends facing it)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to move the caster as part of a skill: a charge toward the enemy, a backward leap, a blink to the aim point, a teleport behind the target. With Subject ReceivedTargets, it moves each received target instead (summons that jump on an enemy).

The movement goes through the simulation: one movement request per tick, walls respected, at the moved entity's pace. Duration 0 is a teleport (through walls if Pass Through Walls is checked). TowardTarget follows the closest received target and stops at Stop Range; BehindTarget places the entity Behind Distance behind it. The outputs run on the tick after arrival: a hit chained there starts from the arrival position. A knockback with a higher Movement Priority interrupts the dash.

When not to use: for a dodge with invulnerability frames and recovery, use Dodge; to push or pull an entity that is hit, Reactions.

Example:

[Start] ─► [Dash] (TowardTarget, 8 m, 0.3 s) ─► [Simple damage]

docs.title: Destroy spell
docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Destroy spell Class DestroySpellModel Serialized type {class: DestroySpellModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description As Expiration asExpiration Boolean no Ends the module like a natural end: its OnExpire and its expiration effect fire. Unchecked: destruction, without OnExpire

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to end modules that already exist: detonate the mines the caster placed, dispel enemy projectiles around you, recall a summoned totem. The node ends each received skill instance, whoever cast it; the instances are usually brought by a Target selection whose source finds modules (SpellsAroundCaster, SpellsAroundTargetPoint, NamedObjects).

As Expiration chooses how the module ends: unchecked, it is destroyed without its On expire; checked, it ends like a natural end, so its On expire and its expiration effect run (a mine that explodes when detonated). No instance destroyed: the node ends without outputs.

When not to use: to change a module without ending it (slow it, reflect it, grow it), use Modify spell.

Example:

[Start] ─► [Target selection] (NamedObjects: “Mine”, Count 0) ──Targets──► [Destroy spell] (As Expiration)

docs.title: Detach
docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Detach Class DetachModel Serialized type {class: DetachModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: No fields.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to release entities held by an Attach before its end: a second activation that drops the victim, a cleanse that frees an ally, a hit that breaks the grab. The node releases the current grab of each received target, whatever the skill that made it; that Attach sees it on the next tick and runs its outputs once all its grabs are over. No target attached: the node ends without outputs.

When not to use: a grab that ends after a time, with its anchor or on an event needs no Detach: set the Duration or the Release Event of the Attach.

Example:

[Start] ─► [Target selection] (AroundCaster, Ally) ──Targets──► [Detach]

docs.title: Dodge
docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Dodge Class DodgeModel Serialized type {class: DodgeModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Direction direction Choice: Forward (0), Backward (1), Left (2), Right (3), TowardTargetPoint (4) Forward Direction: forward (branch direction, otherwise the caster's aim), backward, left, right, aim point Movement Mode movementMode Choice: None (0), Advance (1), Rush (2), FixedSpeed (3), RootMotion (4) Advance Lunge: distance spread over the duration. Fixed speed. Rush: toward the aim point, at the speed, at most the distance. Root motion: the animation's. None: dodge in place (invulnerability only) Movement Ticks movementTicks Integer 12 Duration of the movement, in the caster's ticks Distance distance Number 3 Lunge: distance traveled, in meters. Rush: maximum distance (0 = no limit) Speed speed Number 10 Fixed speed and rush: speed, in meters per second Face Direction faceDirection Boolean no Turns the caster toward the dodge direction (roll); otherwise they keep their orientation (sidestep) Movement Priority movementPriority Integer 5 Priority of the movement requests (the highest of the tick wins: a knockback of 10 interrupts the movement) Invulnerability Start Tick invulnerabilityStartTick Integer 0 First invulnerability tick, from the start of the dodge (0 = right at cast) Invulnerability Ticks invulnerabilityTicks Integer 8 Invulnerability duration in the caster's ticks: intangible, no skill hits them (0 = none). Cut at the end of the dodge (movement + recovery) Recovery Ticks recoveryTicks Integer 0 Recovery ticks after the movement, before the end of the dodge and its outputs Lock Movement lockMovement Boolean yes The game's controller is locked during the whole dodge (movement and recovery) Cancelable During Movement cancelableDuringMovement Boolean no Another action of the caster can cancel the dodge during the movement (otherwise it is refused) Cancelable In Recovery cancelableInRecovery Boolean yes Another action of the caster can cancel the dodge during the recovery (otherwise it is refused) Animation animationUuid Presentation definition (AnimationDefinition) — Caster animation, played at the start of the dodge; its extracted root motion is used by the Root motion mode

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: for an action-game dodge: a roll, a sidestep, a backstep, with invulnerability frames. The caster moves for Movement Ticks (Advance spreads the Distance, FixedSpeed moves at the Speed, Rush goes toward the aim point, RootMotion uses the animation's), and is intangible from Invulnerability Start Tick for Invulnerability Ticks: no skill hits them. Optional Recovery Ticks follow the movement.

The cancel checkboxes say whether another action of the caster can interrupt the dodge during the movement or the recovery; otherwise it is refused while the dodge lasts. Lock Movement locks the game's controller. Every duration is counted in the caster's ticks (hitstop and time scales included). The outputs run at the end of the dodge; canceled, it ends without outputs.

When not to use: to move without invulnerability (a charge, a blink), use Dash.

Example:

[Start] ─► [Dodge] (Forward, Advance 3 m, 12 ticks, invulnerable 8 ticks, Face Direction)

docs.title: Emit event
docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Emit event Class EmitEventModel Serialized type {class: EmitEventModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Event eventUuid Event (configuration) — Custom event emitted (configuration, Events section) Subject subject Choice: ReceivedTargets (0), Caster (1) ReceivedTargets Subject: one event per received target, or a single one on the caster Value value Dynamic value 0 Value carried by the event, read by the listeners' “Event value” source

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to signal something that other skills react to, without linking them: “Marked target detonated”, “Combo finisher landed”, “Shield broken”. The event is a custom event of Main Menu → Events; any On event listening to it (a passive, an item, another skill) runs its outputs. The source is the caster; the Subject is each received target (one event per target) or the caster alone. Value travels with the event and is read by the listeners' Event value source (damage dealt, stacks removed…).

Native events (Hit, Death, Skill cast…) are raised by the engine itself and cannot be emitted by this node.

When not to use: to pass a value to the next nodes of the same skill, use Store value; to cast a known skill directly, Cast skill.

Example:

[On hit] ─┬─► [Remove status] (Mark, all stacks)
          └─► [Emit event] (“Mark detonated”, Subject: ReceivedTargets, Value: stacks removed)

docs.title: Heal
docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Heal Class HealModel Serialized type {class: HealModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Condition (2) 0 — Input Trigger (1) 0 — Output Condition (2) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Heal Stat healStatUuid Stat (configuration) — Healed stat (e.g. Health) Recipient recipient Choice: ReceivedTargets (0), Caster (1) ReceivedTargets Healed: each received target, or the caster, by the sum of the amounts evaluated for each received target (drain 10% of its summons' health: source Stat of the target × 0.1) Calculation Mode calculationMode Choice: Simple (0), StatBased (1), Percentage (2) Simple Simple: fixed amount. Percentage: % of the healed stat's maximum. StatBased: computed by the modifiers Amount amount Dynamic value 10 Heal amount (Simple) or percentage of the maximum (Percentage): fixed, or read at cast time (damage dealt, stat…), evaluated for each target Can Overheal canOverheal Boolean no Allows exceeding the stat's maximum Stats Used For Heal statsUsedForHeal List of StatModifierComponent (valueDamageModifier, valueDamage, modifierType, statUuid, statMultiplier, useStatFromTarget) empty Stat modifiers for the heal calculation (StatBased mode, starting from 0) Healer Stat Multiplier healerStatMultiplier Number 1 Multiplier applied to the computed heal, whatever the mode

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to restore a stat at once: health, mana, shield points. Recipient ReceivedTargets heals each received target (a heal on an ally hit, the allies of an Area); Caster heals the caster by the sum of the amounts evaluated for each received target, which makes drains: 20% of the damage dealt to each enemy hit, 10% of the health of each summon.

Calculation Mode: Simple adds the Amount (fixed or a dynamic value); Percentage adds a percentage of the stat's maximum; StatBased computes the heal from Stats Used For Heal (the caster's Spirit × 2…). Healer Stat Multiplier applies in every mode. Without Can Overheal, the stat stops at its maximum.

When not to use: a heal over time is a status with a periodic effect (Apply status); a change of a stat that is not a heal (fill the rage, drain mana) is a Stat modifier.

Example:

[Start] ─► [Area] (6 m circle) ──Targets in the area──► [Heal] (Health, Percentage 15)
              ▲ (Selection)
[Target selection] (Ally, lowest Health %, 3)

docs.title: Kill
docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Kill Class KillModel Serialized type {class: KillModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: No fields.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to kill outright, without going through the damage: a sacrifice of the caster's summons, an execute below a threshold, a trap that kills. Each living received target dies, killed by the caster: the Death event is raised and the entity's death runs (a summon ends). Stats are not touched, so no damage is dealt or reported.

The node writes the number of entities killed into the branch, readable by the next nodes through the Kills value (heal per summon sacrificed…). Its outputs run even if nobody is killed.

When not to use: when the kill must count as damage (armor, damage events, lifesteal), deal damage: an Advanced damage of the target's remaining health.

Example:

[Start] ─► [Target selection] (MySummons, Count 0) ──Targets──► [Kill] ─► [Heal] (Caster, 50 × Kills)

docs.title: Modify cooldown
docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Modify cooldown Class ModifyCooldownModel Serialized type {class: ModifyCooldownModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Spells spells SlotSelector (mode, index, spellTagUuid) — Affected skills: those of a slot (index), the current skill, or the skills that have a tag Operation operation Choice: Reset (0), Reduce (1), Set (2) Reset Reset, reduce by the value, or set the remaining time to the value Amount amount Dynamic value 0 Seconds (turns in turn-based mode) removed or set; no effect for a reset Holder holder Choice: Caster (0), ReceivedTargets (1) Caster Cooldowns of the caster, or of each received target

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to change a cooldown from a skill: reset the dash on a kill, shorten every “Fire” skill by 2 seconds on a critical hit, set an enemy's ultimate back to its full cooldown. Spells chooses which skills: those of a slot (original skill and replacement, combo steps included), the current skill, or every skill carrying a tag. Operation: Reset ends the cooldown, Reduce removes the Amount, Set sets the remaining time to the Amount (seconds, or turns in turn-based mode). Holder chooses whose cooldowns: the caster's, or each received target's.

When not to use: to cast a skill despite its cooldown only during a window, use the Free Cast option of Replace slot.

Example:

[On event] (Kill, source: me) ─► [Modify cooldown] (Slot 2, Reset)

docs.title: Modify spell
docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Modify spell Class ModifySpellModel Serialized type {class: ModifySpellModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Speed Multiplier speedMultiplier Dynamic value 1 Speed multiplier (1 = unchanged, 0 = stop, 2 = twice as fast) Scale Multiplier scaleMultiplier Dynamic value 1 Shape scale multiplier (body, area, visual; 1 = unchanged) Direction direction Choice: Keep (0), Reverse (1), TowardCaster (2), AwayFromCaster (3), TowardTargetPoint (4), BranchDirection (5) Keep New direction: unchanged, U-turn, toward / away from the node's caster, toward the aim point, branch direction

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to change modules already in flight: reflect enemy projectiles, slow every projectile in an area, call your blades back toward you, make a placed orb grow. The node changes each received skill instance, whoever cast it; the instances are usually brought by a Target selection whose source finds modules (SpellsAroundCaster, SpellsAroundTargetPoint, NamedObjects).

Speed Multiplier and Scale Multiplier combine with the previous changes and with Scale over time; Direction turns the module (Reverse for a reflect, TowardCaster for a recall, TowardTargetPoint, BranchDirection). The movement keeps its speed in the new direction. No living instance: the node ends without outputs.

When not to use: to end the modules, use Destroy spell; to set a module's growth from the start, Scale over time.

Example (reflect):

[Start] ─► [Target selection] (SpellsAroundCaster, 3 m, Enemy, Count 0) ──Targets──► [Modify spell] (Reverse, speed × 1.5)

docs.title: Modify status
docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Modify status Class ModifyStatusModel Serialized type {class: ModifyStatusModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Status statusUuid Status (configuration) — Modified status Holder holder Choice: ReceivedTargets (0), Caster (1), BranchSpells (2) ReceivedTargets Holder: each received target, the caster, or each received skill instance Duration Change durationChange Dynamic value 0 Seconds added to the duration of each stack (negative: shortens) Stack Change stackChange Dynamic value 0 Stacks added (negative: removed), rounded

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to change a status already applied, without applying it again: extend a burn by 2 seconds on each hit, shorten the caster's stun, add 3 stacks of poison, consume one stack of a charge. Duration Change adds seconds to each stack (negative shortens it; a stack brought to 0 is removed); Stack Change adds or removes stacks. Holder: each received target, the caster, or each received skill instance.

Immunities and diminishing returns do not apply: the status is already there. The outputs run if at least one holder had the status; otherwise the node ends without outputs, which also makes it a test (“if the target burns, extend and add damage”).

When not to use: to apply the status, use Apply status (its stacking rules decide refresh or new stack); to remove it, Remove status.

Example:

[On hit] ─► [Modify status] (Burn, +2 s) ─► [Simple damage] (bonus)

docs.title: Reactions
docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Reactions Class ReactionModel Serialized type {class: ReactionModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Reactions reactions List of ReactionEntry (reactionUuid, forceSource, durationSource) 1 items Reactions applied to each received target Direction direction Choice: AwayFromAttacker (0), TowardAttacker (1), ImpactNormal (2), Lateral (3), Vertical (4), AttackerAim (5) AwayFromAttacker Direction of the displacements: from the attacker toward the target, the opposite, into the target along the impact normal, to the side of the attacker's aim, upward (launch), or along the attacker's aim Movement Priority movementPriority Integer 10 Priority of the movement requests (the highest of the tick wins) Attacker Hitstop Ticks attackerHitstopTicks Integer 0 Attacker hitstop in ticks when at least one reaction is applied (0 = none)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to give a hit its physical response: knockback, launch, pull, stagger, freeze. Each entry of Reactions is a reaction of Main Menu → Reactions (displacement, freeze, event only) with its force; each received target applies it through its reaction profile (immunity, threshold, multiplier), so a boss can resist a knockback that throws a small enemy away. A reaction's status (stunned, airborne) is applied with it, and each applied reaction raises a Hit event that On event listeners hear.

Direction orients the displacements: away from the attacker (knockback), toward it (pull), along the impact normal, sideways, upward (launch), or along the attacker's aim. Attacker Hitstop Ticks freezes the attacker for a few ticks when a reaction lands, for weight. The node ends when its displacements are done; no reaction applied, it ends without outputs.

When not to use: to move the caster, use Dash; to carry a target with a module, Attach.

Example:

[Attack] ──Hit targets──► [Simple damage] ─► [Reactions] (Knockback 3 m, AwayFromAttacker, hitstop 4)

docs.title: Remove status
docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Remove status Class RemoveStatusModel Serialized type {class: RemoveStatusModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Removal removal Choice: Status (0), Category (1), AllNegative (2), AllPositive (3) Status A status, a category, or all negative / positive ones Status statusUuid Status (configuration) — Status to remove (when “A status” is chosen) Category categoryUuid Status category (configuration) — Category to remove (when “Category” is chosen) Holder holder Choice: ReceivedTargets (0), Caster (1), BranchSpells (2) ReceivedTargets Holder: each received target, the caster, or each received skill instance All Stacks allStacks Boolean yes Removes all stacks; unchecked: the number below, per status Stack Count stackCount Dynamic value 1 Stacks removed per status (if “all stacks” is unchecked)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to take statuses off: a cleanse that removes all negative statuses from allies, a purge of enemy buffs, consuming the marks of a target to detonate them. Removal chooses what goes: one Status, a Category (all poisons), or AllNegative / AllPositive. All Stacks removes everything; unchecked, Stack Count stacks per status (those lasting the longest). Holder: each received target, the caster, or each received skill instance.

The node writes into the branch the number of stacks removed and the periodic damage they would still have dealt, readable by the next nodes (StacksRemoved, RemainingDamage in a formula): detonate a poison for all its remaining damage at once. Its outputs run even if nothing is removed.

When not to use: to shorten a status or remove a few seconds of it, use Modify status.

Example (detonation):

[On hit] ─► [Remove status] (Poison, all stacks) ─► [Simple damage] (Amount: RemainingDamage)

docs.title: Replace slot
docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Replace slot Class ReplaceSlotModel Serialized type {class: ReplaceSlotModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Replacements replacements List of SlotReplacementPair (slot, skill, combo) empty Replaced slots and their replacement. Several pairs: shapeshift Duration duration Dynamic value 0 Duration of the replacement in seconds, at the caster's pace (0 = no duration) Uses uses Dynamic value 0 Uses: successful casts of the replaced slots, all pairs combined (0 = unlimited) End Event endEventUuid Event (configuration) — Event that ends the replacement, when the caster is its source or subject (None = no end on event) End Event Caster Role endEventCasterRole Choice: Subject (0), Source (1), SubjectOrSource (2) SubjectOrSource Role of the caster in the end event Toggle toggle Boolean no Toggle (shapeshift): casting this node again removes its current replacement instead of applying another one Lock Other Slots lockOtherSlots Boolean no Locked until exhausted: the other slots cannot be cast while the replacement lasts Free Cast freeCast Boolean no Free recast: the replaced slots are cast without cost, even if the skill is on cooldown (which restarts on cast)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to change the caster's skills for a while: a second activation (the dash becomes “dash again” for 3 seconds), a stance or a shapeshift (four slots replaced at once), an empowered next attack. Each pair of Replacements designates slots (index, the current skill's slot, or a tag) and the skill or combo that replaces them. Passive slots are never replaced.

The replacement ends at the first condition met: Duration, number of Uses (successful casts of the replaced slots), End Event, or Toggle (casting this node again removes it: shapeshift in and out). Without any, it lasts as long as the execution. At the end, the slots get their skills back and the outputs run. Lock Other Slots refuses the other slots meanwhile; Free Cast casts the replacement without cost and despite the cooldown, the usual setting of a second activation.

When not to use: to cast another skill once, use Cast skill; to chain the steps of an attack, a combo in the slot.

Example (second activation):

[Start] ─► [Dash] ─► [Replace slot] (current slot → “Dash again”, 3 s, 1 use, Free Cast)

docs.title: Set passive
docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Set passive Class SetPassiveModel Serialized type {class: SetPassiveModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Slot slot SlotSelector (mode, index, spellTagUuid) — Affected passive slots: an index, the current skill's slot, or a skill tag Change change Choice: Disable (0), Enable (1), Toggle (2) Disable Disable, enable again or toggle the passive Duration duration Dynamic value 0 Duration of the change in seconds, at the caster's pace, before returning to the previous state (0 = permanent)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to switch a passive of the caster from a skill: an activatable aura (the skill toggles it), a passive suppressed for 5 seconds after being hit, a stance that disables one passive and enables another. Slot designates the passive slots (index, the current skill's slot, or a tag); Change disables, enables or toggles them.

Duration 0 is a permanent change and the node is instant. With a duration, the previous state comes back at the end (or if the execution is canceled), then the outputs run. A passive that disables itself cancels its own execution: the change is then permanent.

When not to use: to change an active skill, use Replace slot.

Example (activatable aura):

[Start] ─► [Set passive] (Slot 4, Toggle)

docs.title: Stat modifier
docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Stat modifier Class StatModifierModel Serialized type {class: StatModifierModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Condition (2) 0 — Input Trigger (1) 0 — Output Condition (2) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Custom Stat customStatUuid Stat (configuration) — Stat to modify Stat Modifier Type statModifierType Choice: Append (0), Subtract (1), Divide (2), Multiply (3), Replace (4) Append Type of modification. +10% buff: Multiply 1.1; debuff of 20: Subtract 20 Value value Number 10 Value of the modification Ignore Constraint ignoreConstraint Boolean no Ignores the stat's constraints (min 0 / max)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: for a permanent change of a stat that is not damage or a heal: fill the rage to its maximum, drain 30 mana from each target, gain 1 permanent strength per kill. Stat Modifier Type chooses the operation (Append, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, Replace) and Value its operand; Ignore Constraint lets the stat leave its minimum and maximum. The node applies to each received target and runs its outputs if it changed at least one.

The change is permanent and instant: a timed buff or debuff is a status with a stat modifier behavior, applied by Apply status, which can be cleansed, stacked and read by other skills.

When not to use: to lose health through the damage formula, use Simple damage; to restore health, Heal.

Example:

[On event] (Kill, source: me) ─► [Stat modifier] (Rage, Append 20)

docs.title: Store value
docs.text: Category Action Creation menu Action/Store value Class StoreValueModel Serialized type {class: StoreValueModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Variable variable Skill variable — Skill variable written (skill settings) Operation operation Choice: Set (0), Add (1) Set Set the variable to the value, or add the value to it Value value Dynamic value 0 Value written: fixed, or read at cast time (damage dealt, stat, number of targets…)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to remember a value during the cast and use it further on: the number of enemies hit by the first wave, the damage dealt by the opening strike, the caster's health at cast time. The Variable is declared in the skill's settings (Skill settings → Variables); the node sets it to the Value or adds the value to it (Add: a counter). The value is evaluated for the first received target.

The variable is shared by the whole execution, every branch included: any later node reads it through a dynamic value (Execution value mode, or Var(name) in a formula).

When not to use: to signal a value to other skills, use Emit event.

Example:

[Area] ──Targets in the area──► [Store value] (Hits, Add 1)
[Delay] (1 s) ─► [Simple damage] (Amount: 10 × Hits)

docs.title: Scale over time
docs.text: Category Behavior Creation menu Behavior/Scale over time Class ScaleOverTimeModel Serialized type {class: ScaleOverTimeModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Behaviors, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Module (0) 0 — Input Support (3) 0 — Output Support (3) 0 — Output Condition (2) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Start Scale startScale Dynamic value 1 Scale when the module starts (1 = the module's configured size) End Scale endScale Dynamic value 2 Scale reached at the end of the duration, kept afterwards Duration duration Dynamic value 1 Duration of the growth in simulation seconds (0 = end scale immediately) Curve curve AnimationCurve — Scale progression: normalized time (0-1) → share of the way traveled between start and end (0-1)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to make a module grow or shrink over its life: a fireball that swells as it flies, a ring of fire that widens, a poison cloud that dissipates. Connected as a support of a module, it takes the module's scale from Start Scale to End Scale in Duration simulation seconds, along the Curve, then keeps the end scale. The scale multiplies everything that has a size: the swept body, the area's radii and width, and the visual.

The node does not decide when the module ends: its lifetime, On hit or Max Lifetime do.

When not to use: to change the size of a module already in flight from another skill or event, use Modify spell (Scale Multiplier).

Example:

[Start] ─► [Area] (3 m circle, Tick Rate 0.5) ──Targets in the area──► [Simple damage]
              ▲
     [Scale over time] (1 → 3, 2 s)

docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Module (0) 0 — Input Support (3) 0 — Input Selection (4) 0 — Output Support (3) 0 — Output Condition (2) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Movement Type movementType Choice: Line (0), Boomerang (1), Wander (2), Pursuit (3) Line Line: straight ahead. Boomerang: go out to the range (or half the duration), then return toward the caster; ends on reaching them. Wander: the direction turns randomly at each interval, in the play plane. Pursuit: turns toward the target of the connected Selection, otherwise toward the received target Speed speed Dynamic value 10 Movement speed (m/s). Turn-based: no effect on the game (visual only). Acceleration acceleration Dynamic value 0 Acceleration (m/s², negative: braking; speed does not go below 0). Boomerang: on the way out. Hidden if Movement Type = Pursuit. Turn-based: no effect on the game (visual only). Direction direction Direction: Toward the aim point (0), Caster forward (1), Toward the received target (2), Away from the caster (3), Random (4) — Start direction from the module body: toward the aim point, caster forward, toward the received target, away from the caster or random; a branch direction (Fork) takes precedence End Mode endMode Choice: MaxRange (0), Lifetime (1) MaxRange Ends at the range (distance traveled) or at the duration. Hidden if Movement Type = Pursuit. Max Range maxRange Dynamic value 50 Distance traveled at the end (m). Boomerang: range of the way out. Hidden if Movement Type = Pursuit. Hidden if End Mode = Lifetime. Turn-based: no effect on the game (visual only). Duration duration Dynamic value 5 Duration of the movement (s). Boomerang: way out during half the duration. Hidden if Movement Type = Pursuit. Hidden if End Mode = MaxRange. Turn-based: no effect on the game (visual only). Catch Radius catchRadius Dynamic value 0.5 Distance to the caster at which the module is caught (end of the movement). Shown if Movement Type = Boomerang. Wander Interval wanderInterval Dynamic value 0.5 Interval between two direction changes (s). Shown if Movement Type = Wander. Turn-based: no effect on the game (visual only). Wander Angle wanderAngle Dynamic value 45 Maximum rotation at each change (degrees, rolled between -angle and +angle). Shown if Movement Type = Wander. Rotation Speed rotationSpeed Dynamic value 180 Maximum rotation speed toward the target (degrees per second). Shown if Movement Type = Pursuit. Turn-based: no effect on the game (visual only). Pursuit Duration pursuitDuration Dynamic value 5 Duration of the pursuit (s, 0 = unlimited). Shown if Movement Type = Pursuit. Turn-based: no effect on the game (visual only). Lost Target lostTarget Choice: ContinueStraight (0), Stop (1), NextSegment (2), Reacquire (3) ContinueStraight Lost target (dead, disabled or missing): keep going straight, stop, end the movement, or reacquire a target through the connected Selection. Shown if Movement Type = Pursuit.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
The movement of a module (Spell body, Area, Summon…): connected as Support, it gives the body its trajectory, run by the trajectory engine at the body's step (time scales and hitstop included).

  • Line: straight ahead, at constant or accelerated speed (braking: negative acceleration), until the range or the duration.
  • Boomerang: out to the range (or during half the duration), then back toward the caster; the module ends when it is caught.
  • Wander: the direction turns randomly at each interval, in the play plane (the execution's roll, reproducible).
  • Pursuit: turns toward its target, at most Rotation Speed degrees per second. Connect a Target selection to the Selection input to choose the target (“the most wounded enemy”); without it, the node follows the first received target of the module.

The start Direction is “toward the aim point” by default; a branch direction (Fork) takes precedence. Modify spell (redirection) rotates the trajectory's frame: a line continues in the new direction, a pursuit resumes its rotation toward the target.

Replaces the obsolete Movement and Homing Movement nodes.

The Convert to definition button adds the equivalent definition to the trajectory library (main menu → Trajectories) and replaces the node with a Trajectory node, connections kept: to go further (curve, orbit, oscillation, bounce on walls). A dynamic duration (stat, variable) stays dynamic in the definition.

Start ──► Spell body ──► On hit ──► Damage
              ▲
   Movement (Pursuit) ◄── Target selection (the most wounded)

docs.title: Trajectory
docs.text: Category Behavior Creation menu Behavior/Trajectory Class TrajectoryModel Serialized type {class: TrajectoryModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Behaviors, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Module (0) 0 — Input Support (3) 0 — Input Selection (4) 0 — Output Support (3) 0 — Output Condition (2) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Trajectory trajectoryUuid Trajectory (library) — Definition from the trajectory library (UnleashSkill > Main Menu > Trajectories) Direction direction Direction: Toward the aim point (0), Caster forward (1), Toward the received target (2), Away from the caster (3), Random (4) — Forward of the trajectory's frame, from the module body: toward the aim point, caster forward, toward the received target, away from the caster or random; a branch direction (Fork) takes precedence

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
The movement of a module through a trajectory definition of the global library (main menu → Trajectories): a sequence of segments played one after another in the aim frame (forward = Direction, side = right), run by the same engine as the Movement node.

Available segments:

  • Line: speed, acceleration, angle in the frame, end at the distance, at the duration or never, wander.
  • Curve toward a point: toward an anchor (aim point by default), in a duration or at a speed, with a lateral curvature (positive: to the right) and an Apex Height (bell, lobbed shot). Exact arrival at the destination, brought back into the play plane of the start.
  • Orbit: around the caster, the aim point, the received target or a named object (read again on each tick), radius reached in a quarter turn, clockwise or counterclockwise, end after turns, a duration or never.
  • Pursuit: toward the target of the Target selection connected to the Selection input, otherwise the first received target.
  • Return: toward the caster or an anchor, end at the catch radius.

Each segment has a rule when blocked (wall, scenery, blocking body): stop (end of the module), slide along the obstacle, bounce, or move to the next segment; and overlaid oscillations (side or height, amplitude, frequency, phase). The definition has a time scale and can loop from a segment.

Max Blocks limits the blocks a segment handles with its rule (bounces, slides): 0, the default, is unlimited. The next block follows After Max Blocks: stop (end of the module, like a block without a bounce, the default) or next segment (from the contact point). The count restarts at each segment. A ricochet that bounces three times then disappears: Line, rule Bounce, Max Blocks 3; a bullet that bounces twice then flies back to the caster: After Max Blocks Next segment, followed by a Return segment.

To act on each bounce, put an On blocked under the module: it fires its outputs at each block the trajectory goes on from (effect, sound, area at the contact point). The Blocks execution value (formula Blocks) reads the number of blocks of the module body: as the Damage Multiplier max(0, 1 - 0.25 * Blocks) of an Advanced damage under the On hit, the damage drops by 25% after each bounce.

Height: the Apex Height of a Curve and the height oscillations move the body along the normal of the play plane. In 3D (XZ plane), it is a real movement: a lobbed shot passes over an entity standing lower than it and hits an obstacle or an entity higher than it, in the air (the scenery stops a body only where it crosses its height). In 2D (XY plane), the body stays in the plane, with its collisions: only the visual is offset along the normal (Z). A top-down 2D view, whose camera looks along Z, does not show it; a side view draws its bell in the plane with the curvature of the Curve instead.

Rules in flight, per segment: Hits In Flight unchecked, the body passes through entities and other module bodies without hitting them during the segment (obstacles still stop it); Ignores Obstacles, walls and scenery no longer stop it. Both override the Hit Policy of the module's On hit for the duration of the segment, and the next segment applies its own. A mortar shell detects on arrival: Curve with an apex, Hits In Flight unchecked, then an On expire (with Trigger If Destroyed, to also explode against a wall) followed by an instant Area anchored on the module body:

Start ──► Spell body ──► On expire ──► Area (instant, Module body) ──► Damage
              ▲
   Trajectory “Mortar lob” (Curve toward the aim point, Apex Height 4, Hits In Flight unchecked)

A pushed module body (forced movement) suspends its trajectory, then resumes it from its new position.

A Movement node converts to a Trajectory through its Convert to definition button: the equivalent definition is added to the library, the node is replaced, connections kept.

Start ──► Spell body ──► On hit ──► Damage
              ▲
   Trajectory “Lob” (Curve toward the aim point, bounce)

When blocked and Hit Policy: the segment's rule decides before the Hit Policy of the module's On hit. A body that bounces bounces even if Blocked By Obstacles is Yes; the wall ends the module only when no segment continues. With Blocked By Obstacles No, the body passes through walls and the rule never applies. A body stopped by a wall is destroyed, not expired: On expire fires only with Trigger If Destroyed.

docs.title: Chance
docs.text: Category Condition Creation menu Condition/Chance Class ChanceConditionModel Serialized type {class: ChanceConditionModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Conditions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Condition (2) 0 — Input Trigger (1) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 True Output Trigger (1) 1 False

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Chance Source chanceSource Dynamic value 50 Probability of firing the True output, in % (0 = never, 100 = always): fixed, or read at cast time (critical chance stat…). Otherwise, False output

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Rolls a chance on each pass and switches the branch: success → True output, failure → False output. An unconnected output stops the branch. The roll uses the execution's randomness (reproducible for a seed); a chance read from a stat is evaluated for the branch's first target. The targets are not modified.

Chance only rolls: what the success does is connected after the True output.

On hit ──► Chance (25) ──True──► Mark branch (Critical) ──► Simple damage
                       └─False──► Simple damage
  • Forced critical hit: Mark branch with the Critical mark, the damage formula's Roll step then succeeds without rolling.
  • Doubled damage: Multiply damage (factor 2), before the damage nodes.
  • Other effect: any node on the True output (another fireball, a status…).

Graphs saved before 1.0: the damage multiplier and the success mark, if they were set, stay applied to the True branch and are shown in the node's options; set them back to 1 and empty after connecting the equivalent nodes.

docs.title: Entity type
docs.text: Category Condition Creation menu Condition/Entity type Class EntityTypeConditionModel Serialized type {class: EntityTypeConditionModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Conditions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Condition (2) 0 — Input Trigger (1) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Entity Type entityTypeUuid Entity type (configuration) — Entity type to keep among the targets (subtypes are included)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to keep only some kinds of entities among the received targets: bonus damage against undead, a heal that only affects mechanical allies, a spell that ignores buildings. A target is kept if its type is the chosen Entity Type or inherits from it (types are configured in Main Menu → Entity Types, with their hierarchy). The outputs run with the remaining targets, only if at least one remains.

When not to use: to choose targets among candidates with several criteria (type, team, status, stat, distance, count), use a Target selection; for a stat threshold, Stat condition.

Example:

[On hit] ─┬─► [Simple damage] (20)
          └─► [Entity type] (Undead) ─► [Simple damage] (bonus 30)

docs.title: Attack phase
docs.text: Category Condition Creation menu Condition/Attack phase Class OnAttackPhaseModel Serialized type {class: OnAttackPhaseModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Conditions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Phase phase Choice: Startup (0), Active (1), Recovery (2) Active Phase whose start fires the outputs

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to act at a precise moment of an Attack: a sound and a flash when the wind-up starts, a step forward when the active frames begin, a recovery effect. Connected to the attack's Listeners output, it runs its outputs once, on the tick its Phase starts (Startup, Active, Recovery), in the attack's branch. It ends with the attack; a phase of 0 ticks never starts.

When not to use: to act on the entities the attack hits, use its Hit targets output (or an On hit).

Example:

[Start] ─► [Attack] ──Hit targets──► [Simple damage]
              └──Listeners──► [Attack phase] (Startup) ─► [Play sound] (Swing)

docs.title: On blocked
docs.text: Category Condition Creation menu Condition/On blocked Class OnBlockedModel Serialized type {class: OnBlockedModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Conditions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Trigger On Stop triggerOnStop Boolean no Also fires for the block that stops the module body (no movement goes on: end of the module)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Under a module's Condition output: fires its outputs each time the module body is blocked (wall, scenery, blocking body) and its movement goes on: bounce, slide or next segment of its Trajectory (When blocked rule, Max Blocks). The block that stops the body, which ends the module, only fires with Trigger On Stop.

Each block starts in a branch of its own, without a received target, at the contact point (impact point and normal of the branch): an effect or a sound on the wall, an Area at the impact point, a fragment launched from the wall. A damage node directly under On blocked has no target: go through an Area.

The Blocks execution value (formula Blocks) reads the number of blocks of the module body, bounce included: 1 at the first one. Read in the Damage Multiplier of an Advanced damage under the module's On hit, it lowers or raises the damage after each bounce: max(0, 1 - 0.25 * Blocks) loses 25% per bounce.

Start ──► Spell body ──► On hit ──► Advanced damage (multiplier: max(0, 1 - 0.25 * Blocks))
              │  ▲
              │  Trajectory “Ricochet” (Line, Bounce, Max Blocks 3)
              └──► On blocked ──► Play effect (spark at the impact point)

A Movement node stops on the first wall (rule Stop): On blocked only fires there with Trigger On Stop.

docs.title: On expire
docs.text: Category Condition Creation menu Condition/On expire Class OnExpireModel Serialized type {class: OnExpireModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Conditions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Trigger If Destroyed triggerIfDestroyed Boolean no Also fires when the prefab is destroyed before expiring (e.g. projectile destroyed on impact) Only If No Hit onlyIfNoHit Boolean no Only fires if the module hit no entity during its life (missed shot). Scenery does not count as a hit

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Under a module's Condition output: fires its outputs when the module's prefab disappears (end of life, or destruction with Trigger If Destroyed), at the last position of the module body. Example: an arrow that leaves a fire area where it stops (Area anchored on the parent prefab).

In real time, the outputs fire at the world tick that follows the disappearance. In turn-based mode, the module resolves in the cast call: the outputs fire at the end of the current start, without a tick.

Expired or destroyed? Expiration is the module's own end: end of its movement (range, duration, end of the trajectory), Max Lifetime, Duration of an area. Everything else is a destruction: a body stopped by a wall, the scenery or a blocking body, a body that reached the number of targets of its On hit, a module removed by another node. A projectile stopped by a wall therefore fires On expire only with Trigger If Destroyed. A body that bounces or slides along the wall is not stopped: it goes on.

For an explosion at the impact or at the end of the range, never missed nor doubled: one On expire with Trigger If Destroyed, under the projectile. It fires exactly once, however the module ends (except when the execution is canceled).

docs.title: On hit
docs.text: Category Condition Creation menu Condition/On hit Class OnHitModel Serialized type {class: OnHitModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Conditions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Target Filter targetFilter Choice: Any (0), Enemy (1), Ally (2) Enemy Entities hit that fire the outputs, by team relation with the caster: any, enemies or allies Hit Policy hitPolicy HitPolicy (maxTargets, rehit, rehitCooldown, blockedByObstacles, requireLineOfSight) — Hit rules of the module body: targets before stopping (1 = classic projectile, 0 = unlimited piercing), re-hit of the same target, obstacles, line of sight.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to act on what a module touches. Connected to the Condition output of a module, it listens to its body: for each entity hit that passes Target Filter (enemy, ally, any), it runs its outputs in a branch of its own, whose only target is the event's target (the entity hit), with the impact point. The nodes after it (damage, status, effect at the impact point) therefore apply to that entity only.

On a Spell body, its Hit Policy becomes the rules of the moving body: number of targets before it stops (1 = classic projectile, 0 = pierces everything), hitting the same target again, stopped by walls, line of sight. When the body stops, the module ends. On a module that detects by itself (Area, Beam), it receives the targets that module detected.

When not to use: to act on every entity of an area at once, use the Area's Targets in the area output. To react to hits from any skill (passive “when I am hit”), use On event with the Hit event.

Example:

[Start] ─► [Spell body] ─► [On hit] (Enemy, 1 target) ─┬─► [Simple damage]
                ▲                                       └─► [Play effect] (impact point)
           [Movement]

Against a wall, the When blocked rule of the trajectory segment (Trajectory) decides first: with Bounce, Slide or Next segment, the body goes on, even if Blocked By Obstacles is Yes. The wall stops the body, and ends the module, only when no segment continues (rule Stop, the default and that of the Movement node, no next segment, or Max Blocks reached). Blocked By Obstacles decides whether walls block the body at all: with No, the body passes through them and the segment's rule never applies. A body stopped by a wall is destroyed, not expired (On expire).

Under an Area, a Beam or a Summon (modules that detect by themselves), the On hit filters the detected entities with part of its Hit Policy:

  • Rehit Once: an entity fires the outputs only once over the module's whole life (a persistent area that hits each target once). Cooldown: an entity fires them again once Rehit Cooldown has elapsed in the module's time (time scales and hitstop included, within one tick; in turn-based mode, in turns rounded up), for example once every two activations of an Area with a Tick Rate of 0.5 and a Rehit Cooldown of 1. Every Tick: on each detection, so at the module's Tick Rate.
  • Max Targets: once that many entities are hit, the module ends. The default policy has 1 target: an Area with that On hit ends at its first entity. Set Max Targets to 0 for an explosion or an aura. The Node Editor shows the warning W116 on an On hit with Max Targets 1 under a module that lasts (Area or channeled Beam with a Duration, Summon).
  • Blocked By Obstacles and Require Line Of Sight do not apply: the module's detection decides (for an Area, its own Require Line Of Sight).

docs.title: On tick
docs.text: Category Condition Creation menu Condition/On tick Class OnTickModel Serialized type {class: OnTickModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Conditions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Tick Interval tickInterval Number 0.5 Interval between two ticks, in seconds (> 0) Max Ticks maxTicks Integer -1 Maximum number of ticks (-1 = as long as the module's prefab exists) Trigger On Start triggerOnStart Boolean yes A first tick as soon as the module appears

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to do something periodically while a module exists, at its position: an arrow that drops a fire puddle every 0.5 s along its path, a totem that pulses, a rolling boulder that leaves a trail. Connected to a module's Listeners output, it runs its outputs every Tick Interval seconds in the module's branch, so a node anchored on the module body plays where the module currently is. Trigger On Start adds a first tick as soon as the module appears; Max Ticks caps the count (-1 = as long as the module lives). It ends with the module.

When not to use: for a rhythm that does not depend on a module (a passive aura, a channel), use a Timer; for an area that damages everything inside it periodically, set the Area's Tick Rate.

Example:

[Start] ─► [Spell body] ──Listeners──► [On tick] (0.5 s) ─► [Area] (Module body, 2 m) ──Targets in the area──► [Simple damage]
                ▲
           [Movement]

docs.title: Stat condition
docs.text: Category Condition Creation menu Condition/Stat condition Class StatConditionModel Serialized type {class: StatConditionModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Conditions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Target Entity targetEntity Choice: Caster (0), Target (1) Target Caster: checks the caster (all or nothing). Target: filters each target of the context Stat statUuid Stat (configuration) — Which stat to check Comparison Operator comparisonOperator Choice: GreaterThan (0), LessThan (1), EqualTo (2), NotEqualTo (3), GreaterOrEqual (4), LessOrEqual (5) GreaterThan Comparison operator Comparison Type comparisonType Choice: Value (0), Percentage (1) Value Comparison type (absolute value or percentage of the stat's maximum) Comparison Value comparisonValue Number 0 Value to compare (as an absolute value or a percentage depending on the type) Execute Only If True executeOnlyIfTrue Boolean yes If false, the condition is ignored: the outputs always fire, without filtering the targets

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to act only above or below a stat threshold: an execute that only hits enemies under 20% health, a heal reserved for wounded allies, a desperate strike that only works when the caster is under 30% health. Comparison Type compares the absolute value or a percentage of the stat's maximum.

  • Target Entity Target: filters the received targets one by one; the outputs run with those that pass, if at least one remains.
  • Target Entity Caster: all or nothing on the caster's stat; the received targets go through unchanged.

Unchecked, Execute Only If True disables the test (the outputs always run): handy to try a skill without the condition.

When not to use: to choose “the 3 most wounded allies” among candidates, use a Target selection (stat filter and sort); to test any expression (stat and status, distance…), Check condition.

Example (execute):

[On hit] ─► [Stat condition] (Target, Health < 20%) ─► [Kill]

docs.title: Debug log
docs.text: Category Debug Creation menu Debug/Debug log Class DebugLogModel Serialized type {class: DebugLogModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Utils, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Debug Message debugMessage Text — Message written to the Unity console when the node runs (development only)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: while building a skill, to check that a branch is reached, and when. Insert it after the node to watch: the Debug Message appears in the Unity console each time the branch passes, and its output continues the chain, so the nodes after it still run. Remove it before shipping: it has no effect on gameplay and only clutters the console. The scene preview and the skill's flow analysis are usually faster to see what a branch receives.

Example:

[On hit] ─► [Debug log] (“Fireball hit”) ─► [Simple damage]

docs.title: Ports

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Visual visualUuid Presentation definition (ModuleVisualDefinition) — Module visual (presentation library): body prefab, launch, loop, impact and expiration effects and sounds. Empty: invisible body Scale scale Vector3 (1, 1, 1) Dimensions of the simulated body's box (one-meter cube scaled), approximated by a swept capsule: axis along the largest dimension, radius = half of the smallest of the other two. A cube gives its inscribed sphere. Offset offset Vector3 (0, 0, 0) Position offset Anchor anchor Anchor: Caster (0), Aim point (1), Received target (2), Module body (4), Impact point (5), Named object (6) — Spawn point, before the offset: caster, aim point, received target, module body, impact point or named object. Falls back to the caster if the point does not exist Object Name objectName Skill named object — Name (skill named objects) under which the module registers with its caster: another skill finds it (Target selection, spawn point). Empty: none. docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Area: on each activation, the entities whose hurtbox overlaps the shape go out through the “Targets in the area” output; the listeners (OnHit…) receive the detected entities.

Choose among the entities in the area: connect a Target selection to the “Selection” input. Its filters, its sort (distance measured from the area's center) and its count replace the area's team filter, on each activation: “the 3 most wounded enemies in the area”. The Selection's source is not read: the candidates are always the entities in the area. The listeners keep their own filter.

[Area: 6 m circle] ──Targets in the area──► [Heal]
        ▲ (Selection)
[Target selection: allies, lowest stat (HP), 3]

Area or Spell body? The area detects by itself: on each activation (a single one if Tick Rate is 0), all the entities whose hurtbox overlaps its shape, whether it moves or not. The Spell body hits what its body meets on its path, swept by the world on each tick: it is the module of a projectile. For an area (explosion, aura, poison puddle), an Area; for an object that flies and strikes, a Spell body — followed if needed by an Area at the impact point.

Walls: by default, walls and the scenery do not cut an area. An entity whose hurtbox overlaps the shape is detected, even behind a wall. With Require Line Of Sight, an entity is kept only if nothing cuts the line from the area's center to its own: the static scenery (Scenery Layers) and the bodies of the Obstacle layer (walls, Blocker that blocks the caster's side) hide it, an explosion no longer hits behind a wall. The line goes from the center, not from the edge of the shape: a pillar inside the area hides what stands behind it, seen from the center. In turn-based mode, the same rule applies to the selected entities, from the area's center. The listeners receive the same entities.

Number of activations: a first activation at launch, then one every Tick Rate seconds, as long as it falls strictly before the end of Duration: for a Duration above 0, ⌈Duration / Tick Rate⌉ activations (Duration 3 and Tick Rate 0.5: 6 activations, at 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2 and 2.5 s; none at 3 s). The intervals are regular from the first one, counted in simulation time (time scales and hitstop included) from the tick that detects at launch. A Duration of 0 or a Tick Rate of 0 gives a single activation. In turn-based mode, the same rule in turns of the caster: Duration 3 and Tick Rate 1, 3 activations (at launch, then on its next two turns).

Listeners: an On hit under the Area applies its Hit Policy to the detected entities: with Rehit Once, an entity is hit once over the area's whole duration; with Every Tick, at each activation; with Cooldown, again once Rehit Cooldown has elapsed in the area's time (a Tick Rate of 0.5 and a Rehit Cooldown of 1: once every two activations). Its Max Targets ends the area once reached: with the default policy (1 target), the area ends at its first entity, and the Node Editor shows the warning W116 on the On hit when the area has a Duration. For an explosion or an aura, set Max Targets to 0.

Permanent aura: an Area has no unlimited duration (Duration 0 = instant, a single detection). For an aura that lasts as long as its execution (a passive), use a Timer with a Total Duration of 0, followed by an instant Area anchored on the caster, or by a Target selection around the caster.

[Start] ─► [Timer] (0.1 s, 0, Fire Immediately) ─► [Area] (Anchor: caster, 4 m, Duration 0) ──Targets in the area──► [Simple damage]

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Box that follows a bone: choose the attack's animation, then the bone (Follow Bone); Box Center and Box Rotation become relative to the bone. If the bone is not found at cast time (animation missing from the active presentation library, bone not extracted), the box is placed at the Missing Bone Center, relative to the caster (1.25 m in front of them by default), and the console shows a warning, once per skill and per bone. The scene preview flags the case in yellow, with the fallback box.

Turn-based: the attack resolves in the turn it is cast, without waiting for world ticks. Its phases follow one another at once (the Attack phase listeners hear each of them), the impact hits the selected entities (the controller's selection, or the one frozen by the Aim node), each once, wherever they are, then the attack ends. The phase durations only time the presentation: with it, the animation, the impact effects and the end are replayed at their time in ticks from the cast. The caster does not move (Movement Mode ignored), and nothing can cancel or interrupt the attack.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: for a ray that hits instantly along a line: a laser, a lightning bolt, a piercing shot, a channeled drain. The beam starts from its Anchor in its Direction (toward the aim point by default; a branch direction from a Fork takes precedence) over its Range, and hits the entities along the line, from the nearest to the farthest, with a Width of 0 for a thin ray. Unless Penetrate Walls is checked, it stops at the first obstacle.

  • Beam Type Instant: one shot at launch. Delayed: one shot after Delay Before Activation (a telegraphed strike). Channeled: one shot per Tick Rate during Duration; with Stop On Release, firing stops when the player releases the key, and Follow Live Aim makes the beam follow the mouse between shots.
  • Number of shots (Channeled): a first shot at launch, then one every Tick Rate seconds, as long as it falls strictly before the end of Duration: ⌈Duration / Tick Rate⌉ shots for a Duration above 0 (Duration 1 and Tick Rate 0.25: 4 shots, at 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 s). The intervals are regular from the first one, counted from the tick that fires at launch. With Stop On Release, the shots stop at release.
  • The entities hit go out through Hit targets; the Listeners (On hit…) receive them too, with the impact point.

In turn-based mode, durations, period and delay are counted in the caster's turns.

When not to use: for a projectile that travels and can be dodged, use a Spell body with a Movement; for an area, an Area.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Spell body: a module that moves and hits. It has a simulated body in the world (a capsule taken from Scale), which its behaviors (Movement…) move forward; on each tick, the world sweeps this body between its two positions and gives the entities met on the way to its listeners (On hit…). The Visual is only the appearance: it follows the body, with no role in the logic. Without a behavior, the body stays still (until Max Lifetime).

It is the module of a projectile, an arrow, a fireball, a thrown object that bounces.

[Start] ─► [Spell body] ─► [On hit] ─► [Simple damage]
                 ▲ (Support)
            [Movement]

Spell body or Area? The Spell body hits what its body meets while moving: an entity is hit when the body goes through it or reaches it, its output fires from its listeners. The Area does not move to hit (it can follow the caster or a target): it detects by itself, on each activation, the entities whose hurtbox overlaps its shape (circle, cone, ring…), and sends them through its “Targets in the area” output. For “what is on the path”, a Spell body; for “what is in the area, now or on each tick”, an Area.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Summons a world entity, of the caster's team, which follows them, orbits or stays in place.

The entity is the Entity prefab: gameplay data, read even when the presentation library is missing (build without a library, server). Left empty, the summon uses the body prefab of its Visual; without either, the node fails and logs an error.

Its stats start from the Stat template chosen on the node, or failing that from the prefab's: the same prefab serves several summons with different stats. The Initial stats then apply (e.g. HP = 20% of the caster's max HP, through a dynamic value).

The “Selection” input receives the Target selection that will choose the summon's target: it will be read by the AttackEnemies behavior, not implemented yet. Connected today, it has no effect.

Turn-based: the Lifetime counts the caster's turns (AdvanceTurn of the caster): a summon of 3 turns disappears at the caster's 3rd turn after its cast. Its movement, its contact (On Hit listeners) and its end when it dies stay on the world tick.

Limit in turn-based mode: the contact of a summon

A summon's contact is not resolved on the caster's turn: it is an overlap of its body, detected on the world tick, never on the targets selected for the turn. In turn-based mode, an On hit connected to a Summon therefore depends on the number of world ticks that run between two turns: it may fire several times, or never if the world does not advance between turns, and it is not reproducible turn by turn. To hit on a turn, cast a skill from the summon (an Attack, a Spell body…) during its turn, rather than relying on its contact.

docs.text:
When to use: to give an impact weight on screen: an explosion, a heavy landing, a boss slam. The Shake is a definition of Main Menu → Presentation; Emit At chooses its origin (impact point by default), and the distance from that point to the camera attenuates it, so a far explosion barely shakes. Intensity scales the definition's amplitude for this node. The node is instant and has no effect on gameplay: without a presentation (server, tests), it does nothing.

          └─► [Camera shake] (Heavy, impact point)

When to use: to play an animation that is not already carried by the skill's modules: the caster's cast gesture, a stagger on each target hit, a victory pose. The Animation is a definition of Main Menu → Presentation, played over the entity's Animator Controller, which takes control back when the clip ends. Target animates the caster or each received target; Speed multiplies the definition's speed. A looping animation, or one given a Key, is stopped by a Stop effect with the same key, or at the end of the execution.

The node is instant and has no effect on gameplay: the timing of a hit belongs to the skill (an Attack's phases, a Delay), never to the animation.

When not to use: the animation of an attack is set on the Attack itself, that of a dodge on the Dodge.
