docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to show an effect (particles, flash, decal) that is not already part of a module visual: an explosion at the impact point, a glow on each target healed, a burst on the caster at cast. The effect is a definition of Main Menu → Presentation → Effects; Emit At chooses where it plays: impact point (default), each received target, the received target, the caster, the module body, the aim point or a named object. Attached makes it follow the entity or the body (Bone for a bone of a character); a Key lets a Stop effect node stop a lasting effect.

The node has no effect on gameplay: with the presentation disabled (server, tests), it does nothing and the fight is the same.

When not to use: the trail of a projectile and its impact belong to its module visual (Visual of the Spell body), played by themselves. For a sound, Play sound; for a screen shake, Camera shake.

Example:

[On hit] ─┬─► [Simple damage]
          └─► [Play effect] Explosion, at the impact point

docs.title: Play sound
docs.text: Category Presentation Creation menu Presentation/Play sound Class PlaySoundModel Serialized type {class: PlaySoundModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Sound soundUuid Presentation definition (SoundDefinition) — Sound from the presentation library Emit At (Options) emitAt Anchor: Caster (0), Aim point (1), Received target (2), Each received target (3), Module body (4), Impact point (5), Named object (6) — Where to play the sound: impact point (default), each received target, received target, caster, module body, aim point, named object Attached (Options) attached Boolean no Follows the entity or the module body (no effect on an impact point). Otherwise, stays where it was played Bone (Options) bone Text — Attached to an entity: name of the followed bone (empty or not found = root) Key (Options) key Text — Key of a looping sound, to stop it with “Stop effect” (same execution)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to play a sound that is not already part of a module visual: a cast shout, an impact sound on each target, a loop while a channel lasts. The Sound is a definition of Main Menu → Presentation; Emit At chooses where it plays (impact point by default, each received target, the caster, the module body, the aim point…), one sound per point. Attached makes it follow the entity or the body (Bone for a bone of a character). A looping sound needs a Key so that a Stop effect can stop it; the end of the execution stops the remaining ones.

The node is instant and has no effect on gameplay.

When not to use: the launch, loop, impact and expiration sounds of a module are set once in its Visual (module visual definition).

Example:

[Start] ─┬─► [Beam] (Channeled, Stop On Release) ──Hit targets──► [Simple damage]
         └─► [Play sound] (Beam hum, Caster, Attached, Key “hum”)

docs.title: Stop effect
docs.text: Category Presentation Creation menu Presentation/Stop effect Class StopEffectModel Serialized type {class: StopEffectModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Actions, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Key key Text — Key given to the effects and sounds to stop

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to stop a lasting effect, sound or animation before the end of the skill: the charging aura when the charge is released, the shield glow when the shield breaks, a loop when a channel is interrupted. It stops cleanly (end of emission) everything that a Play effect, Play sound or Play animation started with the same Key in the same execution; the other casts of the skill are not touched. Whatever is still playing stops by itself at the end of the execution.

The node is instant and has no effect on gameplay.

Example:

[Start] ─┬─During cast─► [Play effect] (Charge aura, Caster, Attached, Key “charge”)
         └─► [Stop effect] (“charge”) ─► [Spell body] …

docs.title: Start
docs.text: Category Start Creation menu Start node Class StartNode Serialized type {class: StartNode, ns: UnleashSkill.Execution, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Output Module (0) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 1 During cast

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: No fields.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: every skill has exactly one Start, created with the graph: it is the entry point, run when the skill is cast (after its cast time, if it has one).

  • Module output (blue): the skill's first module (Spell body, Area, Beam, Attack, Summon).
  • Trigger output (green): actions or supports that run at cast, without a module (a self-heal, a Delay, a Repeat, an On event listener of a passive).
  • During cast output: runs at the start of the cast (cast time or charged cast, Skill settings) and stops at its end, released or interrupted. A charging aura, a slowdown while casting. Never run for a skill without a cast.

When not to use: a second entry point is not possible; to run several things at cast, connect several nodes to the same output.

Example:

[Start] ─Module─► [Spell body] ─► [On hit] ─► [Simple damage]
   └─Trigger─► [Heal]  (the caster heals at cast)

docs.title: Blocker
docs.text: Category Support Creation menu Support/Blocker Class BlockerModel Serialized type {class: BlockerModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Supports, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Output Support (3) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Layer Name layerName Text Obstacle Simulation layer of the body. Obstacle: stops skills (default matrix). A custom layer only blocks the layers the matrix makes it block (e.g. an anti-projectile shield). Blocks Enemies blocksEnemies Boolean yes Blocks enemy skills (team different from the wall caster's). Blocks Allies blocksAllies Boolean no Blocks allied skills (same team, or same caster), including those that target allies. Triggers Impact triggersImpact Boolean no A skill stopped by the wall triggers its impact: its OnHit nodes fire their chain at the impact point, without a target. Otherwise, it is destroyed with no effect. Blocks Entities blocksEntities Boolean no Also blocks entity movement (CharacterController, Rigidbody), allies included: Unity collider on the configuration's walls layer (Simulation).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to turn a module into a wall or a shield that stops skills: an ice wall, a wind barrier that eats projectiles, a dome that protects allies. Connected as a support of a module (Spell body), it makes the module's body an obstacle of the simulation, with the shape of the module's Scale box. Blocks Enemies and Blocks Allies say whose skills it stops; Layer Name puts it on another simulation layer when the default Obstacle is too broad (a shield that only stops projectiles). A skill stopped by the wall ends; with Triggers Impact, its On hit nodes run at the impact point first (an arrow that explodes on the wall). Blocks Entities also stops characters from walking through.

The wall lives as long as its module: give the module a lifetime (Max Lifetime).

Example:

[Start] ─► [Spell body] (Aim point, 6 × 3 × 0.5, Max Lifetime 8 s)
                ▲
           [Blocker] (Blocks Enemies, Blocks Entities)

docs.title: Chain
docs.text: Category Support Creation menu Support/Chain Class ChainModel Serialized type {class: ChainModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Supports, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Support (3) 0 — Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Input Selection (4) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Max Chain Count maxChainCount Integer 3 Maximum number of bounces (= of branches) Chain Range chainRange Number 5 Maximum distance between two successive targets Damage Reduction damageReduction Number 0 % damage reduction per bounce (0-100), cumulative: bounce n receives (1 - r)^n (from a target; from the caster, the first bounce is at full). Applied by the damage nodes Can Chain Same Target canChainSameTarget Boolean no Allows a bounce on a target already hit (never on the current target)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Bounces from target to target (chain lightning), one branch per bounce that only contains the bounce's target.

Choose the bounces: connect a Target selection to the “Selection” input. The Chain keeps its own candidates (the entities in range of the previous target); the Selection provides the filters (team, type, status, stat, position) and the sort, applied on each bounce, distances measured from the previous target. Its count is ignored: one bounce = one target. A target already hit is excluded (except with “Can Chain Same Target”). The connected Selection is not executed; its source is not read (“provided by the consumer” is the recommended value).

[Target selection] ──Selection──► (Selection) [Chain] ──► [Damage]
  source: provided by the consumer
  filter: enemies with “Burn”, sort: lowest stat (HP)

Without a connected Selection, a Chain from an old graph keeps its old settings (Nearest / Random / LowestHealth / HighestHealth choice, team filter, health stat), hidden in the editor. The node's “Create the Selection” button creates the equivalent Selection and connects it.

docs.title: Check condition
docs.text: Category Support Creation menu Support/Check condition Class ConditionalCheckModel Serialized type {class: ConditionalCheckModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Supports, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Support (3) 0 — Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 True Output Trigger (1) 1 False

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Check Type checkType Choice: TargetStatPercent (0), CasterStatPercent (1), Distance (2), TargetCount (3), RandomChance (4), TargetHasStatus (5), CasterHasStatus (6), ParentModuleHasStatus (7), Formula (8) TargetStatPercent What is checked. Stat and distance: per target (the targets are split between True and False). Formula: per target if it reads the target Formula formula Formula — Condition true if the formula is non-zero, e.g. Stat(HP, Target, Percent) < 30 and Distance <= 5. Per target if it reads the target (Stat(…, Target), Stacks, Distance), all or nothing otherwise. Shown if Check Type = Formula. Stat statUuid Stat (configuration) — Compared stat, in % of its maximum (TargetStatPercent / CasterStatPercent only). Hidden if Check Type = Formula. Comparison comparison Choice: GreaterThan (0), LessThan (1), EqualTo (2), NotEqualTo (3), GreaterOrEqual (4), LessOrEqual (5) LessThan Operator: measured value [operator] threshold (ignored for RandomChance). Hidden if Check Type = Formula. Threshold threshold Number 50 Threshold: % of the stat, distance in units, number of targets, or chance in % (RandomChance). Hidden if Check Type = Formula. Status statusUuid Status (configuration) — Status looked for (TargetHasStatus / CasterHasStatus / ParentModuleHasStatus only). Hidden if Check Type = Formula. Min Stacks minStacks Integer 1 Minimum stacks of the status (TargetHasStatus / CasterHasStatus / ParentModuleHasStatus only). Hidden if Check Type = Formula.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Switch: each received target goes to True or to False, never both. A branch without a target is not fired.

Formula mode — the condition is written as a formula, with the comparators < > <= >= = != and not, and, or: it is true if the formula is non-zero.

  • If the formula reads the target (Stat(…, Target), Stacks(…), Distance), it is evaluated for each target and the targets are split between True and False.
  • Otherwise, it is evaluated once: all the targets go to True, or all to False.
Need Formula Targets below 30% HP and close Stat(HP, Target, Percent) < 30 and Distance <= 5 At least two summons killed Kills >= 2 Caster below half health or enraged Stat(HP, Caster, Percent) < 50 or Var(Rage) = 1 One chance in four (like Chance) Random() < 25

Several Check conditions in a cascade (False output → next Check condition) make a multi-step switch: Kills >= 3, then Kills >= 2, then the rest.

docs.title: Delay
docs.text: Category Support Creation menu Support/Delay Class DelayModel Serialized type {class: DelayModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Supports, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Support (3) 0 — Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Delay Duration delayDuration Number 1 Delay in seconds before firing the outputs (0 = immediate). Turn-based: in turns, rounded up to the next turn. Use Random Delay useRandomDelay Boolean no Rolls the delay randomly between Min Delay and Max Delay, on each pass Min Delay minDelay Number 0.5 Minimum delay in seconds (random delay). Turn-based: in turns, rounded up to the next turn. Max Delay maxDelay Number 2 Maximum delay in seconds (random delay). Turn-based: in turns, rounded up to the next turn.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to wait before what follows: an explosion one second after the impact, a second strike, a meteor that falls after a warning. Placed on a trigger chain, the Delay receives its parent's targets and aim, waits Delay Duration (or a random delay between Min Delay and Max Delay), then runs its outputs with them. Its time follows the caster's (slowdowns and time zones included); in turn-based mode, it is counted in the caster's turns.

Several delays of the same node can run at once (a Repeat in front of a Delay): each one has its own countdown.

When not to use: to do the same thing several times at an interval, use Repeat. For a status that acts over time (damage every second), use a status with a Periodic behavior.

Example:

[On hit] ─┬─► [Simple damage]  impact
          └─► [Delay] 1 s ─► [Area] radius 3 ─► [Simple damage]  delayed explosion

docs.title: Fork
docs.text: Category Support Creation menu Support/Fork Class ForkModel Serialized type {class: ForkModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Supports, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Support (3) 0 — Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Input Selection (4) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Fork Count forkCount Integer 3 Maximum number of branches Pattern pattern Choice: Spread (0), Circle (1), Targeted (2), Random (3) Spread Targeted: one branch per target, nothing without a target. Random: targets picked at random. Spread: branches in a fan, Circle: branches spread over 360° (branch direction, read by the modules and the Movement) Spread Angle spreadAngle Number 45 Total angle of the fan in degrees (Spread), between the two outermost branches, centered on the Fork's direction. Shown if Pattern = Spread. Random Angle randomAngle Number 0 Random deviation in degrees: the direction of each branch turns by a random angle between -value and +value, rolled by the execution (0 = none). Only affects the branch directions written by the Fork (Spread, Circle, Orientation of a position pattern) Direction direction Direction: Toward the aim point (0), Caster forward (1), Toward the received target (2), Random (4) — Direction of the Fork, from the caster: axis of the fan (Spread), start of the circle (Circle), forward of the position patterns; a branch direction (Fork behind a Fork) takes precedence Damage Multiplier damageMultiplier Number 1 Damage multiplier of each branch (combined with the Fork's own branch multiplier), applied by the damage nodes Position Pattern positionPattern Choice: None (0), Circle (1), Arc (2), Line (3), Grid (4), RandomInDisk (5), RandomInRing (6), RandomInParentShape (7), OnTargets (8) None Spawn point of each branch (read by the branch's first module instead of its anchor). None: no point, direction only Center center Anchor: Caster (0), Aim point (1), Received target (2), Module body (4), Impact point (5), Named object (6) — Center of the pattern: caster, aim point, received target, module body, impact point or named object. Falls back to the caster. Hidden if Position Pattern = None or OnTargets. Radius radius Dynamic value 3 Radius (Circle, Arc, RandomInDisk, outer radius of RandomInRing). Shown if Position Pattern = Circle or Arc or RandomInDisk or RandomInRing or RandomInParentShape. Inner Radius innerRadius Dynamic value 1 Inner radius (RandomInRing). Shown if Position Pattern = RandomInRing. Arc Angle arcAngle Dynamic value 90 Opening of the arc in degrees (Arc), between the two outermost branches. Shown if Position Pattern = Arc. Spacing spacing Dynamic value 2 Spacing between two points (Line, Grid). Shown if Position Pattern = Line or Grid. Grid Columns gridColumns Integer 3 Number of columns of the grid, across the direction (Grid); the rows follow the direction. Shown if Position Pattern = Grid. Random Offset randomOffset Dynamic value 0 Random jitter: each point is shifted randomly within a disk of this radius (0 = none). Hidden if Position Pattern = None. Orientation orientation Choice: KeepDirection (0), Outward (1), Inward (2), AimDirection (3) KeepDirection Direction of each placed branch: the direction pattern's (Spread, Circle), outward, toward the center, or the Fork's direction. Hidden if Position Pattern = None. Time Offset timeOffset Dynamic value 0 Offset in seconds between two branches (caster time): branch i starts i × offset after the first one. 0 = all together

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Splits the flow into several branches: one per received target (at most Fork Count), or Fork Count branches without a target (fan, circle, position pattern).

Targeted Fork with a Selection: a Target selection connected to the “Selection” input replaces the received targets with those it keeps (its source: around the caster, the aim point…; “provided by the consumer”: the targets received by the Fork, filtered and sorted). One branch per kept target, capped by Fork Count. An “around” source is a world query: the branches fire at the next tick.

[Start] ──► [Fork: Targeted, 3] ──► [Projectile]
                ▲ (Selection)
[Target selection: around the caster, 10 m, enemies, the closest]

Scattered volley (shotgun): Random Angle turns the direction of each branch by a random angle between −N° and +N°, around the regular direction of the fan (Spread), of the circle (Circle) or of the Orientation of a position pattern. With Spread, 5 branches, Spread Angle 30 and Random Angle 10, each pellet leaves within ± 10° of its place in the fan. The angle is rolled by the execution: the same seed gives the same volley (Skills → Testing a skill). A branch without a direction written by the Fork (Targeted, Random) is not affected.

[Start] ──► [Fork: Spread, 5, Spread Angle 30, Random Angle 10] ──► [Spell body] ──► [Movement]

docs.title: Mark branch
docs.text: Category Support Creation menu Support/Mark branch Class MarkBranchModel Serialized type {class: MarkBranchModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Supports, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Support (3) 0 — Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Mark markUuid Mark (configuration) — Mark applied to the branch (e.g. Critical): read by the damage nodes and the listeners of the following nodes

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Applies a configuration mark (Critical, or a mark declared in the marks panel) to the branch, then fires its outputs, which inherit it. A sibling branch does not see it.

The mark is read by the damage formula (a Roll step whose mark forces success: the Critical mark makes the hit critical) and by the listeners filtered on the mark (hit dealt event).

Chance (25) ──True──► Mark branch (Critical) ──► Simple damage

docs.title: Multiply damage
docs.text: Category Support Creation menu Support/Multiply damage Class MultiplyBranchDamageModel Serialized type {class: MultiplyBranchDamageModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Supports, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Support (3) 0 — Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Factor factor Dynamic value 2 Factor applied to the damage of the following nodes (2 = double, 0.5 = half; negative counted as 0): fixed, or read at cast time (critical damage stat…)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Multiplies the branch's damage multiplier, then fires its outputs, which inherit it: the following damage nodes apply it at the formula's “node and branch multipliers” step. The factors combine with those of Fork and Chain. The factor is evaluated once per pass, for the branch's first target.

Chance (25) ──True──► Multiply damage (2) ──► Simple damage

docs.title: Random choice
docs.text: Category Support Creation menu Support/Random choice Class RandomModel Serialized type {class: RandomModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Supports, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Support (3) 0 — Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 Output 1 Output Trigger (1) 1 Output 2 Output Trigger (1) 2 Output 3 Output Trigger (1) 3 Output 4

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Weight 1 weight1 Dynamic value 1 Weight of output 1 (relative to the other connected outputs) Weight 2 weight2 Dynamic value 1 Weight of output 2 Weight 3 weight3 Dynamic value 1 Weight of output 3 Weight 4 weight4 Dynamic value 1 Weight of output 4

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to run one branch out of several, at random: a staff that casts fire, ice or lightning, a critical voice line one time out of four, a boss that picks one attack. Connect up to four outputs; each pass runs exactly one of them, rolled according to the Weights of the connected outputs (an unconnected output or a weight of 0 is never chosen). Weights are dynamic values, evaluated on each pass: a weight can grow with a stat or a skill variable. The roll uses the execution's random generator, so it is reproducible for a given seed (tests, replays, server).

When not to use: for a single chance of something happening, use Chance; to run every branch, connect the nodes directly; to vary a value, a formula with Random().

Example:

[On hit] ─► [Random choice] ─┬─Output 1 (2)─► [Apply status] (Burn)
                             ├─Output 2 (1)─► [Apply status] (Frozen)
                             └─Output 3 (1)─► [Apply status] (Shock)

docs.title: Repeat
docs.text: Category Support Creation menu Support/Repeat Class RepeatModel Serialized type {class: RepeatModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Supports, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Support (3) 0 — Input Trigger (1) 0 — Input Condition (2) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Mode mode Choice: Fixed (0), Infinite (1), UntilCondition (2) Fixed Fixed: Repeat Count casts. Infinite: until the caster is destroyed or the execution ends. UntilCondition: not supported yet, treated as Fixed Repeat Count repeatCount Integer 3 Total number of output casts (Fixed mode) Delay Between Repeats delayBetweenRepeats Number 0.1 Seconds between two casts (0 = all in the same frame, forbidden in Infinite mode). Turn-based: in whole turns (1 = every turn).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to run the same outputs several times in a row: a volley of arrows, three fireballs one after the other, a pulse every second. Mode Fixed runs them Repeat Count times, Delay Between Repeats apart (0 = all at once); Infinite runs them until the execution ends or the caster disappears (a delay is then required). Each run receives the Repeat's targets and aim, as frozen when it started. In turn-based mode, the interval is a whole number of the caster's turns.

When not to use: for several projectiles at the same moment in different directions (fan, circle), use Fork. For a damage over time on a target, a Periodic status is easier to balance and can be cleansed.

Example:

[Start] ─Trigger─► [Repeat] 3 times, 0.2 s ─► [Spell body] ─► [On hit] ─► [Simple damage]
                                                    ▲
                                               [Movement]

Hidden if Source = SpellsAroundCaster or SpellsAroundTargetPoint or SpellsAroundParentModule or NamedObjects. Distance measured from the source's center (caster for received targets) Sort Stat Kind sortStatKind Choice: Current (0), Max (1), PercentOfMax (2) Current Value of the stat compared by the sort by stat. Hidden if Source = SpellsAroundCaster or SpellsAroundTargetPoint or SpellsAroundParentModule or NamedObjects. Shown if Sort = LowestStat or HighestStat. docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Chooses targets: candidates (the source), filters, a sort and a count.

Two uses of the same node:

  • In the flow: it runs and fires the “Targets” output (one branch, or one per target) or “No target”.
  • As configuration: its “Selection” output connected to another node's “Selection” input (Chain, Fork, Area, Summon). The node is then never executed and its flow ports are ignored: the consumer reads its settings and applies them itself. The same Selection can configure several nodes.
Consumer Candidates Settings used Chain its own: in range of the previous target filters and sort on each bounce; count ignored Fork those of the source (“provided by the consumer”: the received targets) all; one branch per target, capped by Fork Count Area the entities in the area, on each activation filters, sort, count (“the 3 most wounded”) Summon those of the source reserved for the AttackEnemies behavior (not implemented yet)

The “provided by the consumer” source (ProvidedByConsumer) is the recommended value as configuration; in the flow, it behaves like “received targets”.

docs.title: Aim
docs.text: Category Support Creation menu Support/Aim Class TargetingModel Serialized type {class: TargetingModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Supports, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Module (0) 0 — Input Trigger (1) 0 — Output Module (0) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Mode mode Choice: Immediate (0), HoldRelease (1), PressConfirm (2) HoldRelease Immediate: the aim point is taken right away. HoldRelease: preview while the key is held, cast on release. PressConfirm: preview after the press, click (or press again) to cast, right-click to cancel. Without a key (code, AI), the aim confirms on the first tick Max Range maxRange Number 10 Maximum range of the aim point around the caster, in the play plane (0 = unlimited). A farther point is brought back to this distance Preview Color previewColor Color — Preview color. Hidden if Mode = Immediate. Preview Effect previewEffectUuid Presentation definition (EffectDefinition) — Library effect displayed instead of the default outline, scaled to the shape's radius (optional). Hidden if Mode = Immediate. Show Range showRange Boolean yes Also shows the range circle around the caster (Max Range > 0). Hidden if Mode = Immediate.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to let the player choose where the skill lands before it fires: a meteor on a circle that follows the mouse, a wall placed by click, a blink to a chosen point. Placed between the Start and a module (Area, Beam, Spell body), it shows a preview that reads the shape of the next module, follows the live aim brought within Max Range, then, on confirmation, sets the aim point of its branch and runs its outputs: the module, anchored at the aim point, appears there.

  • Mode HoldRelease: preview while the key is held, cast on release. PressConfirm: preview after the press, click (or press again) to cast, right-click to cancel. Immediate: no preview, the aim frozen at cast is only brought within range.
  • Canceled (right-click, execution canceled), the node ends without outputs: the cost is refunded and the cooldown reset.

A skill cast without a key (from code, by an AI) confirms on the first tick. The preview is local presentation and has no effect on gameplay.

When not to use: a skill that simply fires toward the cursor needs no Aim: every node already reads the aim frozen at cast.

Example:

[Start] ─► [Aim] (HoldRelease, 12 m) ─► [Area] (Aim point, 4 m) ──Targets in the area──► [Simple damage]

docs.title: On event
docs.text: Category Trigger Creation menu Trigger/On event Class OnGameEventModel Serialized type {class: OnGameEventModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Triggers, asm: UnleashSkill}
