docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Event eventUuid Event (configuration) — Event listened to (native or custom) Status statusUuid Status (configuration) — Status applied / removed: only this status (None = all) Damage Type damageTypeUuid Damage type (configuration) — Hit, Kill, Death: only this damage type (None = all) Reaction reactionUuid Reaction (configuration) — Hit: only this reaction (None = all hits, damage included) Removal Reason removalReason Choice: Any (0), Expired (1), Removed (2), Replaced (3), Immunity (4), Event (5), Cleared (6), Consumed (7) Any Status removed: only for this reason (consumed by an interception, expired, removed…) Source Role sourceRole Choice: Anyone (0), Me (1), MyAllies (2), MeOrMyAllies (3), MyEnemies (4), MySummons (5) Anyone Role of the event's source, as seen from the caster Subject Role subjectRole Choice: Anyone (0), Me (1), MyAllies (2), MeOrMyAllies (3), MyEnemies (4), MySummons (5) Anyone Role of the event's subject, as seen from the caster Spell spell Choice: Any (0), ThisExecution (1), ThisSpell (2), OtherSpells (3) Any Skill the event comes from: any, this execution, this skill, or another skill Spell Tags spellTagUuids Skill tag (configuration) empty Tags of the source skill: at least one of them (empty = no filter) Required Marks requiredMarkUuids Mark (configuration) empty Marks the source branch must all have (e.g. Critical) Branch Target branchTarget Choice: Subject (0), Source (1) Subject Event target: the event's subject, or its source Duration duration Dynamic value 0 Listening duration in seconds, at the caster's pace. 0 = as long as the execution lives Max Triggers maxTriggers Dynamic value 0 Maximum triggers (0 = unlimited) Cooldown cooldown Dynamic value 0 Internal cooldown in seconds between two triggers (0 = none)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to react to something that happens in the fight, whoever caused it: a hit, a kill, a death, a status applied or removed, a critical hit, or an event of your own (Emit event). It is the base of passives (“when I am hit, I gain a shield”, “each kill restores mana”) and of reactive skills.

The node listens from the moment it runs. Each event that passes its filters runs its outputs in a dedicated branch whose target is the event's subject (the entity hit, the one that died…) or its source (Branch Target), with the event's value (damage dealt, stacks…) readable by a dynamic value. Filters: data of the event (status, damage type, reaction, removal reason), Source Role and Subject Role seen from the caster (me, my allies, my enemies, my summons), the skill it comes from, its tags, and the marks of its branch (Critical).

It listens for Duration (0 = as long as the execution lives: the whole life of a passive), at most Max Triggers times, with an internal Cooldown. An event it produces itself does not trigger it again (no loop).

When not to use: to act on what one module of this skill touches, use On hit, simpler and tied to the module. To react to the value of a stat (health under 30%), use Stat listener.

Example (passive: each enemy killed by the caster gives 10 mana back):

[Start] ─Trigger─► [On event] Kill, source: Me ─► [Heal] Mana 10, recipient: caster

docs.title: Stat listener
docs.text: Category Trigger Creation menu Trigger/Stat listener Class StatListenerModel Serialized type {class: StatListenerModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Triggers, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Stat statUuid Stat (configuration) — Stat to watch Listened Event listenedEvent Choice: OnChange (0), OnDecrease (1), OnIncrease (2), OnReachZero (3), OnReachMax (4), OnCrossBelow (5), OnCrossAbove (6) OnDecrease Change that triggers the listener Subject subject Choice: Caster (0), ReceivedTargets (1) Caster Watched entities: the caster, or the targets received at start Threshold threshold Number 0 Threshold for OnCrossBelow / OnCrossAbove Threshold Is Percentage thresholdIsPercentage Boolean no The threshold is a percentage of the stat's maximum Duration duration Number 0 Listening duration in seconds. 0 = as long as a watched entity exists Trigger Once triggerOnce Boolean no Ends after the first trigger

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to react to a stat changing, usually in a passive: a shield when the caster's health goes below 30%, a rage burst when mana reaches 0, a counter each time health drops. It watches the Stat of the caster or of each received target (Subject) and runs its outputs on each matching change (Listened Event: any change, decrease, increase, reaching 0 or the maximum, crossing a Threshold downward or upward), in a branch whose only target is the entity whose stat changed.

It ends when its Duration elapses (0 = as long as a watched entity lives), when no watched entity remains, or after the first trigger with Trigger Once. On the caster with a duration of 0, the skill lasts as long as the caster lives.

When not to use: to react to a hit, a death or a status, use On event, which carries the event's value and its source; to test a stat once, Stat condition.

Example (passive slot):

[Start] ─► [Stat listener] (Health, OnCrossBelow 30%, Caster) ─► [Apply status] (Shield, Caster)

docs.title: Timer
docs.text: Category Trigger Creation menu Trigger/Timer Class TimerTriggerModel Serialized type {class: TimerTriggerModel, ns: UnleashSkill.Nodes.Triggers, asm: UnleashSkill}

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Direction Type (portType) Rank (portRank) Label Input Trigger (1) 0 — Output Trigger (1) 0 —

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Serialized name Type Default Description Interval interval Number 1 Interval between two triggers, in seconds (> 0). Turn-based: in whole turns (1 = every turn). Total Duration totalDuration Number 5 Total duration in seconds. 0 = infinite: the timer runs until the caster is destroyed or the execution ends. Turn-based: in turns, rounded up to the next turn. Fire Immediately fireImmediately Boolean no Triggers a first time right at start, without waiting for the first interval

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
When to use: to run nodes at a regular rhythm for a while, independently of any module: a passive aura that heals nearby allies every second, a storm that strikes a random enemy every 0.5 s for 5 s, a channel that pulses. It runs its outputs every Interval seconds during Total Duration (0 = until the execution ends), with a first run right away if Fire Immediately is checked. Any nodes can follow. In turn-based mode, the interval and the duration are counted in the caster's turns.

When not to use: for a rhythm tied to a moving module (at its position, as long as it exists), use On tick; for damage over time on a target, a status (Apply status); to run a branch a fixed number of times in a row, Repeat.

Example:

[Start] ─► [Timer] (1 s, 0, Fire Immediately) ─► [Target selection] (AroundCaster, Ally, 6 m, Count 0) ──Targets──► [Heal] (10)

A permanent aura: an Area has no unlimited duration (Duration 0 is an instant area, a single detection; a negative duration is brought back to 0). For an aura that lasts as long as the skill, put the rhythm in a Timer with Total Duration 0, and an instant Area after it: each run of the Timer is one detection, with the Area's shape, visual and listeners. Without the Area (no shape or listener needed), a Target selection is enough, as in the example above.

[Start] ─► [Timer] (0.1 s, 0, Fire Immediately) ─► [Area] (Circle 3 m, Anchor Caster, Duration 0) ──Targets in the area──► [Damage] (5)

docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
Beyond its graph, a skill has its own settings (cooldown, cost, cast time, tags), and is stored in a caster's slots.

Page Contents Skill settings Cooldown, cost, fixed or charged cast, interruption, tags, variables, named objects Slots, passives and combos SkillSlots, passives, combos, slot replacement Testing a skill Preview in the editor, test scene, automated tests

docs.title: Skill settings
docs.text: In the graph editor, Skill settings shows the skill's settings in the inspector (you can also select the asset). At 0, a skill is cast without cooldown, without cost and without cast time.

docs.title: Cooldown and cost
docs.text:
Setting Role Cooldown Delay before the skill can be cast again, per caster. In seconds in real time, in turns in turn-based mode. Cost stat Caster stat consumed on cast (mana, energy…). Empty: no cost. Cost Amount Amount taken. The skill is refused if the caster has less.

The cost is taken and the cooldown starts at cast, before the cast time. An interrupted cast or a canceled aim refunds the cost and resets the cooldown.

Real cadence. In real time, the cooldown is counted on the world tick, at the caster's step (its time scale and hitstop slow it down), and ends on the first tick that reaches its duration: it is rounded up to a whole number of ticks. A skill cast again as soon as it is ready (continuous fire) fires every ceil(Cooldown × Ticks per second) ticks, that is Ticks per second / ceil(Cooldown × Ticks per second) casts per second. At 60 ticks per second, a cooldown of 0.125 s (7.5 ticks) ends on the 8th tick: 7.5 casts per second, not 8.

A cadence is exact when the cooldown is a whole number of ticks. At 60 ticks per second (Simulation, Ticks per second):

Cooldown Ticks Casts per second 1/60 s (0.0167) 1 60 1/30 s (0.0333) 2 30 0.05 s 3 20 1/15 s (0.0667) 4 15 1/12 s (0.0833) 5 12 0.1 s 6 10 0.1167 s 7 8.57 0.1333 s 8 7.5 0.15 s 9 6.67 1/6 s (0.1667) 10 6 0.2 s 12 5 0.25 s 15 4

For 8 casts per second, raise Ticks per second to a multiple of 8 (at 120 ticks per second, 0.125 s is 15 ticks). In turn-based mode, the cooldown is counted in the caster's turns (AdvanceTurn).

docs.title: Cast time
docs.text:
Setting Role Cast Time Cast time before the release: in seconds in real time, in turns in turn-based mode (the skill fires on the caster's AdvanceTurn() that reaches it, rounded up to the next turn). 0: immediate. Cast Mode Fixed: the skill fires after the cast time. Charged: the player holds the key, the skill fires on release; the cast time is the maximum charge. Charge Min Time (Charged) Minimum time (seconds, or turns in turn-based mode) before the release casts the skill. Released earlier, the cast continues until this time. A cast without a key (code, AI) fires at this time. Charge Release At Max (Charged) The skill fires on its own at maximum charge. Unchecked: the charge stays at maximum until release. Cast Interruption Interrupts the cast: never, when the caster's actions are locked (stun), or on any hit taken.

During the cast, the Start's During cast output is active (charge visual, slowdown). The charge ratio is read with the Charge dynamic value: “the longer you charge, the more it hurts”.

A charged skill is cast with PressSlot / ReleaseSlot (see Cast a skill from code).

docs.title: Skill lifetime
docs.text:
Cancel On Caster Death (checked by default): the skill stops when its caster dies or is disabled. Uncheck it for a skill that must outlive them: a projectile already fired, an area placed on the ground.

Override Turn Wait (turn-based): replaces, for this skill, the configuration's Turn wait (General settings) with its own Turn Wait: Presentation (the next turn waits for the end of its logic and of its effects), Execution (the end of its logic) or None. See Cast from code.

docs.title: Tags, variables, named objects
docs.text: Setting Role Skill tags Skill tags: carried by the skill's events and hits, read by listeners, status immunities and locks, Replace slot and Modify cooldown. Variables Name and initial value, reset on each cast. Written by Store value, read by dynamic values. Object Names Names under which a module registers with its caster (named reference). Another skill finds them: teleport to the thrown hammer, recall the sword.

docs.title: Slots
docs.text:
The SkillSlots component, on the caster, holds its slots in key order. Each slot has:

Setting Role Skill Skill cast by the slot. Combo Combo cast by the slot, takes priority over the skill when it has steps. Passive Passive slot (see below).

The game casts a slot with CastSlot, or PressSlot / ReleaseSlot for a key (see Cast a skill from code).

docs.title: Passives
docs.text:
A passive slot casts its skill when the caster is enabled, without cost or cooldown, and casts it again when the caster respawns. It is never cast by hand. A passive is often a listener:

[Start] ─► [On event]  Kill · source = me
              └─► [Heal]  10% of the caster's max HP

The Set passive node disables or enables a passive from another skill; code can do the same with SetPassiveEnabled(slot, enabled).

docs.title: Combos
docs.text:
A combo (ComboDefinition, Create → UnleashSkill → Combo) chains several skills on the same key: hit 1, hit 2, hit 3.

Setting Role Steps Combo steps, in order. Each step has its skill. Window Start Opening of the chaining window: at the end of the step, or at the start of its attack's recovery (melee). Window Ticks Duration of the window, in the caster's ticks. When it closes, the combo goes back to the first step. Input Buffer Ticks Input buffer: a press during the current step is kept for this time, and casts the next step if the window opens meanwhile. 0: a press during the step is refused.

During a step, a press returns ComboBuffered (buffered) or ComboBusy (ignored).

docs.title: Replace a slot
docs.text:
The Replace slot node temporarily changes what a slot casts: recast of a skill after a kill, shapeshift, special ammunition.

Setting Role Replaced slots By index, the current skill's slot, or by skill tag. Replacement Replacement skill or combo (empty: the slot is cleared). Several pairs in the same node: a shapeshift. End Duration, number of uses, event (caster as source or subject). Toggle Casting the node again removes the current replacement (form on/off). Locked The other slots cannot be cast while the replacement lasts. Free recast The replaced slots are cast without cost, even on cooldown.

Example — recast of Execution after a kill:

[On event] Kill (source = me, this skill)
   └─► [Replace slot] current → Execution · 1 use · 3 s

docs.title: Cooldowns
docs.text: The Modify cooldown node acts on slots or skills (by tag): reset, reduce by N seconds, set a value.

docs.title: Testing a skill
docs.text: Three ways, from the quickest to the most complete.

docs.title: 1. The preview in the editor
docs.text:
Preview button of the graph editor. The skill plays next to the graph, in an isolated scene (a separate simulation world, which does not touch your scene), on a caster and dummies.

Command Effect ⏮ Restart from the beginning ▶ Play / pause ⏭ Advance one tick Speed Slow down or speed up the playback Frame Recenter the camera on the caster and the targets Staging Number, layout and team of the dummies, 2D or 3D plane

The preview restarts on every change to the graph. The world's bodies and searches are shown as an overlay.

The Presentation menu has the same preview for a single definition (effect, sound, animation, module visual).

docs.title: 2. In a scene
docs.text:
Add the SkillTester component on a caster of your scene (see Set up a scene); the Link to scene button of the graph editor puts the open skill in its slot 0. In Play Mode:

  • Space casts slot 0, keys 1 to 9 cast slots 0 to 8;
  • the inspector of the SkillTester has the same commands (Cast skill, one button per slot), plus Reload skill graph, Stop all active skills and, in turn-based mode, Advance turn (one round: the caster, then each registered entity).

Place enemies, allies and walls around the caster to try the skill in the situations of your game.

UnleashSkill → Add Skill Preview to Scene creates a Skill Preview object (SkillPreviewController). Give it a Skill Graph: without playing anything, the Scene view draws the reach of the skill's modules from the object (or from its Caster Transform) and in its forward direction: spawn point of the module bodies, areas, beam range. The inspector chooses what is drawn, and Refresh preview redraws it.

docs.title: 3. Automated tests
docs.text: A skill is plain data: it can be cast without a scene, in an EditMode test of the Unity Test Framework (Window → General → Test Runner), and its effects checked on the targets' stats. The engine pieces such a test relies on (simulation world, entities registered without colliders, execution without presentation) are described in Technical → Simulation world and Cast cycle.

docs.title: A complete test
docs.text:
The skill tested here, Firebolt, is a Spell body (Movement: forward, 10 m/s) whose On hit (enemy, 1 target) deals 10 damage to the health stat with a Simple damage. The test assembly (.asmdef of your EditMode tests) references UnleashSkill.

using System.Collections.Generic;
using NUnit.Framework;
using UnityEditor;
using UnityEngine;
using UnleashSkill;
using UnleashSkill.Configuration;
using UnleashSkill.Execution;
using UnleashSkill.PersistentDataModel;
using UnleashSkill.Simulation;
using UnleashSkill.SkillUtils;

public class FireboltTests
{
    const string Health = "health";
    const string Template = "test-template";

    SkillWorld world;
    UnleashSkillConfiguration previousConfiguration;
    readonly List<Object> created = new List<Object>();
    readonly List<SkillTarget> entities = new List<SkillTarget>();

    [SetUp]
    public void SetUp()
    {
        // 1. A world of its own, without scenery (a wall: World.AddBody on the Obstacle layer)
        world = new SkillWorld(new SimulationSettings { SceneryBackend = StaticSceneryBackend.None });
        UnleashSkillManager.ResetWorld(world);

        // 2. Active configuration: the stats and the stat template of the entities
        var configuration = Track(ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<UnleashSkillConfiguration>());
        var health = Track(ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<StatAsset>());
        health.Initialize(new CustomStat { uuid = Health, statsName = "Health", hasMaximumValue = true });
        configuration.StatAssets.Add(health);
        var template = new StatTemplate { uuid = Template, templateName = "Test" };
        template.floatStats[Health] = new StatInGame<float>
            { customStatUuid = Health, value = 100f, maxValue = 100f, originalValue = 100f };
        configuration.StatTemplates.Add(template);
        previousConfiguration = ConfigurationManager.ActiveConfiguration;
        ConfigurationManager.ActiveConfiguration = configuration;

        // 3. Pooler of the module bodies: in EditMode, AddComponent does not call Awake
        Track(new GameObject("SkillPooler")).AddComponent<SkillPooler>().Init();
    }

    [TearDown]
    public void TearDown()
    {
        foreach (SkillExecution execution in new List<SkillExecution>(UnleashSkillManager.ActiveSkillExecutions))
        {
            if (!execution.IsCompleted)
                execution.Cancel();
            execution.Cleanup();
            UnleashSkillManager.UnregisterActiveSkillExecution(execution);
        }
        foreach (SkillTarget entity in entities)
        {
            SkillEntityRegistry.Unregister(entity);
            entity.Stats?.StopRegeneration();
        }
        entities.Clear();
        foreach (Object obj in created)
            if (obj != null)
                Object.DestroyImmediate(obj);
        created.Clear();
        ConfigurationManager.ActiveConfiguration = previousConfiguration;
        UnleashSkillManager.ResetWorld(null);
    }

    [Test]
    public void Firebolt_HitsTheEnemyAhead_Deals10Damage()
    {
        SkillCaster caster = CreateEntity("players", Vector3.zero);           // faces +Z
        SkillCaster enemy = CreateEntity("monsters", new Vector3(0f, 0f, 5f));
        var skill = AssetDatabase.LoadAssetAtPath<SkillGraphModel>("Assets/Skills/Firebolt.asset");

        Assert.AreEqual(SkillCastResult.Success, caster.Cast(skill, out SkillExecution execution));
        RunUntilCompleted(execution);

        Assert.AreEqual(90f, enemy.Stats.GetStatValue(Health));
    }

    // Entity without a scene: Start and OnEnable do not run in EditMode
    SkillCaster CreateEntity(string team, Vector3 position)
    {
        var gameObject = Track(new GameObject(team));
        gameObject.transform.position = position;
        var entity = gameObject.AddComponent<SkillCaster>();
        entity.teamUuid = team;
        entity.ResetStats(Template);
        SkillEntityRegistry.Register(entity);
        entities.Add(entity);
        return entity;
    }

    // Without the manager's Update: the world advances one tick, then the execution does its frame
    void RunUntilCompleted(SkillExecution execution, int maxTicks = 1000)
    {
        for (int tick = 0; tick < maxTicks && !execution.IsCompleted; tick++)
        {
            world.Step();
            execution.Update();
        }
        Assert.IsTrue(execution.IsCompleted, "The execution did not end");
        UnleashSkillManager.UnregisterActiveSkillExecution(execution);
    }

    T Track<T>(T obj) where T : Object
    {
        created.Add(obj);
        return obj;
    }
}

What each step does:

  • World: UnleashSkillManager.ResetWorld(world) makes it the world of the engine. Without scenery (StaticSceneryBackend.None), the colliders of the open scene are not read.
  • Configuration: the entities read their stats in the active configuration: one built by the test, as here, or your project's (AssetDatabase.LoadAssetAtPath<UnleashSkillConfiguration>). Without teams in the configuration, two different teamUuid are enemies.
  • Pooler: a module (Spell body, Area, Beam…) takes its object from the SkillPooler. In a scene, the UnleashSkillManager creates it; in a test, create it and call Init(). Without a pooler, the module logs an error and ends without its outputs.
  • Entities: Start and OnEnable do not run in EditMode. ResetStats(template) gives the stats, SkillEntityRegistry.Register adds the entity to the world. Without a collider, an entity is a capsule of 0.5 m radius and 2 m height.
  • Ticks: each world.Step() advances the simulation by one tick (bodies, hits, persistent nodes); execution.Update() then detects the end of the execution, as the manager does every frame.
  • Cleanup: between two tests, cancel the executions, remove the entities from the registry, destroy the objects, give back the configuration and the world. The statuses, cooldowns and regenerations started by a test stay tracked by the engine until they end: to isolate each test completely, or to test while a game runs in Play Mode, cast the skill in a SimulationSandbox (Technical → Static state and preview).

The expected values are best read in the skill's nodes (DamageSimpleModel.Damage…) rather than written in the test: the test follows the tuning of the skill.

docs.title: Reading the module bodies of an execution
docs.text:
To check where the module bodies of a skill go (directions of a Fork, spawn point, speed), read the bodies still running in the execution: each running module has an instance in SkillExecution.ActiveInstances, whose RuntimeData is a GameObjectRuntimeData (UnleashSkill.Nodes.Modules) and whose Body is the simulated body (ModuleBody).

// Fork (Spread, 5 branches over 30°) → Spell body (Movement: forward, 10 m/s)
Assert.AreEqual(SkillCastResult.Success, caster.Cast(skill, out SkillExecution execution));
world.Step();

var angles = new List<float>();
foreach (ActiveNodeInstance instance in execution.ActiveInstances)
{
    if (instance.IsCompleted || !(instance.RuntimeData is GameObjectRuntimeData module) || !module.Body.IsAlive)
        continue;
    Vector3 direction = module.Body.Direction;      // unit vector
    Vector3 position = module.Body.WorldPosition;
    angles.Add(Vector3.SignedAngle(Vector3.forward, direction, Vector3.up));
}
angles.Sort();   // -15, -7.5, 0, 7.5, 15
  • WorldPosition and WorldVelocity (units per second) are the body's position and velocity as Vector3, while it lives (IsAlive). Direction is the direction of its velocity, or the module's orientation when it does not move (area, beam, body not yet moved).
  • Position, Velocity and Rotation are the same values in Unity.Mathematics types (float3, quaternion): an assembly that reads them adds Unity.Mathematics to the references of its .asmdef. The Vector3 accessors need only UnleashSkill.
  • A body exists from the module's start until its end: read it between two world.Step(), before RunUntilCompleted.

To compare the same skill with and without its visual, choose the Visual of a Spell body from code: new GameObjectModel().WithVisual(definition) (or the definition's UUID, null for an invisible body). The definition is looked up in the active presentation library (PresentationLibrary.Active) when the module starts; one created in the test is added with library.Add(definition).

docs.title: Walls and variants of a skill
docs.text:
A wall of the test is a body of the Obstacle layer added to the world. Shape.Box(x, y, z) (half-sizes as float), WorldPosition and WorldRotation (Vector3, Quaternion) need only UnleashSkill in the test assembly. Shape.Box(float3) and the Position / Rotation fields are the same values in Unity.Mathematics types; there is no Shape.Box(Vector3), because an overload next to Box(float3) would require Unity.Mathematics to compile the call.

using UnleashSkill.Simulation.Collision;

// Wall 4 m wide and 0.5 m thick, 3 m in front of the caster, turned by 30°
world.AddBody(new Body
{
    Layer = SimulationLayers.Obstacle,
    Shape = Shape.Box(2f, 2f, 0.25f),   // half-sizes
    WorldPosition = new Vector3(0f, 0f, 3f),
    WorldRotation = Quaternion.Euler(0f, 30f, 0f),
    Active = true
});
  • Whether the wall stops a module body depends on the layer matrix (Skill / Obstacle: Block by default) and on the Blocked By Obstacles of the On hit that listens to the body.
  • A body left without a rotation is not rotated. Shape.WithOffset(x, y, z) moves the shape in the body's frame.

To try a variant of a skill (stopped by obstacles, more targets, re-hit), change a copy of its graph from code, never the asset: WithHitPolicy and WithTargetFilter replace the Hit Policy and the Target Filter of an On hit (UnleashSkill.Nodes.Conditions).

SkillGraphModel blocked = Object.Instantiate(skill);   // the asset stays as it is
var onHit = (OnHitModel) blocked.Nodes.Find(node => node is OnHitModel);
HitPolicy policy = onHit.HitPolicy;
onHit.WithHitPolicy(new HitPolicy(policy.MaxTargets, policy.Rehit, policy.RehitCooldown,
    ObstacleBlocking.Yes, policy.RequireLineOfSight));   // Blocked By Obstacles: Yes

Assert.AreEqual(SkillCastResult.Success, caster.Cast(blocked, out SkillExecution execution));

Destroy the copy at the end of the test (Object.DestroyImmediate, or Track in the complete test above). Other nodes have the same methods for construction from code (AreaModel.WithLineOfSight, GameObjectModel.WithVisual…).

docs.title: Reproducible rolls
docs.text:
The random rolls of an execution come from its own generator (SkillExecution.Random): Chance, Random choice, Check condition by chance, random sort of a Target selection or of a Chain, Fork in a random pattern, Random Angle of a Fork, random Direction, wander of a Movement or a Line segment, random range of a Delay, critical hits, Random() in a formula. By default, its seed comes from the execution's identifier, unique to each cast: two casts roll differently.

To replay the same rolls (a test, a replay), set the seed before the first node, through the cast options:

var options = new SkillCastOptions
{
    InitializeContext = context => context.Execution.SetRandomSeed(42)
};
skill.TryCompute(caster, out SkillExecution execution, options);

Two executions with the same seed, the same graph and the same situation roll the same values. The presentation (camera shakes, effects) does not use this generator.

docs.title: Technical documentation
docs.text:
This tab is for extending UnleashSkill: how the engine is built, where the code lives, which rules hold it together, how to add a node, a status behavior or a presentation backend without breaking anything.

These pages summarize the engine's contracts. In case of disagreement, the code is authoritative: the public API carries XML documentation comments, visible in your IDE.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
1. Architecture: the assemblies, what goes where, what is serialized with the assembly name.
  2. Cast cycle: from TryCompute to the end of the execution.
  3. Writing a node: the most common case, with a complete example.
  4. Extension points: the public API of 1.0 and what a dependent asset can extend.

The other pages are read as needed:

Page Topic Simulation world Tick, bodies, queries, HitPolicy, layers, clock, Burst Diagnose and measure Counters, simulation profile, trace, what lives with the world Presentation Command queue, library, backends, handles Statuses, events, damage Damage pipeline, status behaviors, native events, dynamic values and formulas Static state and preview SimulationSandbox: simulate beside the game, state of an add-on Data Configuration, ConfigurationData, UUIDs, migrations, localization tables

docs.title: Map of the asset
docs.text:
Assets/UnleashSkill/
├── Runtime/          # Assembly UnleashSkill (all platforms): Core/, Execution/, Nodes/, Simulation/, Presentation/,
│                     #   Configuration/, Localization/, Preview/
├── Editor/           # Assembly UnleashSkill.Editor: Graph/ (Node Editor), Windows/, PropertyDrawers/, Localization/…
├── Documentation/    # README, CHANGELOG, offline documentation (PDF)
├── LICENSE.md
└── Third-Party Notices.txt

Your own data (configuration, presentation library, trajectories) lives in the data folder (Project Settings → UnleashSkill, Assets/UnleashSkillData by default), your skills wherever you create them.

docs.title: Assemblies
docs.text:
The whole framework is under Assets/UnleashSkill/, the only folder of the asset.

Assembly Platform Folder Role UnleashSkill All Assets/UnleashSkill/Runtime/ Node models, execution engine, simulation, presentation, configuration, localization UnleashSkill.Editor Editor Assets/UnleashSkill/Editor/ Graph window (GraphView), editor nodes, main menu, inspectors, preview, language preference UnleashSkill.Cinemachine All Runtime/Presentation/Cinemachine/ Shake through Cinemachine, compiled only if the Cinemachine 3 package is present (versionDefines → UNLEASHSKILL_CINEMACHINE, defineConstraints)

Dependencies: UnleashSkill.Editor → UnleashSkill. Required packages: Burst, Mathematics, uGUI. Optional packages, detected by the asmdef's versionDefines: Addressables (UNLEASHSKILL_ADDRESSABLES, SkillGraphLoader), Input System (UNLEASHSKILL_INPUT_SYSTEM, SkillTester), Cinemachine 3 (UNLEASHSKILL_CINEMACHINE, separate assembly). An asmdef reference to a missing package is ignored by Unity: the code that uses it is under its define. No render pipeline required. Your own code references UnleashSkill (and UnleashSkill.Editor for editor code) from its asmdef.

No editor dependency in the runtime: a use of UnityEditor in UnleashSkill is wrapped in #if UNITY_EDITOR.

No hard-coded Assets/... path in the framework: the asset can be moved in the user's project.

  • The interface files (uxml, uss of Editor/UI/) are found by GUID: UnleashSkillEditorAssets. The translation tables (Editor/Localization/*.po) are found through the GUID of their folder (EditorLocalization.TablesFolderGuid).
  • The user's data goes to the data folder, UnleashSkillDataFolder.Path: project setting (Project Settings → UnleashSkill, file ProjectSettings/UnleashSkillSettings.json), Assets/UnleashSkillData by default. The presentation library is in its Presentation/ subfolder (PresentationLibrary.DefaultFolder).

docs.title: Namespaces
docs.text:
Namespaces follow the folders, under the UnleashSkill root:

Folder Namespace Runtime/Core/ UnleashSkill (manager, caster, targets, UnleashSkillVersion, DataFormat); subfolders: UnleashSkill.Conditions, .ListenerData, .PersistentDataModel, .SkillUtils, .Stats, .Utils, .Weapons (SkillPrefab/ stays in UnleashSkill) Runtime/Execution/ UnleashSkill.Execution (NodeModel, SkillGraphModel, SkillExecution, context, NodeType, PortType) Runtime/Nodes/[Category]/ UnleashSkill.Nodes.[Category] (Actions, Behaviors, Conditions, Modules, Supports, Triggers, Utils), plus UnleashSkill.Nodes.Attributes and UnleashSkill.Nodes.Targeting Runtime/Simulation/ UnleashSkill.Simulation (scenery included), UnleashSkill.Simulation.Collision Runtime/Presentation/ UnleashSkill.Presentation (backends and Cinemachine included) Runtime/Configuration/ UnleashSkill.Configuration Runtime/Localization/ UnleashSkill.Localization (Localizer, LocalizationTable, NodeText) Runtime/Preview/ UnleashSkill.Preview Editor/[Folder]/ UnleashSkill.Editor.[Folder]: Graph (window, EditorNode), Graph.Nodes.[Category] (editor nodes), Graph.Ports, Inspectors, Localization, Migration, Presentation, Preview, PropertyDrawers, UI, Windows, Windows.Modern

A type that a model needs (enum, struct) goes in Runtime/, never in Editor/.

In a UnleashSkill.* namespace, a simple name that is also a sibling namespace (Execution, Simulation, Presentation, Localization, Editor…) refers to the namespace: qualify the member (context.Execution) or the type (UnityEditor.Editor). The public API therefore has no type named like a framework namespace, nor like a common UnityEngine type (hence SimulationProfileStage, not SimulationStage). What is public, internal, and the extension points: Extension points.

docs.title: What lives where
docs.text:
Assets/UnleashSkill/Runtime/:

Folder Contents Core/ UnleashSkillManager (global singleton), SkillCaster, SkillTarget, SkillSlots, combos; Stats/ (EntityStats), SkillUtils/ (SkillPooler), SkillPrefab/, Conditions/, Weapons/, PersistentDataModel/ Execution/ NodeModel, SkillGraphModel, SkillExecution, SkillExecutionContext, ValueSource, ValueFormula, StartNode, NodeType, PortType, SkillGraphLoader… Nodes/[Category]/ One model per node: Actions, Behaviors, Conditions, Modules, Supports, Triggers, Utils; Targeting/ (aim, anchors, directions, selection); Attributes/ (NodeInfo, ExposedProperty…) Simulation/ SkillWorld, clock, entities, statuses, damage pipeline, events, SimulationSandbox; Collision/ (core, Burst CollisionKernel); Scenery/ (static scenery: Physics 3D, 2D, none) Presentation/ Commands, library, definitions, PresentationSystem; Backends/: default implementations Configuration/ UnleashSkillConfiguration, ConfigurationManager, ConfigurationData, UnleashSkillDataFolder, configurable definitions (statuses, events, reactions…) Localization/ Interface language: Localizer (current language, Tr), gettext tables, node texts Preview/ Preview (SkillPreviewManager, SkillPreviewEntity), SkillTester

Assets/UnleashSkill/Editor/:

Folder Contents Graph/ Graph window (NodeEditor), NodeGraphView, EditorNode, DefaultEditorNode; Nodes/[Category]/: editor nodes; Ports/ UI/ uxml, uss; UnleashSkillEditorAssets Localization/ Translation tables (fr.po), table loading, Preferences → UnleashSkill page Windows/ Main menu (UnleashSkillMainMenu), configuration panels (Modern/), Project Settings page, default data of a new project (UnleashSkillDefaultData) Presentation/, Preview/, PropertyDrawers/, Inspectors/, Migration/ Presentation editing, preview in the editor, drawers, inspectors (SkillCaster, SkillTester), migration menus

docs.title: Central objects
docs.text: Object Role UnleashSkillManager Scene singleton and static facade: world (World), presentation (Presentation, PresentationCommands), active executions, legacy data SkillGraphModel The skill: nodes, connections ([SerializeReference]), settings (cost, cooldown, cast time, tags). Entry point TryCompute SkillExecution One cast: active instances, randomness (ExecutionRandom), cast time, cancellation SkillExecutionContext One branch of the execution: targets, aim (Aim), branch data, access to shared data SkillAim, SkillAnchor, SkillDirection Aim frozen at cast; single vocabulary of the nodes' positions and directions (Runtime/Nodes/Targeting/) SkillWorld Fixed-step simulation world PresentationSystem Consumes the presentation commands after the simulation Localizer Interface language: English source in the code, other languages from tables, switched without recompiling

docs.title: What is serialized with the assembly name
docs.text:
The name UnleashSkill is written into the data:

  • graphs (skill .asset) store their nodes through [SerializeReference], with type: {class: …, ns: …, asm: UnleashSkill};
  • status behaviors (StatusDefinition.behaviors) are also [SerializeReference].

Consequences:

  • Never rename the UnleashSkill assembly, nor move a serialized type (model, behavior, field struct) to another assembly.
  • Renaming or moving a class serialized by reference (subtype of NodeModel or StatusBehavior): add [MovedFrom(true, sourceNamespace: "…", sourceClassName: "…")] (UnityEngine.Scripting.APIUpdating) with the old name, and never remove it within the same major version.
  • A piece of data whose shape changes goes through the format number (see Data).
  • The rid of the references of a hand-written .asset must fit in a signed int64 (see Data).
  • A node's displayed title and tooltips are not part of its identity: they are translated at display time (NodeText), the class name and field names are what the data stores.

docs.title: Cast cycle
docs.text: User version: Running a skill. Here, the path in the code.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
SkillCaster / SkillSlots / game
        │
        ▼
SkillGraphModel.TryCompute(caster, out execution, options)
        │  CheckCast: valid graph, locks, cooldown, cost
        │  new SkillExecution(graph, caster)       ← root context
        │  PayCost, StartCooldown
        │  UnleashSkillManager.RegisterActiveSkillExecution
        ├── cast time? execution.BeginCast / BeginChargedCast
        │              (Start's “During cast” output, IsCastPhase branch)
        └── otherwise: GameEvents.RaiseSkillCast, then ExecuteNodeAndChain(StartNode)

Each world tick (step 6b)                        Each frame (manager Update)
  ExecutionStepper → execution.Step(clock)         execution.Update()
    cast time, hold                                  node.OnRuntime (visual only)
    node.OnSimulationStep(…, clock)                  AreAllNodesCompleted → IsCompleted
                                                     → execution.Cleanup(), removed

docs.title: Cast: SkillGraphModel.TryCompute
docs.text:
TryCompute(caster, out execution, options) (Runtime/Execution/SkillGraphModel.cs):

  1. CheckCast returns a SkillCastResult: InvalidGraph (not exactly one StartNode, a node whose type no longer exists, or a graph from before the first release; checked before the cost and the cooldown, logged once per skill), ActionLocked, SkillBlocked (status that blocks a tag of the skill), AttackInProgress (attack in a non-cancelable phase), OnCooldown, InsufficientResource. Only Success casts.
  2. A new action cancels the caster's attacks that can still be canceled (AttackCancellation.CancelAttacks).
  3. new SkillExecution(this, caster) creates the execution and its root context. SkillCastOptions.InitializeContext can write to it before release (imposed target, values).
  4. Cost taken and cooldown started at cast, hence at the start of the cast time (refunded if it is canceled: RefundLaunch).
  5. The execution is registered in the manager, then starts: directly, or through the cast time.

SkillCastOptions covers the special cases with its flags (PayCost, CheckCooldown, StartCooldown, CheckLocks, Passive): ForPassive() (passive slot: no cost, no cooldown, no lock), free recast, skill cast by another skill (CastSkillModel). Compute(caster) is a shortcut that ignores the reason for a refusal.

docs.title: Starting a node: the engine never fires the outputs
docs.text:
ExecuteNodeAndChain (private) registers the instance then calls OnStart, nothing else:

var instance = new ActiveNodeInstance(node, null, caster, context);
instance.StartTick = UnleashSkillManager.TickInProgress;
execution.AddActiveInstance(instance);          // before OnStart: an instant node can complete inside it
execution.BeginNodeStart();
try { instance.RuntimeData = node.OnStart(caster, context); }
catch (Exception exception) { execution.Fail(exception, instance); }   // see Errors below
finally { execution.EndNodeStart(); }   // end of the outermost start: deferred actions (SkillExecution.Defer)

Deferred actions serve the instant resolution of turn-based mode: a query on the selection returns its result after the OnStart that queued it, never during it. In turn-based mode, TryCompute ends the execution without waiting for a tick if all its nodes are done (CompleteIfResolved).

The node fires its outputs:

Call (SkillExecution) Effect CompleteNodeInstance(node, caster) Ends the node's most recent instance and fires all its outputs CompleteNodeInstance(node, caster, runtimeData) Same, for the exact instance that carries this runtimeData (several simultaneous instances of the same node) CompleteNodeInstanceWithoutOutputs(node, caster) / (node, runtimeData) Ends without firing: failure, false condition, module whose outputs are listeners ExecuteChainedNodes(node, caster, context) Fires the outputs without ending: a listener, on each event ExecuteChainedNodes(node, caster, context, portType, rank) Fires a single output (true / false of a condition) ExecuteChainedNodes(node, caster, context, filter) Fires the outputs whose port passes the filter (the Start leaves out “During cast”)

A node that does neither blocks the chain: its instance stays active and the execution never ends.

docs.title: Branches: SkillExecutionContext
docs.text:
Each time outputs are fired, each chained node receives sourceContext.CreateBranch():

Copied per branch (the child inherits, sisters do not see each other) Shared by the whole execution (SharedState) Targets Caster, Execution MainSkillPrefab, MainBody SetData / GetData data ImpactPoint, ImpactNormal, Aim StartTime Branch data SetBranchData / GetBranchData

Named branch data: BranchDirection (Fork Spread / Circle, read by modules and the Movement), BranchSpawnPoint, BranchDamageMultiplier (multiplied by Fork, Chain, Multiply damage; applied by the damage nodes), BranchMarks (marks such as “Critical”, applied by Mark branch), IsCastPhase, SpellTargets (targeted skills), the source listeners (listener anti-loop).

Aim (SkillAim, context.Aim): frozen by the execution at cast (end of the cast time included) from caster.PointedTarget, or given by the caller (SkillCastOptions.Aim, SkillExecution.SetAim: AI, code, server). It carries the aim point (Point, null if nothing is aimed at), the direction from the caster toward this point (Direction), the pointed entity (Entity) and the caster's position (Origin). The Aim node (Targeting) replaces the one of its branch (SetAimPoint).

Anchors and directions: a position configured on a node is a SkillAnchor (caster, aim point, received target, each received target, module body, impact point, named object; offset in the aim frame, max range), a direction a SkillDirection (toward the aim point, caster forward, toward the received target, away from the caster, random; branch direction takes priority, angle offset). A single resolution: SkillAnchor.Resolve / TryResolve, SkillDirection.Resolve(caster, context, anchor). The field limits the sources offered with [AnchorSources] / [DirectionSources]. A direction defaults to toward the aim point, for a node created in the editor as for one built from code.

Rules:

  • A node never reads caster.PointedTarget: it reads context.Aim. Only the Aim node and the channeled beam (“Follow the live aim” option) read the mouse again, through SkillAim.Live.
  • A position or a direction configured on a node is a SkillAnchor / SkillDirection, never a new enum.
  • A node reads and filters the targets of its context, never those of another branch.
  • Fire your outputs with the context received (ExecuteChainedNodes(this, caster, context)).
  • An event node adds the event's target to a dedicated branch (context.CreateBranch()), not to its own context (otherwise targets accumulate from one event to the next).
  • A module writes its prefab and its body in its branch (context.MainSkillPrefab, MainBody), which its listeners receive.
  • SetData is for skill variables (Store value) and shared values. Data specific to a branch goes in SetBranchData.

docs.title: During the execution
docs.text:
• World tick (SkillWorld, step 6b): ExecutionStepper calls execution.Step(clock) on each active execution. Step advances the cast time and the hold at the caster's pace, then calls OnSimulationStep on each active instance that did not start during this tick (StartTick). This is where persistent nodes outside modules count.
  • Turn (turn-based, SkillCaster.AdvanceTurn): execution.AdvanceTurn() advances a cast started in turn-based mode by one turn (CastInTurns; the world tick no longer advances it) and fires the skill on the turn that reaches its duration, then calls OnTurnAdvanced on each active instance that did not start during this turn.
  • Module bodies: advanced at step 2 of the tick (OnBodyStep, see Writing a node).
  • Frame (UnleashSkillManager.Update): execution.Update() calls OnRuntime (visual only), then marks the execution completed if all its instances are and it is no longer casting.

docs.title: End of execution
docs.text:
AreAllNodesCompleted(): no active instance. Listeners (On event, On tick), flying modules and persistent nodes keep it alive. A completed execution is cleaned up (Cleanup: OnEnd of the remaining instances, stop of the tracked presentation) and removed in the same Update.

The effects applied to a target (status, burn) live in the target's StatusContainer, not in the execution: the Fireball ends on impact, the burn goes on.

docs.title: Cancellation
docs.text:
SkillExecution.Cancel():

  1. Marks IsCanceled; during the cast time, refunds the cost and resets the cooldown (RefundLaunch), likewise during an aim.
  2. Marks all instances completed, then calls their OnEnd, most recent first (listeners before their module).
  3. Stops the tracked presentation (StopAllPresentation).

After Cancel, a late CompleteNodeInstance or ExecuteChainedNodes (callback) is ignored, and ExecuteNodeAndChain no longer starts anything.

Who cancels:

Call Case SkillCaster.CancelSkill(graph) / UnleashSkillManager.CancelSkillExecutions The game interrupts an aura, a channeling SkillCaster.CancelSlot(slot) Cancellation by slot SkillCaster.CancelSkillsOnDeath() Death or disabling of the caster; spares the skills whose CancelOnCasterDeath is false (passives are always canceled) SkillExecution.Interrupt() Interrupted cast (hit taken, stun depending on InterruptionMode) CancelTargeting() Aim canceled: the Targeting node reads the request (ConsumeTargetingCancel), refunds the cost and ends without outputs (it is not a Cancel)

Hold() / Release() cancel nothing: they change IsHeld, which the nodes that use it read at their step (Beam stopOnRelease, charge).

The effects already applied remain; modules remove their body in their OnEnd.

docs.title: Errors: exceptions and loops
docs.text:
An exception thrown by a node cancels its execution, and only it. The engine catches it around each call into node code: OnStart (in ExecuteNodeAndChain), OnSimulationStep, OnTurnAdvanced and OnRuntime (per instance), a module's body step, impacts and listeners (ModuleBody), the result of a node's query, a deferred action, an On event handler. It then:

  1. logs it (Debug.LogException, with the skill as context);
  2. ends the failing instance without outputs;
  3. cancels the execution (Cancel), which keeps the first exception in SkillExecution.Fault.

The other executions, the rest of the tick (statuses, cooldowns, regeneration, combos, locks, movements, history) and the turn manager go on: TurnReady is still raised, since a canceled execution is completed. An exception thrown by an OnEnd during a cancellation is logged and does not prevent the other instances from ending.

The world isolates its own listeners the same way (IBodyStepListener, IQueryListener, IBodyHitListener, IWorldStepListener): an exception goes to SkillWorld.ExceptionHandler (Debug.LogException by default) and the tick goes on with the next listener. The subscribers of GameEventBus, ExecutionStarted, ExecutionEnded and TurnReady are called one by one: one that throws is logged and the others are still called.

A loop of instant nodes is stopped. A node that starts its outputs during its own OnStart (instant node, Delay of 0, first fire of a Repeat) nests the starts: a loop of such nodes would never end. Beyond SkillGraphModel.MaxStartDepth (256) nested starts, all skills included (Cast skill), the engine logs an error, refuses every start until the outermost one returns, and cancels the executions involved. The flow analysis warns before: W115 on each node of the loop (NodeModel.StartsOutputsDuringStart), and the editor refuses to connect a node to itself.

A node that never completes (it returns no runtimeData without calling CompleteNodeInstance) keeps its execution alive forever: in the editor and in a Development Build, the execution reports it once after SkillExecution.StuckInstanceDelay seconds.

docs.title: Data
docs.text: User version: Configuration.

docs.title: Active configuration
docs.text:
• UnleashSkillConfiguration (Runtime/Configuration/UnleashSkillConfiguration.cs, ScriptableObject) contains everything configurable: stats (StatAssets), damage types, teams, tags, entity types, stat templates, reactions and reaction profiles, branch marks, statuses and categories, custom events, skill tags, simulation settings (Simulation), GameplayMode.
  • ConfigurationManager.ActiveConfiguration (static) is the configuration read by the engine. At runtime, UnleashSkillManager loads its defaultConfiguration on initialization; without it, the active configuration is reset to null (as in a build): no configured data. In the editor, it is the one chosen in the main menu (failing that, the project's: the first configuration of the data folder, otherwise of the project, which also fills the defaultConfiguration of a manager added by hand in the editor: UnleashSkillDefaultData.AssignProjectData, on ObjectFactory.componentWasAdded; not through Reset(), which Unity also calls for an AddComponent from code).
  • Default data (Editor/Windows/UnleashSkillDefaultData.cs): on the first opening of the editor (once per session, not in batch mode), a project without any configuration receives one in the data folder (UnleashSkillConfiguration.asset: teams Player and Enemy, type Character, stats HP, Mana, Attack under Stats/, template Default); without a presentation library, an empty one is created under Presentation/; without a trajectory library, an empty one is created (TrajectoryLibrary.asset). Nothing is overwritten.
  • PresentationLibrary.Active and TrajectoryLibrary.Active (global, shared by all configurations) are assigned by the manager; when null, the editor takes the library of the data folder (UnleashSkillDefaultData.ProjectPresentationLibrary / ProjectTrajectoryLibrary). The build gives these same libraries to the scene managers whose field is empty (UnleashSkillBuildLibraries, IProcessSceneWithReport, built copy only) and warns if the project has none; a manager that starts without a library warns.

docs.title: Skill graphs in a build
docs.text:
• A graph referenced by a serialized field (a SkillGraphModel field of your script, the slots of a SkillCaster) is included in the build by Unity like any referenced asset: nothing to do.
  • A graph looked up by name goes through SkillGraphLoader (SkillGraphLoader.Instance.GetSkillGraph(name), GetAllGraphs()), which loads every graph when it starts:
    • without the Addressables package: the graphs of the Resources folders (Resources.LoadAll), at once;
    • with Addressables installed, the loader switches to the graphs that carry the SkillGraph Addressables label, loaded asynchronously (IsLoaded becomes true at the end). Resources folders are no longer read: installing Addressables in a project that kept its graphs in Resources empties the loader until the graphs are marked Addressable with the SkillGraph label (and the Addressables content built).
  • The configuration and the presentation and trajectory libraries are referenced by the scene's UnleashSkillManager (see above), never loaded by path.

docs.title: Read data: ConfigurationData
docs.text:
Always go through ConfigurationData (Runtime/Configuration/ConfigurationData.cs): GetTeam, GetEntityType, GetStat, GetStats, GetDamageType, GetTag, GetStatTemplate, GetReaction(s), GetBranchMark(s), GetEvent(s) (natives included), GetSkillTag(s), GetStatus(es), GetStatusCategory(ies), GetReactionProfile.

  • The active configuration is the only source: a UUID missing from the configuration returns null.
  • Without an active configuration: null and empty lists, except the code's default values (damage formula, reactions, marks, statuses and categories, native events).
  • The legacy JSON database and UnleashSkillManager.GetDataByUuid are removed.

docs.title: Compare by UUID
docs.text:
Models and data store UUIDs (strings), not references:

  • teams: SkillTarget.TeamUuid, SkillTarget.SameTeam(a, b) (a SkillPrefab has its caster's team);
  • entity types: EntityType.InheritsFrom(typeUuid, wantedUuid, getType) (hierarchy included);
  • resolve the object (Team, EntityType, CustomStat) only to read its properties.

In a model, a UUID field is decorated so that the editor shows a list ([DamageTypeUuid], [GameEventUuid]…, in Runtime/Attributes/). Presentation definitions follow the same rule (UUID of the PresentationLibrary).

Fixed UUIDs: the native events (event-hit…) and a few statuses of a new configuration (StatusDefinition.StunnedUuid = status-stunned, referenced by the Stun reaction) are constants of the code. Never change them.

The names of the code's default data (statuses, categories, reactions, marks, damage formula steps, native events) are in English since 1.0. Data already created in a configuration keeps its names: only new configurations receive the English names.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
The project migrates without breaking existing assets:

  • [Obsolete] on old signatures and old nodes: never deleted while the migration is not complete. Obsolete model classes are hidden from the creation menu, but still open.
  • Migration step: a field whose shape changes is converted by a step of the data format (below), never by a flag stored next to the field: a node built from code or read from JSON (JsonUtility) gets the same values as one loaded from an asset.
  • Renamed serialized field: [FormerlySerializedAs("oldName")] (Unity attribute, not used in the project yet), or keep the old name and migrate on read.
  • Serialized type ([SerializeReference]): do not change its assembly; a changed name or namespace takes a [MovedFrom] (see Architecture).

docs.title: Data format
docs.text:
SkillGraphModel, UnleashSkillConfiguration, PresentationLibrary and TrajectoryLibrary carry a format number (formatVersion, hidden in the inspector; CurrentFormatVersion in the code). An asset created in memory takes the current format.

  • On opening (OnEnable), UpgradeFormat() applies the migration steps one by one up to the code's format (DataFormat.Upgrade), then marks the asset modified: it is rewritten at the next save, or right away through UnleashSkill → Migration → Data format.
  • Format newer than the code (asset from a newer version of UnleashSkill): warning in the console, no migration, never written: every save (Ctrl+S, Save Project, AssetDatabase.SaveAssets) leaves it out, so its unknown fields are kept; the Node Editor shows such a graph disabled (read-only).
  • Skill graph older than SkillGraphModel.MinimumFormatVersion (data from before the first release): error in the console, no migration, no write (DataFormatStatus.Unsupported); the skill cannot be cast (InvalidGraph), and the Node Editor shows it read-only. A configuration or a library of format 0 (saved before the format number existed) has the same fields as format 1: it is loaded and brought to format 1.
  • Node identifiers: a node whose identifier is missing or already used by another node of the graph (two versions of a graph merged) receives a new one on load, with a warning; the connections stay on the first node of that identifier (SkillGraphModel.RepairNodeIds).
  • A step only touches the asset's data (no editor API: it can run during a load) and must stay correct on a new asset (created in memory, then brought to the current format).
Asset Current format SkillGraphModel 2 (oldest format read: 2) UnleashSkillConfiguration, PresentationLibrary, TrajectoryLibrary 1

A new format adds its step to the asset's UpgradeFormat.

Nodes outside an asset. A node has no default specific to the editor: the Node Editor's creation menu, a node built from code (new AreaModel()) and a node read with JsonUtility (missing fields keep the values of the field initializers) are identical. A direction defaults to “toward the aim point”, which falls back to the caster's forward without an aim point.

The version of the asset and of the public API is UnleashSkillVersion (SemVer): Current, ApiVersion, and IsApiCompatible(version) for a dependent asset.

docs.title: Localization tables
docs.text:
The interface texts are not data of the skills: the English text is written in the code, the other languages are gettext files of Editor/Localization/ (fr.po), read by EditorLocalization and registered with Localizer.

  • A msgid is the exact English text of the code (escapes decoded); msgctxt distinguishes two meanings of the same text (event for native event names); msgstr is the translation. A changed English text loses its translation until the table is updated.
  • Formatted texts use {0}, {1} placeholders (TrFormat), kept in the translation.
  • The language is a per-user editor preference (EditorPrefs, key UnleashSkill.Language); in a build, without tables, the texts stay in English.

docs.title: Hand-written assets
docs.text: A skill is a YAML .asset file (Unity's text serialization), which can be written or modified by hand: generation by a tool, merge of two versions. The node reference gives what such a file needs for each node: its serialized type, the type and rank of each port, the serialized name of each field and the numeric value of each choice.

docs.title: A minimal graph
docs.text:
Start → Spell body ← Movement, then Spell body → On hit → Simple damage: a projectile that flies 15 m/s forward and deals 25 damage to the first enemy it hits. Saved as HandWrittenBolt.asset in the project, this file is a complete skill:

Replace your-hp-stat-uuid with the UUID of the stat that takes the damage (HP): the uuid line of its asset, in the Stats/ folder of the data folder.

docs.title: Skeleton of the file
docs.text: Line Value m_Script {fileID: 11500000, guid: b5e95930826c4e2791b143f79d73fdb8, type: 3}: the SkillGraphModel script, found by this GUID (the one of its .meta, identical in every project) m_Name Name of the asset: the name of the file, without .asset m_EditorClassIdentifier Informative (the script is found by m_Script): Unity rewrites it on save, empty is accepted formatVersion 2, required. Without it, the graph is format 0: refused on load (error in the console), never cast (InvalidGraph), shown read-only (see Data format) nodes One - rid: … entry per node, in any order connections The links between the nodes' ports (below) Skill settings cooldown, costStatUuid, costAmount, castTime, castMode, chargeMinTime, chargeReleaseAtMax, castInterruption, cancelOnCasterDeath, overridesTurnWait, turnWait, spellTagUuids, variables, objectNames (see Skill settings): all optional references version: 2, then RefIds: the data of each node

docs.title: Nodes
docs.text:
A node is an entry of references.RefIds, designated by its rid in nodes:

  • rid: an integer unique in the file, which only links nodes to RefIds.
  • type: {class: …, ns: …, asm: UnleashSkill}, written as the Serialized type line of the node's page in the reference. A type that does not exist (typo, add-on removed) is loaded as a missing node: warning in the console, skill refused until the node is fixed or deleted.
  • data.id: identifier of the node, unique in the graph, used by the connections; a GUID by convention. A missing identifier, or one already taken by another node, is replaced on load with a warning (the connections stay on the first node of that identifier).
  • data.position: place in the Node Editor (Rect: serializedVersion: 2, x, y, width, height), with no effect on the cast.
  • The fields: under data, with the Serialized name of the reference's field table (endMode, not End Mode). A choice is written as the number given in parentheses in the Type column (targetFilter: 1 for Enemy), a boolean as 0 or 1, a text without quotes (an empty text: nothing after the colon), a Vector3 as {x: 0, y: 0, z: 0}.

rid below signed int64

Each rid must stay below 9,223,372,036,854,775,807. Use prefixes in 85…, 87…, 88… (19 digits), never 93… or more: the editor crashes on import (StringToIntCheckedSInt32), on every restart, without a clear message. In case of a crash at startup, read %LOCALAPPDATA%/Unity/Editor/Editor.log (“Failed to convert … in file …”).

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
A connection links an output port (outputPort, the node upstream) to an input port (inputPort, the node downstream). Each end gives:

Field Value nodeId data.id of the node hasPortKey 1: without it, the end designates no port portType Type of the port, as a number (table below) portRank Rank of the port among the ports of the same type and the same direction of the node, from 0: the Rank column of the reference (the Start's second Trigger output, During cast, is portType: 1, portRank: 1) portType Type Usage 0 Module Main flow between modules (Start → Spell body) 1 Trigger Starts actions (On hit → Damage) 2 Condition Listeners and conditions of a module (Spell body → On hit) 3 Support Behavior of a module (Movement → Spell body), modifiers 4 Selection Configuration, not flow: Target selection → the node that chooses targets

A connection whose node or port does not exist is not drawn by the Node Editor, which writes Connection ignored in '…' in the console; it stays in the file.

docs.title: Dynamic values, anchors and directions
docs.text:
A field of type Dynamic value (ValueSource) is a block of fields; a fixed value only needs mode: 0 and value:

Field Value mode 0 Fixed, 1 Stat, 2 ExecutionValue, 3 Distance, 4 StatusStacks, 5 EventValue, 6 Formula value Fixed value (mode: 0) holder Stat or stacks read on: 0 Caster, 1 Target statUuid Stat read (mode: 1) statKind 0 Current, 1 Max, 2 PercentOfMax executionValue mode: 2: 0 BranchTargetCount, 1 LastDamageDealt, 2 Variable, 3 StatusStacksRemoved, 4 StatusRemainingDamage, 5 CastElapsed, 6 ChargeRatio, 7 KilledCount, 8 ModuleBlockCount variable Skill variable read (executionValue: 2) distance mode: 3: 0 CasterToTarget, 1 CasterToImpactPoint, 2 ImpactPointToTarget statusUuid Status whose stacks are read (mode: 4) formula Expression (mode: 6), for example 0.5 * LastDamage + Stat(Strength) multiplier, add Applied to the raw value: value × multiplier + add (1 and 0 by default) useMin, min, useMax, max Clamping, if useMin / useMax is 1

A field of type Anchor (SkillAnchor) has source (the number in parentheses in the reference), objectName (named object), offset (Vector3) and maxRange (aim point). A field of type Direction (SkillDirection) has source, followBranchDirection (1 by default: a Fork's branch direction wins), angleOffset (degrees) and random3D. Another structure (for example HitPolicy) lists its serialized names in the Type column of the reference.

docs.title: Missing fields
docs.text: A field missing from the file keeps the value of its initializer in the code, the Default column of the reference: in a node ([SerializeReference]), in a structure of a node (a dynamic value written with only mode and value keeps multiplier: 1), and in the skill settings. The example above relies on it: the Movement keeps its 50 m range, On hit its single target.

docs.title: Check a hand-written graph
docs.text:
1. Open the skill in the Node Editor: every connection must be drawn (otherwise, read the Connection ignored warning in the console), and no node must carry the “!” badge of the graph analysis (a node that reads what it will never receive).
  2. Cast it in the editor preview, or in a test (see Testing a skill).
  3. When Unity saves the asset again (after a change in the Node Editor), it writes it in its complete form, every field included.

docs.title: Diagnose and measure
docs.text: What a game can read at runtime to display counters, measure the simulation or find out why a skill missed. Everything here is read-only and costs nothing while it is not used.

docs.title: Counters
Profile of the simulation
docs.text:
UnleashSkillManager.World.Profile (SimulationProfile) records the time of each step of a tick. Disabled by default: no measurement, zero cost.

Member Meaning Enabled Measures the following ticks Samples Ticks measured since the last Reset() AverageTickMs Average time of a tick (all steps), in milliseconds WorstTickMs Worst measured tick, in milliseconds AverageMs(stage) Average time of one step per tick (SimulationProfileStage: Snapshot, Step, Advance, Grid, Collision, Sort, Scenery, Resolve, Dispatch, Movement, History) Hits Impacts distributed to the bodies Queries Queries executed (sweeps and one-shot queries) GridBodies Bodies inserted into the grid, accumulated over the measured ticks Reset() Starts the measurements over 
SimulationProfile profile = UnleashSkillManager.World.Profile;
profile.Enabled = true;
// … a few seconds later
Debug.Log($"{profile.AverageTickMs:0.000} ms per tick, worst {profile.WorstTickMs:0.000} ms over {profile.Samples} ticks");
profile.Reset();

The time is measured with System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch: it works in a build, without the Unity Profiler.

docs.title: Cost of a refused cast
docs.text: A game can try to cast every frame while a key is held (SkillCaster.Cast, SkillGraphModel.TryCompute), or check with CanCast / CheckCast. A refused cast (actions locked, skill blocked, attack in progress, cooldown, cost) reads only the caster's own state: its locks, its statuses, its running attacks and dodges (indexed by caster), its cooldowns and its stats. Its cost does not grow with the active executions of the other casters; nothing is created nor paid.

docs.title: Trace and warnings
docs.text:
With SimulationSettings.Debug on, the world:

  • writes a trace in World.Trace (SimulationTrace, circular buffer of TraceCapacity entries): Count, trace[i] (TraceEntry: Tick, Kind — sweep, query, impact, rejected, truncated, dropped ticks —, Rule that discarded a candidate, Source, QuerySerial, Target, Count), Clear();
  • sends warnings (dropped ticks, truncated results) to World.WarningHandler, or to Debug.LogWarning if it is null;
  • draws the gizmos chosen in SimulationSettings.Gizmos in the Scene view (bodies, last queries, sweeps, impacts).

docs.title: Where to change a setting
docs.text:
The world created by UnleashSkillManager.World works on a copy of the configuration's settings (SimulationSettings.Clone()):

  • For the current game: UnleashSkillManager.World.Settings.Debug = true (or Gizmos, or any other setting read at runtime). The configuration asset is never modified, even in the editor.
  • For good: in the configuration (Simulation settings, or UnleashSkillConfiguration.Simulation from code), then UnleashSkillManager.ResetWorld() to apply it to a running game. Settings read when the world is created (tick rate, cell size, plane, scenery, history depth, trace capacity) only change this way.

docs.title: What lives with the world
docs.text:
The profile, the trace, DroppedTicks, the tick count and the bus of events belong to the world. UnleashSkillManager.ResetWorld() (new game) replaces the world:

  • the profile of the new world is enabled if the replaced one's was; its measurements start over;
  • Debug and Gizmos changed from code on the replaced world are kept; the other settings come back from the configuration (a value changed in the configuration before the call wins);
  • the trace, DroppedTicks and the tick count start empty.

ResetWorld(world) uses the given world and its settings as they are; only its profile is enabled if the replaced world's was. To follow the world from a diagnostics panel, subscribe to UnleashSkillManager.WorldChanged (Extension points).

docs.title: Without the manager
docs.text: In a SimulationSandbox or an Edit Mode test, UnleashSkillManager.Update does not run: a completed execution stays in ActiveSkillExecutions (and in SimulationSandbox.Executions). Count only the executions still running (!execution.IsCompleted), or remove the completed ones with UnleashSkillManager.UnregisterActiveSkillExecution(execution). SimulationSandbox.Dispose() removes them all (Static state and preview).

docs.title: Extension points and public API
docs.text: Contract of 1.0 with dependent assets (Server, AI, user add-ons): what they can use without modifying a file of Assets/UnleashSkill/.

docs.title: Version and compatibility
docs.text:
• UnleashSkillVersion.Current (1.0.0) is the asset's version; UnleashSkillVersion.ApiVersion (major.minor) the API's.
  • A dependent asset declares the API it requires and checks it on load ([InitializeOnLoad] or first use):
static readonly System.Version RequiredApi = new System.Version(1, 0);

if (!UnleashSkillVersion.IsApiCompatible(RequiredApi))
    Debug.LogError($"This add-on requires UnleashSkill API {RequiredApi}, installed: {UnleashSkillVersion.Text}");
  • IsApiCompatible: same major, installed minor at least equal. SemVer: a minor only adds compatible things; a break of the public API waits for the next major.
  • The data format (formatVersion of graphs, configuration, library) is independent from the API version (see Data).

docs.title: What is public
docs.text:
Every public or protected type and member of the UnleashSkill and UnleashSkill.Editor assemblies is part of the API and follows SemVer. The extension points below are those designed to be extended; the rest of the public API is meant to be used, with no guarantee that it is made to be overridden.

What is not part of it:

Element Visibility Why Old choice of the Chain's next target (ChainTargetSelection) internal, [Obsolete] Only read without a connected Target selection Runtime state of the nodes (*RuntimeData, except GameObjectRuntimeData) and the world steppers of statuses, cooldowns, locks, combos and regeneration internal State of a running node: an implementation detail. A step listener added twice would advance the statuses twice The editor's windows, panels, inspectors, property drawers and editor nodes internal Only the editor extension points below are public Any internal member — Implementation detail, can change with each version

[assembly: InternalsVisibleTo] (Runtime/AssemblyInfo.cs, Editor/AssemblyInfo.cs) only opens to the framework's own tests, never to a dependent asset. A public [Obsolete] no longer exists at 1.0: a signature replaced after 1.0 stays [Obsolete] for at least one minor version, then is removed in the next major version.

docs.title: Naming decisions of 1.0
docs.text:
• Data definitions keep their lowercase public fields (StatusDefinition.statusName, CustomStat.uuid, StatusDefinition.maxStacks…). They are Unity serialized fields, read by name by the inspectors and written in the assets: renaming them would break both the API and the data. They stay as they are for the whole 1.x line.
  • Skill, not spell: a graph is a skill (SkillCastResult.SkillBlocked, GameEvents.RaiseSkillCast, EventDefinition.SkillCastUuid, ConfigurationData.GetSkillTag). Spell remains in established names of the configuration and of the module bodies (SpellTagDefinition, SpellInstance, the Destroy spell and Modify spell nodes).
  • Received targets: the option that acts on the targets a node receives is ReceivedTargets in every enum (HealRecipient, StatusHolderTarget, TargetSelectionSource…).
  • One global entry point per role: UnleashSkillManager (instance, world, presentation) and ConfigurationManager, a static class (ConfigurationManager.ActiveConfiguration).
  • Controller input: PointedTarget is written through properties (Ally, Enemy, Spell, Position, Selection).

docs.title: Rules of a dependent asset
docs.text:
• Its own root folder and its own assemblies, which reference UnleashSkill (and UnleashSkill.Editor for the editor); never the other way around, never a file of the base asset modified.
  • Its own namespace (not UnleashSkill.*): a simple name equal to a sibling namespace of UnleashSkill would be ambiguous (Architecture page).
  • Its types serialized by reference (nodes, status behaviors) are written into the data with the name of its assembly: never rename it, and move a renamed type through [MovedFrom].
  • It follows the node rules (Writing a node): simulation time, collisions through the SkillWorld, presentation through commands, texts in English translated by tables.

docs.title: Nodes
docs.text:
Extension point Use NodeModel + [NodeInfo] + [Serializable] A third-party node, in any assembly: offered in the creation menu (SearchNodeProvider.GetMenuNodeTypes, all loaded assemblies), executed like ours. Same rules as in Writing a node. A node without its own [NodeInfo] (subclass, test class) is not offered [ExposedProperty], [HideIf] / [ShowIf], [FoldedOption], UUID attributes ([StatUuid], [StatusUuid]…), [AnchorSources], [DirectionSources], [TurnAware] Fields shown by the default editor node, with the same drawers DefaultEditorNode<TModel> (the add-on's editor assembly) Own editor node: a concrete class derived for the model's exact type, constructor (TModel, SerializedObject), found by EditorNodeFactory. Without it: DefaultEditorNode<NodeModel> BehaviorModel.CreateBodyBehavior → IBodyBehavior Module support (simulation step of the body). A movement goes through a trajectory (TrajectoryDefinition, segments), not through a new movement behavior DescribeFlow, ReadsTargets, ReadsAimPoint, ReadsParentBody Declared flow, read by the graph analysis and the validator StatusBehavior Third-party status behavior, offered by the statuses panel (TypeCache) and serialized by reference in the configuration

Build and cast a graph from code: SkillGraphModel.CreateNew() (a graph with its Start node; ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<SkillGraphModel>() gives an empty one), graph.Nodes, graph.Connections (SkillGraphConnection, endpoints SkillGraphConnectionPort(nodeId, PortType, rank), or PortKeyResolver.TryCreatePort), then caster.Cast(graph, out execution) or graph.Compute(caster).

docs.title: Presentation
Authority and simulation
docs.text: Extension point Use ISkillAuthority (SkillWorld.Authority, LocalAuthority by default) Who decides on impacts: ResolvesHits, ConfirmHit consulted before an impact counts IWorldStepListener (SkillWorld.AddStepListener) Step added to the world tick (after the distribution of impacts): sending a tick's events, validation… An exception goes to SkillWorld.ExceptionHandler (Debug.LogException by default: a server logs it its own way) and the tick goes on ISimulationEntity, IMovementDriver World entity (pose read at the start of the tick, requested movements), without a MonoBehaviour BodyHistory Snapshots of the bodies per tick (lag compensation) SimulationSandbox A second world in the same process (preview, network bench). An add-on keeps its per-world state on the SkillWorld (step listener instance, or a dictionary keyed by world), never in a static read during a tick; an object it creates without a parent while simulating goes through SimulationSandbox.AdoptCreated UnleashSkillManager.ResetWorld(world) World with special settings (server, tests)

docs.title: Events
docs.text: Extension point Use GameEventBus (UnleashSkillManager.World.Events): Emitted, Subscribe(uuid, handler) Gameplay events (Hit, Death, Kill, statuses, skill cast, cast interrupted, summon, contact, custom events) UnleashSkillManager.EmitGameEvent The game emits a custom event (parry, dodge) UnleashSkillManager.ExecutionStarted, ExecutionEnded An execution enters the list of active ones (cast, passive, skill cast by a skill), or leaves it (completed or canceled, removed by the manager's Update or by UnregisterActiveSkillExecution). Swapped by SimulationSandbox: the editor preview does not notify the game's subscribers. A subscriber that throws is logged, the others are still called. A canceled execution whose node threw carries the exception in SkillExecution.Fault SkillExecution.DamageDealt Damage dealt by an execution UnleashSkillManager.WorldChanged The world was replaced (ResetWorld): previous world, then new world (null: recreated on the next access to World). Not raised by the first creation of the world, nor inside a SimulationSandbox. A subscriber that throws is logged, the others are still called

docs.title: The bus lives with the world
docs.text:
The event bus belongs to the world: UnleashSkillManager.World.Events is the bus of the current world. Replacing the world (UnleashSkillManager.ResetWorld, a new game) replaces the bus: the subscribers of the old one no longer hear anything, without any error.

  • Subscribe after the manager's Awake: on entering Play Mode, the manager calls ResetWorld() in its Awake, so a subscription taken in another Awake can already be lost. Subscribe in Start (every Awake of the scene has run by then) or later.
  • Subscribe again on WorldChanged: the event is raised after each replacement. Reading UnleashSkillManager.World there gives the new world (or creates it with the active configuration's settings, as the next access would).
using UnleashSkill;
using UnleashSkill.Configuration;
using UnleashSkill.Simulation;
using UnityEngine;

public class HitFeedback : MonoBehaviour
{
    void Start()
    {
        Subscribe();
        UnleashSkillManager.WorldChanged += OnWorldChanged;
    }

    void OnDestroy()
    {
        UnleashSkillManager.WorldChanged -= OnWorldChanged;
        UnleashSkillManager.CurrentWorld?.Events.Unsubscribe(EventDefinition.HitUuid, OnHit);
    }

    void OnWorldChanged(SkillWorld previous, SkillWorld current) => Subscribe();

    void Subscribe() => UnleashSkillManager.World.Events.Subscribe(EventDefinition.HitUuid, OnHit);

    void OnHit(GameEvent hit) { /* flash, sound, score */ }
}

The same holds for everything else the world owns (profile, trace, time scales): see Restart a game.

docs.title: Editor
docs.text:
