Extension point Use NodeEditor.GraphViewCreated (+ NodeEditor.Graph, NodeEditor.GraphView) The graph window has just built its interface: an add-on adds its panel to it (rootVisualElement) and reads the open graph NodeGraphView: AddNode, AddNodeConnectedTo, ReplaceNode, Reload, SelectedNodes, FlowAnalysis Modify the open graph (Undo included) SearchNodeProvider.GetMenuNodeTypes, EditorNodeFactory, NodeFieldReflection List of nodes, editor node of a model, exposed fields (AI catalog) FieldLabel (UnleashSkill.Editor.PropertyDrawers) Displayed label of a field (without its Uuid suffix, unit of a [TurnAware] field), as the editor shows it

InspectorView and SplitView are public only because NodeEditor.uxml instantiates them; they are not extension points. | GraphFlowAnalysis (runtime) | Graph flow and W112 to W116 warnings |

docs.title: Localization
docs.text:
The interface is in English in the code; other languages come from tables.

Extension point Use Localizer.RegisterTable(LocalizationTable) / UnregisterTable An add-on adds its own translations (its texts are written in English in its code). Several tables of the same language combine, the last one registered wins LocalizationTable.ParsePo(text, language), new LocalizationTable(language) + Set(english, translation, context) Read a gettext .po file, or build a table from code Localizer.Tr, TrFormat, TrContext, Translate(text, language), HasTranslation, Languages, LanguageChanged Translate in the current language or in a given one (AI catalog: same tables as the editor), rebuild a window when the language changes NodeText.Title, MenuPath, Tooltip, OutputPortLabel (optional language) Displayed texts of a node, translated without changing its identity (class name, field names) EditorLocalization.Language Language chosen in Preferences → UnleashSkill (per user, EditorPrefs)

A new language for the whole editor is a .po file named after its code (de.po) in Editor/Localization/: it appears in the preferences without recompiling.

docs.title: Statuses, events, damage
docs.text:
User version: Statuses, Events, Damage and reactions, Dynamic values.

Principle: nothing gameplay-related is hard-coded. A need is first expressed as configuration data (status, event, category, tag, mark) carried by a generic behavior. A new coded behavior must serve several pieces of data; never a specialized node (no “OnCrit”, but Chance + Mark branch + On event).

docs.title: Where the code lives
docs.text:
Paths relative to Assets/UnleashSkill/Runtime/.

Topic Data (configuration) Runtime Statuses Configuration/StatusDefinition.cs, StatusCategory.cs, StatusBehaviors.cs, InterceptionStatusBehaviors.cs Simulation/StatusContainer.cs, StatusInstance.cs, StatusStepper.cs Events Configuration/EventDefinition.cs (natives in Natives) Simulation/GameEvent.cs, GameEventBus.cs, GameEvents.cs (native emitters) Damage Damage types, stats, damage formula (ConfigurationData) Simulation/DamageFormula.cs, Simulation/DamagePipeline.cs, Execution/DamageEvent.cs, EntityDeathScope.cs Reactions Configuration/ReactionDefinition.cs, ReactionProfile*.cs Nodes/Actions/ReactionModel.cs Locks Lock behavior Simulation/EntityLocks.cs, Core/EntityLockStepper.cs Values — Execution/ValueSource.cs, Execution/ValueFormula.cs Nodes — Apply / Remove / Modify status, Emit event, On event (OnGameEventModel), Simple / Advanced damage

docs.title: Statuses
docs.text:
• A StatusDefinition (UUID) carries: positive / negative, category, max stacks, duration, stacking policy, presentation, and a polymorphic list of behaviors ([SerializeReference] behaviors).
  • The holder is an IStatusHolder (SkillTarget): its StatusContainer (Apply, Remove, RemoveWhere, AddDuration, AddStacks, Has, GetStacks, IsImmuneTo, BlocksSpell…).
  • StatusStepper (world step listener) advances the durations at the holder's step (clock.DeltaTimeFor(holder)), then StatusBehavior.Step.
  • Application and removal emit the native events Status applied / Status removed (with StatusRemovalReason).
  • Diminishing returns per category (StatusCategory), modulated by the entity's reaction profile (boss).

Existing behaviors: PeriodicStatusBehavior (damage or heal per stack, through the pipeline), StatModifierStatusBehavior (additive, %, or frozen replacement), LockStatusBehavior, UntargetableStatusBehavior, IntangibleStatusBehavior, ImmunityStatusBehavior, RemoveOnEventStatusBehavior, EventOnlyStatusBehavior, and the interceptions: DamageTakenMultiplierStatusBehavior, AbsorbHitsStatusBehavior, RedirectStatusBehavior, MinimumHealthStatusBehavior, ReflectStatusBehavior.

docs.title: Add a status behavior
docs.text:
1. [Serializable] class derived from StatusBehavior in Configuration/ (assembly UnleashSkill, serialized by reference: never rename or move it afterwards).
  2. DisplayName (English text through Tr), public fields with [Tooltip] in English (French in fr.po); a tunable number is a ValueSource (evaluated with the instance: see InterceptionFilter.Evaluate).
  3. Useful hooks: CreateState (state per application), OnApplied, OnStacksChanged, OnReapplied, OnRemoved, Step(instance, state, deltaTime).
  4. The Statuses panel of the main menu offers it automatically (TypeCache.GetTypesDerivedFrom<StatusBehavior> in StatusConfigPanel).
  5. If it acts on damage: call it explicitly at its place in DamagePipeline.Intercept (statuses.ForEach<YourBehavior>(…)). There is no generic hook: the order of the pipeline is a gameplay rule.
  6. EditMode tests (test holder, StatusContainer, SimulationClock.Fixed clock), then a skill that uses it, cast in a test world.

docs.title: Damage pipeline
docs.text:
DamagePipeline is the only path for damage: Simple damage, Advanced damage and the ticks of periodic statuses go through it, as a DamageHit (attacker, target, amount, type, source node, branch, source status, critical). Order (Apply):

  1. Amount computed by the damage formula (see below).
  2. Immunities and before-hit listeners (SkillTarget.BeforeHitListener): blocked, nothing more.
  3. Damage taken multiplier (product of the factors).
  4. Absorption: the first status with a charge absorbs the whole hit.
  5. Redirection: each redirection takes its % of what remains.
  6. Reflection: its % set aside for the attacker.
  7. Application to the stats, capped by minimum HP.
  8. After-hit listeners, Hit / Kill events, then death of the target (EntityDeathScope: Death, then cancellation of its skills).
  9. Redirected and reflected shares, as secondary hits (steps 2 to 8, without redirection or reflection: no loop).

Hit listeners receive an OnHitData (Amount, Origin, DamageType, SpellTagUuids, AffectedStats); a before-hit listener blocks the hit by setting ListenerState.Passed to false. Tag listeners (SkillTarget.BeforeTagApply, OnTagApply) receive an OnTagApplyData (TagToApply), stat changes (EntityStats.StatChanged) a StatChangedData (StatUuid, ValueBefore, ValueAfter, HasMaximumValue, MaximumValue, Origin).

A new damage node computes its amount with ConfigurationData.GetDamageFormula().Compute(...), builds a DamageHit (amount and marks of the DamageRoll) and calls DamagePipeline.Apply; it never modifies a health stat directly.

docs.title: Damage formula
docs.text:
DamageFormula (damageFormula field of the configuration, Damage formula panel) is the only amount calculation, shared by Simple damage, Advanced damage, the ticks of periodic statuses. The amount starts from the node's base (amount, Advanced damage stats, tick amount × stacks), then each declared step (DamageStepDefinition: UUID, name, operation) applies in list order. No step is specific to the code: the operation is generic.

Operation (DamageStepOperation) Effect DamageTypeModifiers DamageType.ApplyModifiers: modifiedByStat on the current amount (attacker's stats; without an attacker, ignored) NodeAndBranchMultipliers node multiplier (Advanced damage) × BranchDamageMultiplier Add / Multiply adds / multiplies by value (ValueSource) Roll roll of chance (%, the execution's randomness); automatically successful if the branch carries markUuid and markForcesSuccess. Success: amount × value, markUuid applied to the hit

A step with appliesToPeriodic false is skipped by the ticks. The default formula (CreateDefaultSteps): damage type, multipliers, then the Critical, a Roll step like any other (0%, × 2, Critical mark, not on ticks), under the UUID DamageFormula.CriticalStepUuid that the nodes' old internal critical hits map to. A node overrides the chance and value of a step by UUID (DamageStepOverride, damageStepOverrides field).

The marks of successful rolls are carried by the hit (DamageHit.Marks, DamageEvent.Marks) and added to the marks of the Hit / Kill event: a listener filters by mark (HasMark), whatever it is. A critical hit is read through its mark (HasMark, mark of the Critical step). An effect per damage type goes through a Hit listener filtered by type, or a Damage taken multiplier status.

Add an operation: a value of DamageStepOperation handled in DamageFormula.Compute and its fields shown by DamageStepDefinitionDrawer; same vocabulary as the calculation phases planned for stats (base = Set, then ordered operations), no second engine.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
• EventDefinition: natives (fixed UUIDs in the code, EventDefinition.Natives, cannot be deleted) and custom (configuration). Natives: event-hit (Hit), event-kill, event-death, event-status-applied, event-status-removed, event-spell-cast, event-cast-interrupted, event-summon-created, event-obstacle-contact. Their names are in English in the code and translated at display time (context event).
  • GameEvent: definition, source, subject, source execution, skill tags, branch marks, value, status and stacks, reason, position.
  • GameEventBus (UnleashSkillManager.World.Events): Subscribe(uuid, handler), Unsubscribe, Emit. Emit first notifies the statuses of the subject and the source (Removal on event), then the subscribers. Depth and nesting are capped (anti-loop).
  • The game emits a custom event with UnleashSkillManager.EmitGameEvent(uuid, source, subject, value) (parry, successful dodge…).
  • Listener in a graph: OnGameEventModel (On event), filters by role (me, allies, enemies, summons), tags, marks; one branch per event, target = subject or source, value in EventValueKey.

docs.title: Add a native event
docs.text:
1. UUID constant and Native(...) entry in EventDefinition (English name, description of the source, the subject and the value), and their French translation in fr.po.
  2. Emitter in GameEvents (RaiseXxx, modeled on RaiseSkillCast) called at the right place in the engine. The engine emits, never a specialized node.
  3. If the event has its own filter (status, damage type), add it to the filter of OnGameEventModel.
  4. EditMode tests on the bus (test subscriber) and an On event case in a cast skill.

docs.title: Dynamic values and formulas
docs.text:
• ValueSource: numeric field of a node. Modes (ValueSourceMode): fixed, stat (caster or target; current, max, %), execution value (number of targets, last damage, skill variable, stacks removed, charge…), distance, status stacks, event value, formula. Then value × multiplier + add, clamped if requested. DependsOnTarget: the node evaluates it per target. Outside an execution (native regeneration of a stat: CustomStat.RegenerationAmount and RegenerationInterval), EvaluateForHolder(stats, owner) evaluates for the entity that carries the stat: it is caster and target, its stats are read in stats (even without an owner), execution values, event values and distance are 0.
  • ValueFormula: expression parsed once (Parse), evaluated without allocation. Operators + - * / % ^, min, max, clamp, Stat(name[, Caster|Target][, Current|Max|Percent]), Stacks(name[, Target|Caster]), Var(name), Random() (0 to 100 excluded, SkillExecution.Random; 0 outside an execution), native values (Targets, LastDamage, Distance…). Names read without case or accents, except variables. Division by zero or non-finite result: 0. The French vocabulary of earlier versions (Lanceur, Cible, Courante, Pourcent, Hasard, Cibles, DerniersDegats…, et, ou, non) stays accepted as aliases.
  • Conditions: comparators < > <= >= = != (== accepted) then not, and, or, all under + - (grammar: or → and → not → comparison → sum). A comparison is 1 or 0, a non-zero value is true; equality within ValueFormula.EqualityTolerance (SimulationClock.Epsilon); non-associative comparisons (1 < x < 3: positioned error); and / or without short-circuit (postfix form). and, or, not and their aliases are reserved (Var(and) for a variable with this name). Check condition (ConditionalCheckModel, ConditionCheckType.Formula) evaluates its formula per target if DependsOnTarget, once otherwise; a formula text field takes [SkillFormula] (help and errors in the editor, SkillFormulaDrawer).
  • A new native value: a member of ExecutionValueKind, read by ValueSource, and its entry in the Natives table of ValueFormula (English displayed name, pre-1.0 alias → source), which feeds NativeNames and the editor's help.

docs.title: Presentation
docs.text:
User version: Presentation.

Code: Assets/UnleashSkill/Runtime/Presentation/ (assembly UnleashSkill).

docs.title: Principle
docs.text:
Nodes emit intentions; reusable definitions (assets) describe the content; a system materializes them after the simulation.

nodes / modules ──► PresentationCommandBuffer ──(LateUpdate)──► PresentationSystem ──► backends
                    (UnleashSkillManager.PresentationCommands)       IEffectPlayer, ISoundPlayer, ICameraShaker,
                                                                     IEntityAnimator, IIndicatorPlayer

Two rules: the presentation never modifies the simulation, and gameplay never holds a Unity presentation object (only UUIDs and handles). Disabled (server, tests, preview without visuals), the queue ignores commands and returns PresentationHandle.None: the fight does not change.

docs.title: Emit a command
docs.text:
UnleashSkillManager.PresentationCommands (PresentationCommandBuffer):

Method Command SpawnEffect(uuid, anchor, position, …) / StopEffect(handle) Effect (EffectDefinition) PlaySound(uuid, anchor, position, …) / StopSound(handle) Sound (SoundDefinition) CameraShake(uuid, position, intensity) Shake (CameraShakeDefinition) PlayAnimation(uuid, entityId, speed) / StopAnimation / SetAnimationSpeed Animation (AnimationDefinition) ShowIndicator(shape, anchor, …) / UpdateIndicator / HideIndicator Ground indicator (IndicatorShape)

Anchor (PresentationAnchor): InWorld, OnEntity(entityId, bone), OnBody(bodyId) (interpolated position of the body). To choose a node's points (impact, received targets, caster, module body), PresentationPoints.Collect does the work shared by the Play effect / Play sound nodes.

The handle is used to stop later: context.Execution.TrackPresentation(key, handle) tracks it in the execution, StopPresentation(key) stops it (Stop effect node), and Cancel / Cleanup stop everything tracked. A one-shot effect does not need to be tracked: it plays until the end.

Model: PlaySoundModel.OnStart (checks commands.Enabled, emits per point, tracks the handle if the sound loops or has a key, then CompleteNodeInstance whatever happens).

docs.title: Library
docs.text:
PresentationLibrary (single global asset, PresentationLibrary.Active): lists of effects, sounds, shakes, module visuals, animations. Each definition (PresentationDefinition) has a stable UUID; models store the UUID (string), never the Unity reference. Resolution: TryGet<T>(uuid, out definition), GetEffect, GetSound… Editing: Presentation section of the main menu.

ModuleVisualDefinition describes a module's visual: body prefab (with SkillPrefab: pooled, interpolated, no logic) and launch, loop, impact and expiration effects / sounds (ModuleVisualPresenter). A module without a visual stays valid. Who carries the body prefab depends on the mode: in real-time mode, the module's SkillPrefab, taken from the SkillPooler (counters: SkillPooler.Current.ActiveVisualCount…); in turn-based mode, for a module replayed by the presentation (resolved on the selection, area or beam in turns), the IModuleVisualPlayer (ModuleVisualPlayer.ActiveCount, which stays at 0 in real-time mode). See Diagnose and measure.

docs.title: System and backends
docs.text:
PresentationSystem (UnleashSkillManager.Presentation) consumes the queue in LateUpdate (Process(world, deltaTime)), associates each handle with the live instance, follows anchors and entity time (hitstop: animation at speed 0).

Interface Default (Backends/) Replace for IEffectPlayer ParticleEffectPlayer (pools per definition) VFX Graph (planned) ISoundPlayer AudioSourceSoundPlayer (pool of AudioSources) FMOD, Wwise ICameraShaker SimpleCameraShaker; Cinemachine 3 if present (UnleashSkill.Cinemachine, DefaultPresentationBackends.CameraShakerFactory) The game's camera IEntityAnimator PlayablesEntityAnimator (Playables on the Animator, blended with the Animator Controller) The game's animation system IIndicatorPlayer LineIndicatorPlayer (LineRenderer outline) Decals, shaders IModuleVisualPlayer ModuleVisualPlayer (body prefab of a ModuleVisualDefinition, pool per prefab, colliders disabled) Visual replayed separately

DefaultPresentationBackends.Install(system, library) connects the defaults to the empty slots; a game assigns before (or replaces) a property of the system (Effects, Sounds, CameraShaker, Animator, Indicators, ModuleVisuals). The resolvers EntityResolver, EntityTimeScaleResolver, EntityCollector link entity identifiers to transforms.

docs.title: Delayed commands and replay (turn-based)
docs.text:
A command can carry a delay (PresentationCommand.Delay, presentation seconds): the system keeps it (ScheduledCount, ScheduledDuration) and runs it on time, in presentation time (sum of the Process steps). A command that targets an instance not yet played (stop) waits at least for it to be played. Disabling the presentation clears the queue.

A node never writes the delay by hand: it is the queue's ambient delay (PresentationCommandBuffer.Delay), set for the duration of a scope by SkillExecution.PresentationAt(delay) (using), which also extends SkillExecution.PresentationDuration. In turn-based mode, every command emitted by the nodes of an execution (start, turn, step) pushes back the end of its presentation by its delay plus its own duration, read from its definition (one-shot effect: emission plus particle lifetime; sound: longest clip; shake; animation without a loop): PresentationDuration, and PresentationRemaining once the frame has started it, which IsTurnReady waits for. A StopAll ends that wait. SkillExecution.Defer keeps the delay of when it was queued: a continuation (result of a query on the selection) is presented with what started it. In real time, the delay stays 0.

The projectile resolved on the selection (GameObjectModel.ResolveOnSelection) uses it: each target is distributed in a scope at its arrival time (distance / speed of the body at spawn), then ModuleVisualPresenter.OnReplayed emits SpawnModuleVisual, the effect and the loop sound on a travel anchor (PresentationAnchor.Travel(from, to, duration), position interpolated since the instance was played, gone at the end of the travel). The pooler does not instantiate its visual (GameObjectModel.InstantiatesVisual).

An area or a beam in turn-based mode (GameObjectModel.PresentsVisualInTurns, carrier module whose logic advances in turns) has its visual played by the presentation too: SpawnModuleVisual in the world at the body's pose (per-axis scale PresentationCommand.AxisScale: the module's box), with the loop effect and sound, placed again when the body moves on a turn. Its end (expiration, stop of the visual and of the loop) is emitted in a scope delayed by ModuleVisualDefinition.TurnDisplayDuration after its last activation, so an instant area stays visible and PresentationDuration includes that display. An Attack in turns has its visual played the same way, without that extra display: its end is already replayed at the end of its recovery.

docs.title: Animation and gameplay
docs.text: Animation never drives gameplay. The data gameplay needs (phases in ticks, bone trajectory, root motion) is extracted in the editor from the clip (AnimationClipExtractor, AnimationExtractedData, inspector of an AnimationDefinition) and read by the Attack module without playing the clip. A stale extraction is flagged (IsStale).

docs.title: Add a command type
docs.text:
1. Value in PresentationCommandType, required fields in PresentationCommand (struct, no managed reference).
  2. Emission method in PresentationCommandBuffer.
  3. Handling in PresentationSystem.Process and backend interface in PresentationBackends.cs, default implementation in Backends/.
  4. EditMode tests on the emitted commands (PresentationCommandBuffer.Commands), Play Mode on the materialization.

docs.title: Simulation world
docs.text:
User version: Simulation world.

Code: Assets/UnleashSkill/Runtime/Simulation/ (assembly UnleashSkill). The Simulation/Collision/ core is pure C#, in Burst format (blittable structs, arrays, no managed reference in the data). To keep a pure .NET server possible, new code in Simulation/ does not import UnityEngine when it can avoid it.

docs.title: Golden rule
docs.text: The simulation never reads the scene, except the static scenery (through its backend) and the pose of the entities at the start of the tick. Everything else is data: no Physics.* query in a node, no SkillPrefab transform read for logic.

docs.title: The tick
docs.text:
SkillWorld is owned by UnleashSkillManager.World, created on first request with a copy of the SimulationSettings of the active configuration (World.Settings changed from code never touches the asset: Where to change a setting). UnleashSkillManager.Update calls World.Update(Time.deltaTime): an accumulator (FixedStepClock) plays zero, one or several ticks (TickRate, 60 by default), capped by MaxTicksPerFrame (the extra ticks are dropped: the game slows down, DroppedTicks). World.Step() plays exactly one tick (tests).

Order of a tick (SkillWorld.Step, numbered comments in the code):

1.  Snapshot N: pose of the entities (hurtboxes), time scale of each body, hitstop
2a. Simulation steps of the bodies (IBodyStepListener: modules' OnBodyStep, behaviors); queries queued
2b. Sweeps N → N+1 of the simulated bodies
3-4 Grid rebuilt (queried layers only), batch run: sweeps then queries, against bodies and scenery
5a. Resolution of the simulated bodies (HitPolicy), in identifier order
5b. Resolution of the one-off queries, in queuing order
6.  Query continuations (ModuleQuery), then impacts distributed (OnHit…)
6b. Step listeners (IWorldStepListener): executions (OnSimulationStep), statuses, locks, combos, cooldowns, regeneration
7.  Movements: one request per entity (the highest priority), applied by its IMovementDriver → pose N+1
8.  Snapshot pushed into BodyHistory
(frame) The visual interpolates between the last two states (InterpolationAlpha)

Contracts to respect:

  • During a tick, entities are still for collision (pose read at step 1).
  • Movements requested during tick N (RequestMovement: dash, knockback, pull) are resolved at step 7: a single request applies per entity, by priority, without accumulation; Block (root, stun) wins except against Forced. The pose actually reached by the Rigidbody or the CharacterController is authoritative.
  • A node started during a tick waits for the next tick for its first OnSimulationStep.
  • Results sorted by time of impact (or distance), then by identifier: it is a gameplay specification, covered by tests.

docs.title: Bodies and entities
docs.text:
Element Code Notes Shape Shape (Sphere, Capsule, Box; queries: Ray, Cone, Ring) Local offset possible Body Body in BodyStore (SoA, stable identifiers BodyId) Identity: OwnerEntityId, SourceExecutionId, Team (hashed UUID) Simulated body AddSimulatedBody(SimulatedBodyDesc) Velocity, HitPolicy, filter, listener; Intangible (carrier), Blocker (wall) Entity ISimulationEntity, implemented by SkillTarget; SkillEntityRegistry Registered on enable; its Hurtboxes become bodies (default capsule derived from the bounds) Movement IMovementDriver (CharacterController, otherwise Rigidbody, otherwise transform) Replaceable through SkillTarget.MovementDriver Static scenery IStaticScenery: PhysicsScenery3D, PhysicsScenery2D, none Unity layers of SceneryLayers; a single batch per tick. A body's sweep carries the plane's normal (SceneryQuery.PlaneNormal): a 3D backend stops a body moving along the plane only where the scenery crosses its height Dynamic obstacle Body of the Obstacle layer Wall (Blocker support), shield

On the module side, ModuleBody wraps the body: Spawn, Position, MoveTo, SetDirection, SetShape, Subscribe(IModuleHitListener), Remove. A module's shape is its Scale box, approximated by a capsule (BoxApproximation). Position, Velocity and Rotation are Unity.Mathematics types; a game that does not reference that package reads WorldPosition, WorldVelocity and Direction (Vector3, see Skills → Testing a skill). In the same way, a static body (a test wall, AddBody) is placed with Shape.Box(x, y, z), Body.WorldPosition and Body.WorldRotation (float, Vector3, Quaternion; see Walls and variants of a skill).

docs.title: Hit rules: HitPolicy
docs.text:
Serialized in the nodes (OnHit, modules):

Field Effect maxTargets Piercing: 1 = classic projectile, 0 = unlimited (always capped by DefaultMaxCandidates) rehit (Once, EveryTick, Cooldown) + rehitCooldown Re-hit of the same target (delay in body time) blockedByObstacles (Inherit, Yes, No) Override of the layer matrix for obstacles requireLineOfSight Nothing is hit behind an obstacle

Detection and resolution are separate: the core finds the candidates and their times of impact, the HitPolicy decides (piercing, re-hit, blocking). A target refused by a listener's filter (AcceptsHit) is gone through without counting.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text: SimulationLayers: Entity (0), Skill (1), Obstacle (2), TimeZone (3), then up to 28 custom layers. LayerMatrix (configuration, Simulation menu) gives for each pair Ignore, Touch (event) or Block (stops a sweep). Query filters (SimulationFilter.ForSkill(caster, execution, team)) leave out the caster, the same execution, or allies (friendly fire).

docs.title: One-off queries
docs.text:
For a detection outside a body (instant area, beam, Chain bounce):

// In the runtimeData: one continuation per instance
var query = new ModuleQuery(caster: caster, context: context, onResult: (world, hits) =>
{
    // Called during the tick that runs the query (step 6); hits is only valid here
    var targets = new List<SkillTarget>();
    ModuleTargeting.CollectTargets(hits, caster, filter, targets);
    // ... fill a branch, fire the outputs, or copy what must be kept
});
query.Overlap(world, shape, position, rotation, ModuleTargeting.QueryFilter(caster, context, ignoreCaster: false));
  • Create the ModuleQuery with the caster and the branch (new ModuleQuery(handler, caster, context)) so that it also works in turn-based mode: it then does not go to the world, but returns one contact per selected entity (TurnBasedSelection; a policy requiring line of sight, HitPolicy.RequireLineOfSight, keeps only those seen from the query's origin, tested against the scenery and the obstacles as in real-time mode), with a continuation deferred to the end of the start (SkillExecution.Defer). With followsSelection: false (new ModuleQuery(handler, caster, context, followsSelection: false)), it always goes through the world, even in turn-based mode (contact of a summoned entity, hitbox of an attack, Target selection). Created with the caster and the branch, an exception thrown by its continuation cancels the execution; the constructor without a caster (outside any execution) leaves it to the world (SkillWorld.ExceptionHandler).
  • ModuleQuery.Overlap, Sweep, Raycast queue into the batch; Pending counts the pending results (a module ends when everything has come back).
  • Queued during step 2 (OnBodyStep), the query runs in this tick; queued elsewhere (an OnStart outside a tick), it runs at the next tick. A continuation cannot queue again for the same tick.
  • The QueryHandle and its results are only valid during the continuation: buffers recycled at the next tick.
  • ModuleTargeting.CollectTargets converts the impacts into SkillTargets of the registry: targetable, alive, team filter, cut at the first block.

docs.title: Time
docs.text:
Notion API World step world.DeltaTime = tick duration × global scale (0 during a global hitstop) Global scale GlobalTimeScale; TickGlobalScale = scale of the current tick Global hitstop ApplyHitstop(ticks): freezes everything, movements included (kept for the first unfrozen tick) An entity's own time ApplyHitstop(entity, ticks), SetEntityTimeScale(entity, scale), ResetEntityTime A body's hitstop ApplyHitstop(bodyId, ticks) Time zones AddTimeZone(shape, position, rotation, scale); overlapping scales multiply; sampled at the start of the tick Effect clock SimulationClock: DeltaTime, DeltaTimeFor(entity), Reached(elapsed, duration), Fixed(dt) for tests

DeltaTimeFor(entity) = tick step × own time × the entity's time zones; for an entity carried by a body (skill instance), it is that body's step. A simulated body advances at its own step (GetBodyDeltaTime), received by OnBodyStep.

docs.title: Performance and Burst
docs.text:
Performance choices:

  • Grid of the targetable bodies (GridInsertion.QueriedLayers): only the layers that a query of the batch accepts are inserted, rebuilt on each tick.
  • Burst on the hot path (CollisionKernel: grid, broad phase, shape tests, filter, sort), as a direct synchronous call, strict floating-point mode. A single code: managed if SimulationSettings.UseBurst is false or if the editor's Burst compilation is off. No parallel jobs.
  • Still managed: sweep preparation, HitPolicy resolution, distribution, time zones.
  • SimulationProfile records the time of each step of a tick, for profiling in a build (Diagnose and measure).

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• SimulationSettings.Debug: warnings (dropped ticks, truncated candidates) and SimulationTrace (circular buffer: tick, query, candidates, impact kept, rule applied).
  • SimulationSettings.Gizmos: bodies, last queries, sweeps and impacts in the Scene view (SkillWorldGizmos).

To turn them on during a game, change UnleashSkillManager.World.Settings: a copy, the configuration stays as it is. Counters, profile and what ResetWorld() keeps: Diagnose and measure.

docs.title: Network extension points
docs.text: ISkillAuthority (LocalAuthority by default) decides on impacts; BodyHistory keeps N snapshots for lag compensation. Nothing is connected in the base asset: they are the entry points of a network layer (dependent asset).

docs.title: Why it matters
docs.text:
The engine reads a lot of state through statics: UnleashSkillManager.World, the presentation, the active executions, SkillEntityRegistry, the steppers (statuses, locks, combos, cooldowns, regeneration), SpellInstanceRegistry, the running attacks and dodges of each caster, SkillPooler, the wall pool, UnityEngine.Random. It is simple and fast: one game runs per process.

But the editor preview (Editor/Preview/SkillPreviewSession) simulates a skill while another world may exist (the game in Play Mode, the tests). It does it in a SimulationSandbox (Simulation/SimulationSandbox.cs): for the duration of a scope, each static of the engine is swapped with the sandbox's, then given back.

docs.title: Simulate in a sandbox
docs.text:
var world = new SkillWorld(new SimulationSettings { SceneryBackend = StaticSceneryBackend.None });
var sandbox = new SimulationSandbox(world, presentation: null, seed: 0);
var created = new List<GameObject>();

using (sandbox.Enter())
{
    // Here, UnleashSkillManager.World, SkillEntityRegistry, SkillPooler… are the sandbox's

    // The sandbox has no pooler (the game's is swapped out): one for the module bodies, in EditMode without Awake
    var pooler = new GameObject("SkillPooler");
    created.Add(pooler);
    pooler.AddComponent<SkillPooler>().Init();

    SkillCaster caster = CreateEntity("players", Vector3.zero, created);
    SkillCaster enemy = CreateEntity("monsters", new Vector3(0f, 0f, 5f), created);

    caster.Cast(skill, out SkillExecution execution);
    for (int tick = 0; tick < 1000 && !execution.IsCompleted; tick++)
    {
        world.Step();
        execution.Update();
    }
}
// Out of scope: the game gets its state back intact

// Cancels what remains, removes the entities from the registry, then destroys the objects inside the scope
sandbox.Dispose(() =>
{
    foreach (GameObject gameObject in created)
        Object.DestroyImmediate(gameObject);
});

static SkillCaster CreateEntity(string team, Vector3 position, List<GameObject> created)
{
    var gameObject = new GameObject(team);
    created.Add(gameObject);
    gameObject.transform.position = position;
    var entity = gameObject.AddComponent<SkillCaster>();
    entity.teamUuid = team;
    entity.ResetStats("test-template");        // Start does not run in EditMode
    SkillEntityRegistry.Register(entity);      // nor does OnEnable: registered in the sandbox's registry
    return entity;
}

Everything that touches the sandbox's simulation (placing an entity, casting, advancing a tick, destroying its objects) is done inside a scope. The sandbox calls the engine's step listeners on its own world.

  • Pooler: a sandbox starts without a SkillPooler: a module (Spell body, Area, Beam…) needs one, created and initialized (Init()) inside the scope. Without it, the module logs an error and ends without its outputs.
  • Entities: outside Play Mode, Start and OnEnable do not run: teamUuid, ResetStats(template) (template of the active configuration) and SkillEntityRegistry.Register, inside the scope.
  • Configuration: the sandbox reads the active configuration (ConfigurationManager.ActiveConfiguration), which it does not swap.
  • Cleanup: Dispose(destroyObjects) cancels the executions still active, removes the entities from the sandbox's registry, stops its presentation, then calls destroyObjects inside the scope.
  • Completed executions: without the manager's Update, a completed execution stays in ActiveSkillExecutions (sandbox.Executions) until UnleashSkillManager.UnregisterActiveSkillExecution or Dispose (Diagnose and measure).
  • Restart: UnleashSkillManager.ResetWorld() inside a scope cancels the sandbox's executions and recreates its world at once, with a copy of the replaced world's settings, its scenery, authority, warning and exception handlers (never the configuration's settings, nor its scenery); sandbox.World then returns the new world. To test a restart with a world of your own, call ResetWorld(world) with a world without scenery.
  • Seed: the seed of the constructor is that of UnityEngine.Random inside the scope. The rolls of an execution have their own seed, set with SkillExecution.SetRandomSeed (Skills → Testing a skill).

The swap covers: world, presentation, active executions (and the ExecutionStarted / ExecutionEnded events: the preview does not notify the game's subscribers), SkillEntityRegistry, the steppers of statuses, locks, combos, cooldowns and regeneration, SpellInstanceRegistry, the running attacks and dodges of each caster (AttackCancellation), the entity walls, SkillPooler, UnityEngine.Random.

The editor language (Localizer) is also a static state, but it is not read during a tick: the simulation never depends on it.

docs.title: State of an add-on
docs.text:
The list of swapped states is internal to the engine: an add-on cannot add its own. So an add-on keeps per-world state on the SkillWorld (an instance of its step listener, or a dictionary keyed by world), never in a static read during a tick. Otherwise the preview writes into the game's state (or the other way around): ghost entities, statuses that advance twice, tests that leak into each other.

An object the add-on creates without a parent while simulating (a root GameObject) goes through SimulationSandbox.AdoptCreated(gameObject): inside a sandbox, the preview stores it in its scene and destroys it with the sandbox; outside, nothing happens.

docs.title: Restart a game
docs.text:
Outside the preview, UnleashSkillManager.ResetWorld() (world recreated on demand) or ResetWorld(world) (world provided, without scenery for a Play Mode test) and ResetPresentation(...) put the engine back in a known state. They do not touch what each entity carries. To restart a game without reloading the scene (game over, retry), call in this order:

  1. UnleashSkillManager.ResetWorld(): cancels every active execution (skills cast, passives, skills that outlive their caster; ExecutionEnded for each), then replaces the world. WorldChanged is raised: the game's subscribers subscribe again to the new bus (Events).
  2. UnleashSkillManager.ResetPresentation(): stops the running effects, sounds and shakes, releases the backends; the presentation is recreated on the next access, according to the active configuration.
  3. caster.ResetEntity() on each caster that stays in the scene: stats recreated from its template, statuses, locks and cooldowns removed, alive again (a caster disabled by its death is re-enabled), passives started again (ResetWorld ended them).
  4. The game puts back what it owns: positions, the entities it spawned (destroyed or returned to its pools), tags, slots (SkillSlots.EndAllReplacements), aim (AimDirectionOverride, PointedTarget).
Call Resets Leaves as is ResetWorld() Active executions (passives included), module bodies, event bus and its subscribers, trace and profile measurements, tick count, world and entity time scales, hitstop. The bodies of the active entities are recreated in the new world Stats, statuses, locks, cooldowns, IsDead, slots and combos of each entity; a dead caster stays disabled; the configuration; the presentation; the profile enabled, Debug and Gizmos changed from code (What lives with the world) ResetPresentation() Running effects, sounds and shakes, backend pools The simulation SkillCaster.ResetEntity() Stats (template), statuses, locks, cooldowns, IsDead; passives that are not running are started; re-enabled if disabled by its death The world and the running executions (skills already cast go on: CancelSkill() cancels them), position, tags, slots, aim

docs.title: Model and editor node
docs.text:
File Folder Assembly Role [Name]Model.cs Runtime/Nodes/[Category]/ UnleashSkill Serialized data and runtime logic [Name]EditorNode.cs Editor/Graph/Nodes/[Category]/ UnleashSkill.Editor UI in the graph

The editor node is optional: EditorNodeFactory looks for the class deriving from DefaultEditorNode<TModel> for the model's exact type, otherwise it creates a DefaultEditorNode<NodeModel>, which shows the [ExposedProperty] fields. The project's convention is still to write one (even empty, like KillEditorNode); it becomes useful for a custom drawing (CustomDraw), named ports or conditional fields.

The model contains no editor code ([SerializeField] yes; PropertyField, EditorGUILayout no), instantiates nothing (new MonoBehaviour, Instantiate), makes no Physics.* query, never reads Time.deltaTime.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
• [NodeInfo("Displayed title", "Category/Displayed title", NodeType.Action)]: title, path in the creation menu, type (Module, Trigger, Conditional, Support, Action). An [Obsolete] class is hidden from the menu but can still be opened. Title and menu are written in English; the editor translates them (each menu segment separately) with the tables of Editor/Localization/.
  • [ExposedProperty] + [SerializeField] + [Tooltip] on each tunable field. The tooltip is written in English, translated at display time, and reused in the node reference of each language.
  • Display attributes (Runtime/Attributes/): [FoldedOption] (folded option), [HideIf] / [ShowIf] (conditional field: hidden or only shown when a field or a property of the model has one of the values, [ShowIf(nameof(shape), AreaShape.Rectangle, AreaShape.Line)]; several conditions combine, the field is hidden if one of them hides it; common resolution FieldVisibility, read by the node editor, the inspector and the generated reference), UUIDs chosen from a list (UuidAttributes.cs, [PresentationDefinitionUuid]), [SimulationLayerName], [UnityLayer], [AnimationBone].
  • A tunable numeric field is a ValueSource (fixed, stat, execution value, distance, stacks, event value, formula), evaluated with Evaluate(caster, context, target).

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
InitPortType() fills InputPortTypes and OutputPortTypes (one entry per port, in order):

PortType Color Use Module Blue Flow between modules (Projectile → OnHit) Trigger Green Firing actions (OnHit → Damage) Condition Orange Filter (Entity type, Chance) Support Purple Modifier (Delay, Fork, Repeat, a module's behaviors) Selection Cyan Configuration, not flow: “Selection” output of the Target selection node, “Selection” input of a node that chooses targets (Chain, Fork, Area, Summon)

A node that chooses targets takes a Selection port, not its own filters. It adds InputPortTypes.Add(PortType.Selection) at the end of its inputs and reads the connected Selection with TargetSelection.ConnectedTo(this, context) (null: its own behavior). It applies the criteria to its own candidates with selection.Criteria.Select(candidates, caster, context, center), or asks for the source's with selection.CollectCandidates(…) (immediate, or a world query whose result arrives at the next tick). The engine never executes a node whose Selection output is connected (SkillGraphModel.IsConfigurationNode), and a Selection connection is not a flow output.

A node declares what it reads and transforms. The editor shows on each connection what it carries and flags a node that reads what it will never receive; it deduces it from two declarations of the node, read by GraphFlowAnalysis without executing anything:

  • DescribeFlow(FlowState input, int outputPosition, GraphFlowAnalysis analysis): what the output at outputPosition emits when the node receives input. By default a pass-through; null for a configuration output. FlowState is immutable: WithTargets(FlowTargets.ModuleHits, this), WithoutTargets(), WithAim(FlowAim.Targeting, this), WithBranchDirection(this), WithParentBody(this). To override by a node that replaces the targets of its branches (listener, trigger, Selection, Fork), writes the aim point, a branch direction or a body.
  • ReadsTargets, ReadsAimPoint, ReadsParentBody: what the node reads. By default, deduced from its exposed and shown SkillAnchor / SkillDirection fields (anchor “received target” or “each received target”, “aim point”, “module body”). A node that acts on the received targets (damage, status on the target) overrides ReadsTargets, depending on its setting if it can target the caster: public override bool ReadsTargets => base.ReadsTargets || holder == StatusHolderTarget.ReceivedTargets;.

Warnings (GraphFlowCodes, reused by the validator): W112 acts on the received targets without receiving any (Damage behind the Start), W113 reads the module body without a module upstream (listener, anchor), W114 Selection connected both as configuration and in the flow, W115 loop of nodes that all start their outputs during their start (the engine stops it, see Cast cycle): a node that only starts them later (listener, delay greater than 0) overrides StartsOutputsDuringStart, depending on its setting if needed (public override bool StartsOutputsDuringStart => fireImmediately;); W116 On hit with Max Targets 1 under a carrier module that lasts (Area or channeled Beam with a Duration, Summon): its first target ends the module. Displayed vocabulary: received targets, event target, aim point, branch direction, module body.

Several outputs of the same type are told apart by their rank: ExecuteChainedNodes(this, caster, context, PortType.Trigger, 1) fires the second Trigger output. GetOutputPortLabel(position) names an output (“True”, “False”, in English: the editor translates it). A switch (Chance, Check condition) ends with CompleteNodeInstanceWithoutOutputs, then fires the single output chosen.

docs.title: The four node shapes
docs.text:
Shape OnStart End Examples Instant Acts, then CompleteNodeInstance(this, caster), returns null Immediate Damage, Apply status, Play sound Failure / false condition CompleteNodeInstanceWithoutOutputs(this, caster), returns null Immediate, without outputs Unmet stat condition, no target Persistent Returns a runtimeData object CompleteNodeInstance(this, caster, runtimeData) from OnSimulationStep Delay, Repeat, Timer Listener Returns a runtimeData, subscribes ExecuteChainedNodes on each event; ends without outputs at the end of its duration On event, OnHit, On tick

Never return null without completing the instance: the chain would be blocked (reported in the editor and in a Development Build).

An exception thrown by a node cancels its execution only (see Cast cycle): do not catch it to hide it. A configuration error that would repeat on each cast (unknown stat, no configuration) goes through LogConfigurationErrorOnce(message), logged once per node.

Life cycle of an instance:

Method Called Use OnStart(caster, context) At start, instance already registered Logic, returns the runtimeData OnSimulationStep(caster, context, runtimeData, clock) On each world tick (step 6b), not on the start tick Count time, deadlines OnTurnAdvanced(caster, context, runtimeData) Turn-based: on each AdvanceTurn of the caster, not on the start turn Count time in turns OnRuntime(caster, context, runtimeData) Each frame Visual only OnEnd(caster, context, runtimeData) Normal end (if the node calls it), cancellation, cleanup Unsubscribe, stop the presentation, mark finished

OnEnd can be called by Cancel or Cleanup without the node having finished: the runtimeData must be able to be marked finished (an IsFinished flag, as in the example below).

docs.title: Time
docs.text:
A persistent node outside a module advances in OnSimulationStep with clock.DeltaTimeFor(entity), the entity that carries the effect:

  • the caster for Delay, Repeat, On tick, Timer, listeners, the cast time;
  • the target for a DoT, a buff, a tag, an immunity (in practice, these are statuses, which advance on their own in the StatusStepper).

This step includes the global scale, the global hitstop, the entity's own time (hitstop and scale per entity) and the time zones it is in. Deadlines are compared with SimulationClock.Reached(elapsed, duration) (rounding tolerance: 1/60 added 60 times gives 0.99999…).

Turn-based: a duration field keeps its value, read in turns. At start, if TurnTime.IsActive, convert it (TurnTime.Duration: rounded up to the next turn; TurnTime.Period: whole rate ≥ 1), remember it in the runtimeData (InTurns), and advance by one turn (1f) in OnTurnAdvanced instead of OnSimulationStep, which then does nothing. Mark the field [TurnAware] (TurnUnit.Duration, Period or VisualOnly): the editor shows its unit according to the mode. A module overrides OnBodyTurn (its lifetime in turns is counted by GameObjectModel); its OnBodyStep no longer runs, unless it overrides StepsBodyInTurns to keep a tick step that does not count time (movement, presence: SummonModel). Example: DelayModel.

A node whose instance still advances on the world tick in turn-based mode (a movement, a delay counted in seconds) overrides HoldsTurn(runtimeData): as long as it returns true, the execution's turn is not ready (SkillExecution.IsTurnLogicResolved, IsTurnReady). False by default: an instance that waits for turns, a listener or a lasting effect does not hold the turn.

docs.title: Complete example: persistent node
docs.text:
A “Countdown” that waits for a tunable duration (stat or formula possible), at the caster's time, then fires its outputs if its branch still has a living target, and fails otherwise.

using UnityEngine;
using UnleashSkill.Execution;
using UnleashSkill.Nodes.Attributes;
using UnleashSkill.Simulation;

namespace UnleashSkill.Nodes.Supports
{
    /// <summary>State of an instance: pure, testable in EditMode without a world.</summary>
    public class CountdownRuntimeData
    {
        public float Duration { get; }
        public float Elapsed { get; private set; }
        public bool IsFinished { get; set; }   // normal end, or cancellation (OnEnd)

        public CountdownRuntimeData(float duration) => Duration = duration;

        public bool Advance(float deltaTime)
        {
            Elapsed += Mathf.Max(0f, deltaTime);   // 0 during a hitstop
            return SimulationClock.Reached(Elapsed, Duration);
        }
    }

    [NodeInfo("Countdown", "Support/Countdown", NodeType.Support)]
    [System.Serializable]
    public class CountdownModel : NodeModel
    {
        [ExposedProperty]
        [SerializeField]
        [Tooltip("Duration in seconds, at the caster's time (hitstop and time zones included)")]
        private ValueSource duration = new ValueSource(2f);

        public ValueSource Duration => duration;

        protected override void InitPortType()
        {
            InputPortTypes.Add(PortType.Trigger);
            OutputPortTypes.Add(PortType.Trigger);
        }

        public override object OnStart(SkillCaster caster, SkillExecutionContext context)
        {
            if (context?.Execution == null)
                return null;   // outside an execution (isolated test): nothing to complete

            // Evaluated once, at start, with the branch's first target
            float seconds = Mathf.Max(0f, duration.Evaluate(caster, context, context.GetPrimaryTarget()));
            if (seconds <= 0f)
            {
                Finish(caster, context, null);   // zero duration: behaves like an instant node
                return null;
            }

            return new CountdownRuntimeData(seconds);
        }

        public override void OnSimulationStep(SkillCaster caster, SkillExecutionContext context, object runtimeData, SimulationClock clock)
        {
            if (!(runtimeData is CountdownRuntimeData data) || data.IsFinished)
                return;

            // The caster carries the wait: its step, not the world's
            if (!data.Advance(clock.DeltaTimeFor(caster)))
                return;

            data.IsFinished = true;
            Finish(caster, context, data);
        }

        private void Finish(SkillCaster caster, SkillExecutionContext context, CountdownRuntimeData data)
        {
            // Reads the targets of ITS branch, never another's
            bool hasTarget = context.Targets.Exists(target => target != null && target.isActiveAndEnabled);

            // Several countdowns of the same node can run (Repeat → Countdown):
            // complete by runtimeData when there is one
            if (hasTarget)
            {
                if (data != null) context.Execution.CompleteNodeInstance(this, caster, data);
                else context.Execution.CompleteNodeInstance(this, caster);
            }
            else
            {
                if (data != null) context.Execution.CompleteNodeInstanceWithoutOutputs(this, data);
                else context.Execution.CompleteNodeInstanceWithoutOutputs(this, caster);
            }
        }

        public override void OnEnd(SkillCaster caster, SkillExecutionContext context, object runtimeData)
        {
            // Also called by Cancel / Cleanup: never fire the outputs afterwards
            if (runtimeData is CountdownRuntimeData data)
                data.IsFinished = true;
        }
    }
}

Key points: CompleteNodeInstance fires the outputs with the instance's context (each chained node receives a copy of the branch); no reference to Time; the state lives in the runtimeData, not in the model's fields (the model is shared by all executions of the skill).

Matching editor node (Editor/Graph/Nodes/Supports/CountdownEditorNode.cs):

using UnityEditor;
using UnleashSkill.Editor.Graph;
using UnleashSkill.Nodes.Supports;

namespace UnleashSkill.Editor.Graph.Nodes.Supports
{
    public class CountdownEditorNode : DefaultEditorNode<CountdownModel>
    {
        public CountdownEditorNode(CountdownModel model, SerializedObject skillGraphObject) : base(model, skillGraphObject)
        {
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Listeners
docs.text:
An event node:

  • subscribes in OnStart (world bus: UnleashSkillManager.World.Events.Subscribe(eventUuid, handler), or ModuleBody.Subscribe for a module's impacts) and returns its runtimeData;
  • on each event, creates a dedicated branch (context.CreateBranch()), adds the event's target to it, then ExecuteChainedNodes(this, caster, branch);
  • counts its duration in OnSimulationStep at the caster's pace, then unsubscribes and ends with CompleteNodeInstanceWithoutOutputs;
  • also unsubscribes in OnEnd (cancellation).

Model to follow: OnGameEventModel (anti-loop through AddSourceListener / HasSourceListener, max count, internal cooldown).

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
A module (Projectile, Area, Beam, Summon, Attack…) derives from GameObjectModel:

  • it has a simulated body (ModuleBody, created by Spawn(SimulatedBodyDesc)), swept by the world; a module that detects by itself (Area, Beam) has a carrier body (Intangible) and queues queries;
  • its logic advances in OnBodyStep(caster, context, runtimeData, deltaTime) (step 2 of the tick, step of the body); OnModuleRuntime (each frame) is reserved for the visual;
  • its outputs are listeners (OnHit, OnExpire) fired right at start (LaunchOutputs), after which it ends with CompleteNodeInstanceWithoutOutputs so as not to fire them again;
  • the position lives in the body (ModuleBody.Position, MoveTo), never in the transform of the SkillPrefab (visual only);
  • behaviors connected as Support (Movement, Scale over time) become IBodyBehaviors;
  • a body movement goes through a trajectory definition (TrajectoryDefinition: Line, Curve, Orbit, Pursuit, Return segments, in the aim frame) run by TrajectoryRunner, never a new movement behavior: on each tick, the current segment computes the desired displacement and the runner sets the body's velocity (swept by the world, never MoveTo), at the body's step × the definition's scale, oscillations added, slide and bounce applied. A new segment derives from TrajectorySegment (data, [Serializable]; the blocking rule, its maximum number of blocks and the oscillations are inherited) and returns its flight state (TrajectorySegmentRun.Step); it overrides OnBounce if it holds its own direction, OnFrameTranslated if it targets a fixed world point (forced displacement). A height along the plane's normal goes through TrajectoryRunner.Rise(delta), which adds the movement in 3D and only offsets the visual in 2D (SimulatesHeight); the rules in flight (Hits In Flight, Ignores Obstacles) are inherited and applied by the runner. A reusable definition goes in the TrajectoryLibrary (Trajectory node), read by ConfigurationData.GetTrajectory.

GameObjectModel hooks: CreateRuntimeData, OnSpawned, LaunchOutputs, OnBodyStep, OnModuleRuntime, and the properties UsesSimulatedBody, HasIntangibleBody, FollowsCasterTime, HasOwnLifetime. Detections: Simulation world.

docs.title: Presentation
docs.text: A node instantiates nothing and holds no ParticleSystem, AudioSource or Animator: it emits a command (see Presentation). Gameplay never depends on the returned handle.

docs.title: Texts shown in the editor
docs.text: The text of a node (title, menu, tooltips, [Header], output labels) is written in English in the model, and translated at display time from the tables of Editor/Localization/ (NodeText, EditorLocalization). Every other text shown by the editor (editor node, drawer, window) goes through Tr("…") or TrFormat("… {0}", value) (using static UnleashSkill.Localization.Localizer;), with its translations in a .po table registered with Localizer (see Extension points). Logs and exceptions stay in English, without Tr.

docs.title: New node checklist
docs.text:
1. Model in a runtime assembly that references UnleashSkill, editor node (if the default one is not enough) in an editor assembly that references UnleashSkill.Editor.
  2. Tests of its ports and behavior: a model is instantiated without MonoBehaviour, in EditMode.
  3. A state read during a tick? Keep it per world, never in a static (state of an add-on).
  4. Texts in English, their translations in a .po table registered with Localizer (title, menu segments, tooltips, output labels).
  5. A tunable position or direction: a SkillAnchor / SkillDirection field (sources limited by [AnchorSources] / [DirectionSources]), resolved by Resolve, never a new enum or a read of caster.PointedTarget (read context.Aim). Its default is the field initializer, the same for a node created in the editor, built from code or read from JSON.
  6. What it reads and transforms: DescribeFlow if it changes the targets, the aim point, the branch direction or the body of its outputs, ReadsTargets if it acts on the received targets (see Ports); tooltips use the “received targets” vocabulary, never “branch targets”.
  7. Replacing an old node: the old model's class becomes [Obsolete] (SearchNodeProvider then removes it from the creation menu), never deleted while assets use it.

docs.title: UnleashSkill
docs.text:
UnleashSkill est un outil Unity pour créer des capacités de jeu (sorts, attaques, passifs, invocations) sans écrire de code, en assemblant des nodes dans un graphe. Il vise les RPG, les jeux d'action et le tour par tour.

[Start] ──► [Corps de sort] ◄── [Movement]        une boule de feu qui avance
                 │
                 ▼
            [Au contact] ──► [Dégâts Simple]     touche un ennemi, lui inflige des dégâts
                         └─► [Appliquer statut]  et le brûle pendant 2 secondes

docs.title: Ce que l'outil fait pour vous
docs.text:
• Un éditeur de graphe : chaque node est un comportement (projectile, zone, dégâts, statut, condition, délai…). Un sort se lit de gauche à droite.
  • Un monde de simulation : les sorts se déplacent et touchent leurs cibles dans un monde à pas fixe, indépendant de la physique Unity et du framerate. Le même sort donne le même résultat à 30 ou 144 images par seconde.
  • Une configuration sans code : stats, équipes, types d'entité, types de dégâts, statuts, événements… se déclarent dans le menu principal et se choisissent ensuite dans des listes.
  • Une présentation séparée du gameplay : effets, sons, animations et tremblements de caméra sont des assets réutilisables. On peut les désactiver (serveur, tests) sans changer le comportement du sort.
  • Un aperçu dans l'éditeur : le sort se joue à côté du graphe, sur des mannequins, sans lancer le mode Play.

docs.title: Par où commencer
docs.text:
Je veux… Lire Installer l'outil et créer mon premier sort Démarrage Comprendre comment un sort s'exécute Concepts Déclarer mes stats, équipes, statuts Configuration Régler le temps de recharge, le coût, les emplacements Sorts Savoir ce que fait un node et ses champs Référence des nodes M'inspirer d'un sort complet Recettes Développer l'outil lui-même (moteur, nodes, tests) Technique

Langue

L'éditeur est en anglais par défaut. Le français se choisit dans Edit → Preferences → UnleashSkill → Language ; cette documentation existe aussi en anglais (sélecteur de langue en haut de page).

En ligne et hors ligne

Cette documentation décrit UnleashSkill 1.x. Sa dernière version est en ligne sur pim103.github.io/UnleashSkill-docs ; le package en contient une copie hors ligne (PDF, en anglais et en français) dans Assets/UnleashSkill/Documentation/, avec le journal des modifications.

docs.title: Les menus déroulants des nodes sont vides
docs.text: Aucune configuration n'est chargée. Main Menu → Charger une configuration.

docs.title: En jeu, les nodes ne trouvent pas les stats (« No active configuration », « Target stat not found »)
docs.text: Le UnleashSkillManager de la scène n'a pas de Default Configuration. Assignez-la dans son inspecteur.

docs.title: Le sort ne part pas
docs.text: Lisez le résultat de Cast / CastSlot (SkillCastResult) : en recharge, coût insuffisant, actions bloquées (étourdi), emplacement vide, emplacement passif, emplacement verrouillé par un remplacement.

docs.title: Le sort part mais ne touche rien
docs.text:
• La cible est-elle d'une autre équipe (filtre Enemy) ? Deux entités sans équipe sont alliées.
  • La cible est-elle ciblable (Is Targetable) et non Inciblable ou Intangible (statut) ?
  • Le filtre Type d'entité garde-t-il bien ce type (hiérarchie des types) ?
  • Les Couches du décor (Simulation) contiennent-elles la couche des colliders des entités ? Le sort s'arrête alors sur leur collider comme sur un mur.
  • La matrice des couches autorise-t-elle le contact ?

Activez le débogage de la simulation (gizmos) pour voir les corps et les hurtboxes dans la vue Scène.

docs.title: Le projectile est invisible
docs.text: Le module n'a pas de Visuel, ou la présentation est désactivée. Le sort fonctionne quand même.

docs.title: Aucun effet ni son dans le build
docs.text: Renseignez la Presentation Library du UnleashSkillManager : sans elle, seule la bibliothèque par défaut de l'éditeur est trouvée.

docs.title: Erreur à chaque lecture d'une animation
docs.text: Le clip porte des événements UnleashPhase mais le personnage n'a pas de composant AnimationPhaseEventReceiver. Ajoutez-le.

docs.title: Le root motion de mon personnage s'ajoute au déplacement d'une attaque
docs.text: Un OnAnimatorMove de votre jeu sur l'Animator d'une entité n'est pas coupé par l'outil pendant une attaque qui déplace le personnage. Testez IsRootMotionCut(animator) du PlayablesEntityAnimator dans votre script et ignorez le root motion quand il est vrai.

docs.title: Le jeu ralentit quand il y a beaucoup de sorts
docs.text: Au-delà de Ticks max par frame, les ticks en trop sont abandonnés et le jeu ralentit visiblement. Activez Burst (Simulation), augmentez la Taille de cellule si les cibles sont grandes, ou baissez les Ticks par seconde.

docs.title: L'éditeur est en anglais (ou en français)
docs.text: La langue se règle par utilisateur dans Edit → Preferences → UnleashSkill → Language. Les menus Unity restent en anglais.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
Ces pages expliquent comment l'outil pense un sort. Elles évitent les surprises : pourquoi un node ne touche que la cible de sa branche, pourquoi un projectile ne lit pas la physique Unity, pourquoi un effet visuel peut être désactivé sans changer le combat.

Page Question Graphe, nodes et ports Comment se lit un graphe, quels nodes se branchent où ? Exécution d'un sort Que se passe-t-il entre le lancement et la fin d'un sort ? Cibles et branches Qui un node touche-t-il ? Visée, ancres et directions Où vise le sort, d'où il part, vers où, et comment choisir ses cibles ? Monde de simulation Comment les sorts bougent, touchent et comptent le temps ? Valeurs dynamiques Comment un montant peut dépendre d'une stat, d'une distance, d'une charge ? Présentation Où vivent effets, sons et animations ?

docs.title: Cibles et branches
docs.text: Quand un node lance ses sorties, chaque node suivant reçoit une branche : une copie des cibles, du point visé et de la direction de son parent. C'est la règle qui décide qui une action touche.

docs.title: Une action touche les cibles de sa branche
docs.text:
[Corps de sort] ─► [Au contact] ─► [Dégâts]

À chaque contact, Au contact crée une branche dédiée qui contient la cible touchée. Les Dégâts s'appliquent à elle, et à elle seule. Si le projectile traverse trois ennemis, il y a trois branches et trois applications de dégâts.

docs.title: Branches sœurs : chacune les siennes
docs.text:
[Start] ─► [Diviser ×3] ─► [Corps de sort] ─► [Au contact] ─► [Dégâts]

Diviser crée trois branches, une par projectile, chacune avec sa direction. Le deuxième projectile ne voit pas les cibles du premier. Une branche fille hérite des données de sa mère ; une branche sœur ne voit jamais les données de l'autre.

docs.title: Choisir de nouvelles cibles
docs.text:
Pour toucher autre chose que la cible courante, on ajoute une Sélection de cibles : elle cherche des entités (dans une forme autour du lanceur, du point visé ou de la cible ; les invocations du lanceur ; des sorts) et les filtre (équipe, type, statut, stat, position), puis les trie et en garde un nombre. Sa sortie Cibles porte les entités trouvées, sa sortie Aucune cible part quand rien n'est trouvé.

Exemples :

  • « soigne l'allié le plus blessé » : Sélection (alliés autour du lanceur, tri par PV les plus bas, 1 cible) → Soin ;
  • « la foudre rebondit sur 3 ennemis » : Enchaîner, qui choisit la cible suivante à chaque rebond.

Une Sélection peut aussi se brancher en réglage d'un autre node (Zone d'effet, Enchaîner, Diviser, Invocation) par sa sortie Sélection : elle n'est alors pas exécutée, elle dit à ce node comment choisir ses cibles. Voir Visée, ancres et directions.

docs.title: Voir ce que reçoit un node
docs.text:
L'éditeur déduit du graphe ce que chaque connexion transporte et l'affiche avec le même vocabulaire :

Terme Ce que c'est Cibles reçues les cibles de la branche du node : celles sur qui une action agit Cible de l'événement l'unique cible d'une branche lancée par un écouteur ou un déclencheur (l'entité touchée, le sujet de l'événement) Point visé figé au lancement, remplacé par une Visée Direction de branche écrite par Diviser (éventail, cercle), suivie par les modules et le mouvement Corps du module le module en amont (projectile, zone…) : ce qu'écoutent Au contact, À chaque tick, À l'expiration
  • Étiquette de connexion : au survol d'un lien, un texte court au milieu (« cibles touchées par « Projectile » », « aucune cible (lanceur seulement) », « une cible par branche (« Diviser ») · direction de branche ») ; le bouton Étiquettes de la barre les affiche toujours.
  • Info-bulle de port : au survol d'un port, tout ce qu'il reçoit ou émet (cibles reçues, point visé, direction de branche, corps du module), et ce que le node lit.
  • Badge « ! » sur le titre d'un node qui lit ce qu'il ne recevra jamais : des Dégâts branchés directement sur le Start (aucune cible reçue : il faut un Au contact, une zone ou une Sélection de cibles), un Au contact sans module en amont, une Sélection branchée à la fois en réglage et dans le flux. Un sort lancé par Lancer un sort reçoit les cibles de celui qui le lance : l'avertissement des Dégâts sur le Start peut alors être ignoré.

docs.title: Données de branche
docs.text:
Une branche porte aussi :

  • une direction (écrite par Diviser en éventail ou en cercle, lue par les modules et le Movement) ;
  • un multiplicateur de dégâts (multiplié par Diviser, Enchaîner ou Multiplier les dégâts, appliqué par les nodes de dégâts) ;
  • des marques (par exemple Critique, posées par Marquer la branche), lues par les dégâts et les écouteurs ;
  • la visée (point visé, direction, entité pointée ; voir Visée, ancres et directions), et la valeur de l'événement qui a créé la branche.

docs.title: Le lanceur
docs.text: Certains nodes visent le lanceur plutôt que les cibles reçues : leur champ porteur ou cible propose Lanceur (Appliquer statut sur soi, Dash, Soin de soi). Le lanceur est commun à toute l'exécution.

docs.title: Valeurs dynamiques
docs.text: Beaucoup de champs numériques (dégâts, soin, chance, durées, stacks, forces des réactions…) ne sont pas de simples nombres : ce sont des valeurs dynamiques (ValueSource). Par défaut elles s'affichent comme un champ ordinaire ; un menu permet de changer leur mode.

docs.title: Les modes
docs.text:
Mode La valeur vient de… Exemple Fixe un nombre 20 dégâts Stat une stat du lanceur ou de la cible : valeur courante, maximum ou % du maximum 50 % de l'Attaque du lanceur Stacks de statut le nombre de stacks d'un statut sur la cible ou le lanceur 10 dégâts par stack de Saignement Valeur d'exécution une valeur du lancement : temps d'incantation écoulé, ratio de charge, derniers dégâts infligés, nombre de cibles reçues, blocages du corps du module (rebonds), ou une variable du sort dégâts × ratio de charge Valeur d'événement la valeur portée par l'événement qui a déclenché la branche soigner de 30 % des dégâts reçus Distance une distance dans le plan de la simulation : lanceur → cible, lanceur → point d'impact, ou centre de la zone (point d'impact) → cible (voir Distances) plus de dégâts de près, explosion qui décroît Formule une expression qui combine les sources ci-dessus 0.5 * LastDamage + Stat(Force)

Chaque mode accepte un multiplicateur, un ajout et des bornes optionnelles : valeur × multiplicateur + ajout, ramenée entre le minimum et le maximum.

docs.title: Formules
docs.text:
Élément Syntaxe Opérateurs nombres (point décimal), + - * / % ^, parenthèses Fonctions min(a, b, …), max(a, b, …), clamp(x, min, max) Stat Stat(nom[, Caster\|Target][, Current\|Max\|Percent]) — lanceur et valeur courante par défaut Stacks Stacks(statut[, Target\|Caster]) — cible par défaut Variable du sort Var(nom), ou le nom seul Valeurs de l'exécution Targets, LastDamage, StacksRemoved, RemainingDamage, CastTime, Charge, Kills, Blocks, EventValue, Distance, ImpactDistance, CenterDistance (voir Distances) Aléatoire Random() — tirage de 0 à 100 (exclu), par l'aléatoire de l'exécution (reproductible) Comparateurs < > <= >= = != (== accepté) — 1 si vrai, 0 sinon ; = tolère un écart de 0,0001 Logique not, and, or — une valeur non nulle est vraie

La formule est vérifiée dans l'éditeur : un nom de stat, de statut ou de variable inconnu est signalé, comme une erreur de syntaxe (avec sa position).

Priorité, de la plus forte à la plus faible : ^, signe -, * / %, + -, comparateurs, not, and, or. Ainsi Stat(PV, Target, Percent) < 30 and Distance <= 5 se lit sans parenthèses, et 2 + 3 > 4 vaut 1. Deux comparaisons ne s'enchaînent pas : 1 < x < 3 est une erreur, écrire 1 < x and x < 3. and, or et not sont réservés : une variable de ce nom se lit avec Var(…).

Une comparaison rend 1 ou 0 : elle sert de condition (mode Formule de Vérifier condition) ou de facteur dans un calcul, ex. 20 + 10 * (Targets >= 3).

Formules écrites avant la 1.0

Le vocabulaire français des versions précédentes reste lu : et, ou, non, Lanceur, Cible, Courante, Pourcent, Hasard(), Cibles, DerniersDegats, StacksRetires, DegatsRestants, TempsIncantation, Tues, ValeurEvenement, DistanceImpact. Les sorts existants fonctionnent sans changement.

docs.title: Distances
docs.text:
Une distance se mesure dans le plan de la simulation (l'écart de hauteur ne compte pas), entre deux points :

Distance (champ) Formule Depuis… Jusqu'à… Sans ce point Caster To Target Distance le lanceur la cible 0 sans cible Caster To Impact Point ImpactDistance le lanceur le point d'impact de la branche (là où un corps de module a touché, depuis Au contact) jusqu'à la cible Impact Point To Target CenterDistance le centre de la Zone d'effet de la branche, à sa dernière détection ; hors d'une zone, le point d'impact de la branche la cible depuis le lanceur

ImpactDistance grandit avec la distance parcourue par le projectile : elle ne dit pas où se tient la cible dans l'explosion. Pour des dégâts qui décroissent depuis le centre d'une zone, utiliser CenterDistance. Dans les branches d'une zone (sa sortie Cibles dans la zone et ses écouteurs, Au contact), la distance part du centre de la zone, même quand le point d'impact d'une détection est sur la cible.

Exemple — explosion qui décroît : Corps de sort → Au contact → Zone d'effet (Anchor : Point d'impact, Radius 3, Duration 0) → Dégâts Simple, dégâts en mode Formule : max(20 - CenterDistance * 5, 0). Un ennemi à 0,5 m du centre subit 17,5 dégâts, un ennemi à 2,5 m en subit 7,5, où que se tienne le lanceur.

docs.title: Évaluée pour chaque cible
docs.text: Quand la source dépend de la cible (une stat de la cible, ses stacks, sa distance), la valeur est calculée cible par cible : une même zone inflige à chacun des dégâts différents.

docs.title: Variables du sort
docs.text:
Les variables se déclarent dans les paramètres du sort : un nom et une valeur initiale, remise à chaque lancement. Le node Stocker une valeur les écrit depuis n'importe quelle source ; le mode Valeur d'exécution les relit. Elles sont communes à toute l'exécution.

Exemple — « chaque ennemi touché augmente les dégâts de l'explosion finale » : Au contact → Stocker une valeur (Compteur + 1) ; puis À l'expiration → Dégâts (Valeur d'exécution : Compteur × 15).

docs.title: Exécution d'un sort
docs.text: Chaque lancement crée une exécution (SkillExecution) : une instance isolée du sort. Deux lancers de la même boule de feu sont deux exécutions indépendantes, avec leurs propres cibles et leurs propres données.

docs.title: Du lancement à la fin
docs.text:
1. Vérification : actions du lanceur non bloquées, temps de recharge écoulé, coût disponible. Sinon, le lancement est refusé et rien ne démarre.
  2. Lancement : le coût est prélevé, le temps de recharge démarre.
  3. Incantation (si le sort en a une) : la branche Pendant l'incantation du Start démarre. Un coup reçu ou un étourdissement peut l'interrompre selon le réglage du sort ; le coût est alors rendu et la recharge remise à zéro.
  4. Départ : la sortie principale du Start part.
  5. Déroulement : chaque node fait son travail, puis lance les nodes qui le suivent.
  6. Fin : l'exécution se termine quand plus aucun node n'est actif. Les écouteurs (Sur événement, À chaque tick) et les modules en vol la maintiennent en vie.

docs.title: Nodes instantanés et persistants
docs.text:
• Un node instantané (Dégâts, Appliquer statut, Jouer son…) agit et passe aussitôt la main à ses sorties.
  • Un node persistant dure : un projectile vole, un Délai attend, un Répéter recommence, un écouteur attend son événement. Il lance ses sorties quand c'est le moment (à l'impact, à la fin du délai, à chaque événement).
  • Un node qui échoue (condition fausse, chance ratée, aucune cible) se termine sans lancer ses sorties : la suite de cette branche n'a pas lieu.

docs.title: Données partagées
docs.text:
• Les variables du sort (déclarées dans les paramètres) sont communes à toute l'exécution. Stocker une valeur les écrit, les valeurs dynamiques les lisent.
  • Les cibles, le point visé et la direction sont propres à chaque branche (voir Cibles et branches).

docs.title: Annulation
docs.text:
Une exécution s'arrête avant sa fin quand :

  • le lanceur meurt ou est désactivé (sauf si le sort est réglé pour lui survivre : un projectile déjà parti, une brûlure déjà posée) ;
  • le jeu l'interrompt (CancelSkill, CancelSlot) ;
  • un sort maintenu est relâché, ou une visée est annulée.

Les effets déjà appliqués restent (dégâts, statuts posés) ; les modules en vol et les écouteurs disparaissent.

docs.title: Graphe, nodes et ports
docs.text: Un sort est un asset SkillGraphModel : une liste de nodes et de connexions, plus les paramètres du sort (temps de recharge, coût, incantation…).

docs.title: Le node Start
docs.text:
Tout sort a un node Start, appelé au lancement. Ses sorties :

  • Module : vers le premier module (projectile, zone, attaque…) ;
  • Trigger : vers des actions immédiates (soin du lanceur, statut sur soi…) ;
  • Pendant l'incantation (sort avec temps d'incantation) : une branche qui démarre au début de l'incantation et s'arrête à sa fin (visuel de charge, ralentissement du lanceur).

docs.title: Les familles de nodes
docs.text:
Famille Rôle Exemples Module Un objet du sort qui existe dans le monde, avec un corps qui se déplace et touche Corps de sort (projectile), Zone d'effet, Rayon, Attaque (mêlée), Invocation Behavior Modifie un module : comment il bouge, comment il grandit Mouvement, Grossissement Condition Écoute un module ou filtre les cibles Au contact, À l'expiration, À chaque tick, Type d'entité, Chance, Condition de Stat Support Façonne le déroulement : attendre, répéter, diviser, choisir des cibles Délai, Répéter, Diviser, Enchaîner, Sélection de cibles, Visée, Vérifier condition, Choix aléatoire Action Fait quelque chose aux cibles ou au jeu Dégâts, Soin, Appliquer statut, Réactions, Dash, Tuer, Lancer un sort, Remplacer emplacement Trigger Écoute le jeu pendant la durée du sort Sur événement, Timer, Stat Listener Présentation Effets, sons, animations, tremblements — sans effet sur le combat Jouer effet, Jouer son, Jouer animation, Tremblement caméra

La liste complète, avec les champs de chaque node, est dans la référence des nodes.

docs.title: Les ports
docs.text:
Chaque connexion relie une sortie à une entrée du même type. La couleur du port indique son type :

Type Couleur Ce qui passe Exemple Module Bleu Le flux principal entre modules Start → Corps de sort Trigger Vert Le déclenchement d'une action, avec ses cibles Au contact → Dégâts Condition Orange L'écoute d'un module, ou un filtre Corps de sort → Au contact Support Violet Un modificateur de comportement Mouvement → Corps de sort Sélection Cyan Un réglage, pas du flux : comment un node choisit ses cibles Sélection de cibles → Zone d'effet (voir Visée, ancres et directions)

Quelques nodes ont plusieurs sorties du même type, nommées :

  • Vérifier condition : Vrai / Faux ;
  • Sélection de cibles : Cibles / Aucune cible, et Sélection (réglage d'un autre node) ;
  • Choix aléatoire : Sortie 1, Sortie 2… ;
  • Zone d'effet, Attaque, Rayon : Cibles dans la zone ou Cibles touchées (actions sur les cibles) / Écouteurs (nodes qui écoutent le module, comme À chaque tick) ;
  • Invocation : Invocation / Écouteurs ;
  • Start : lancement / Pendant l'incantation.

docs.title: Lire un graphe
docs.text:
Un graphe se lit depuis le Start, en suivant les flèches. Une sortie peut partir vers plusieurs nodes : ils s'exécutent tous, chacun avec sa propre copie des cibles (voir Cibles et branches).

[Start] ─► [Corps de sort] ─► [Au contact] ─┬─► [Dégâts]
                ▲                           └─► [Appliquer statut]
            [Mouvement]

docs.title: Dans l'éditeur
docs.text:
• Espace ou clic droit → Create Node : ajouter un node (recherche par nom).
  • Glisser d'un port à un autre : connecter ; seuls les ports compatibles s'accrochent.
  • Les champs principaux s'affichent sur le node ; les réglages secondaires sont repliés dans Options. Certains champs n'apparaissent que si un autre les rend utiles (la portée maximale n'apparaît qu'en mode « portée » du Mouvement).
  • Survoler un lien ou un port montre ce qui y circule ; Étiquettes l'affiche sur tous les liens, et un badge « ! » signale un node qui lit ce qu'il ne recevra jamais (voir Cibles et branches).
  • Save enregistre l'asset. Paramètres du sort affiche les réglages du sort dans l'inspecteur. Aperçu ouvre la lecture du sort.

docs.title: Présentation
docs.text:
La présentation, c'est ce qu'on voit et entend : effets de particules, sons, animations du personnage, tremblements de caméra, visuels des projectiles. Dans UnleashSkill, elle est séparée du gameplay :

  • les nodes émettent des intentions (« joue tel effet ici ») ;
  • des assets réutilisables décrivent le contenu (quel prefab, quel son, quel volume) ;
  • un système de présentation les fait apparaître, les met en pool et les arrête.

Conséquences : un même effet d'impact sert à cent sorts ; régler un son ne touche aucun sort ; la présentation peut être désactivée (serveur, tests) sans changer le combat.

docs.title: La bibliothèque
docs.text:
